html:
Why the Gold Rate Changes Twice a Day in India

If you check the gold rate at 10 AM and again at 6 PM, you will often see two different numbers - even though 'today's rate' sounds like it should be one figure. This is not an error. The IBJA (India Bullion and Jewellers Association) publishes the gold rate twice every working day, and understanding why helps you make smarter decisions about when to sell.

At a Glance

IBJA AM rate published~11:30 AM on working days
IBJA PM rate published~5:00 PM on working days
Why two rates?Morning and evening London gold fixings are separate - IBJA follows both
Which rate do buyers use?The most recently published rate at the time of your transaction
Do rates change often between AM and PM?Yes - can differ by ₹50–₹300/10g depending on global market movement
Weekend rate?Last published rate (PM on previous working day) applies
Last UpdatedMay 2026

The IBJA Rate Publication Schedule

The IBJA publishes two gold rates on every MCX (Multi Commodity Exchange) working day:

• AM rate: published around 11:30 AM IST
• PM rate: published around 5:00 PM IST

These correspond roughly to the two London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) gold price fixings that occur daily - the AM fixing at ~1:30 PM IST and the PM fixing at ~7:30 PM IST.

The IBJA takes the international gold price, converts it to INR using the live USD/INR exchange rate, adds import duty (15%), AGIF cess (3%), and other levies - then publishes the resulting domestic benchmark rate.

Why the AM and PM Rates Differ

Between 11:30 AM and 5:00 PM, the international gold market continues to trade. Global events - US economic data releases, Federal Reserve commentary, geopolitical news, oil price movements - can move the gold price by $10–$30/oz between fixings.

Converted to INR at current rates:
• $10/oz change ≈ ₹1.08/g ≈ ₹10.8 per 10g
• $30/oz change ≈ ₹3.25/g ≈ ₹32.5 per 10g

For a seller with 100g of 22K gold:
• A ₹30/g difference between AM and PM = ₹3,000 on the total payout

This is why knowing which rate applies to your transaction matters.

Which Rate Applies When You Sell?

Time of Your VisitRate That Applies
Before 11:30 AMPrevious day's PM rate (or last published rate)
11:30 AM to ~5:00 PMThat day's AM rate (most recently published)
After 5:00 PM (if buyer still open)That day's PM rate
Weekend or holidayLast working day's PM rate

Does It Matter Which Rate You Get?

For most sellers, the AM vs PM difference is small and unpredictable. You cannot know whether the PM rate will be higher or lower than the AM rate - the gold market moves in both directions.

The better strategy: if today's rate (either fixing) is at a level you are happy with, sell. Waiting for the PM rate hoping it will be higher is a 50/50 bet.

To check the current published IBJA rate before visiting: go to ibja.co and look at the most recent rate and its published time.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why does the gold rate update twice a day?

The IBJA follows two international gold price fixings (London AM and PM) and publishes domestic INR rates twice on each working day - at ~11:30 AM and ~5:00 PM IST.

Which gold rate applies when I sell - AM or PM?

The most recently published IBJA rate at the time you complete the transaction. Before 5 PM, the AM rate applies; after 5 PM, the PM rate.

Does the gold rate change significantly between morning and evening?

It can - differences of ₹50–₹300 per 10 grams are common depending on global market activity that day.

Should I sell in the morning or evening to get a better rate?

There is no reliable pattern. The PM rate can be higher or lower than the AM rate. Sell when the published rate is at a level you are comfortable with.

What rate applies on weekends?

The last published PM rate from the preceding working day.

Where can I check the current IBJA rate?

ibja.co - the official IBJA website, which shows the date and time of each published rate.

html:
Gold Melting Charges in India: What They Are & Who Actually Charges Them

'Melting charges' is a term some gold buyers use to justify deducting an additional amount from the gold sale price - above the standard buyer margin. For many sellers, especially those unfamiliar with the process, this sounds legitimate.

Here is the truth: reputable gold buyers do not charge separate melting fees to sellers. Here is why, and what to do if you encounter this practice.

At a Glance

Should a buyer charge you melting fees?No - reputable buyers do not charge sellers for melting
Who absorbs refining/melting cost?The buyer - covered within their 1–3% margin
Is a melting charge deduction legitimate?Only if disclosed upfront and agreed - otherwise it is an inflated deduction
What to do if charged?Ask for it in writing - then compare with another buyer
Last UpdatedMay 2026

What Is a Gold Melting Charge?

When jewellery is sold to a gold buyer, it eventually goes to a refinery where it is melted, assayed, and purified. The refinery charges the buyer for this process.

A 'melting charge' is when some buyers attempt to pass this refining cost on to you - the seller - by deducting it from your payout on top of their normal margin.

Typical melting charge claims: ₹50–₹200 per gram, or a flat ₹500–₹2,000 per transaction.

Why Reputable Buyers Do Not Charge Melting Fees

The buyer's 1–3% margin below the IBJA rate already covers:
• Refining and melting costs at their partner refinery
• Branch operating costs
• Testing equipment and consumables
• The buyer's profit margin

A buyer who charges both a margin below IBJA AND a separate melting fee is double-dipping - taking more than their declared margin. At today's rate of ₹13,965/g for 22K, a ₹100/g 'melting charge' on top of a 2% margin effectively makes their total deduction 2.7% - which should be disclosed upfront, not hidden as a separate fee.

When Melting Charges Are Legitimate

  • At refineries when you take gold directly for refining (bypassing a buyer) - refineries charge a refining fee of ₹30–₹100/g
  • When you send gold to be smelted and assayed and want the proceeds directly - refineries are different from gold buyers
  • For very unusual alloys (foreign gold, dental gold, industrial alloys) where assay is complex - a nominal extra charge may be disclosed and agreed upfront
  • Always ensure any such charge is disclosed before, not deducted after, the transaction is agreed

How to Respond If You Are Charged a Melting Fee

  • Ask: 'Why is there a separate melting charge on top of your rate?' - a transparent buyer can explain
  • Ask for it in writing on the receipt - if they refuse, that is a red flag
  • Compare: visit another buyer and see if they charge the same
  • Do the maths: include the melting charge in your effective per-gram cost and compare to the IBJA rate
  • You can walk away from a transaction before signing the receipt if the terms are not what you agreed

Frequently Asked Questions

Do gold buyers charge melting fees in India?

What is a fair gold melting charge?

For a standard seller: zero. Refining cost is covered by the buyer's margin. A separate melting fee on top of a margin deduction is not standard practice at certified gold buyers.

Can I refuse to pay a melting charge?

Yes - you can decline the transaction before signing if a melting charge is added without prior disclosure.

Are melting charges deducted from the weight or the rate?

Some buyers deduct melting loss from the weight (e.g. '3% melting loss from gross weight') - this is a different form of the same practice. Ask for a clear breakdown.

Is a stone removal charge the same as a melting charge?

No. Stone removal is a legitimate deduction of the stone's weight from the gold weight (the stone itself is returned or set aside). Melting charges are an additional fee on top of this.

What is the refinery charge if I sell directly to a refinery?

Refineries typically charge ₹30–₹100/g for assaying and refining. This is different from the melting charges some local buyers attempt to impose on retail sellers.

html:
Selling Gold for Your Business: Process, Tax & What to Consider

Using personal gold to fund business expenses or working capital is a centuries-old practice in India. Whether it is a cash flow emergency, a new machinery purchase, or seed capital for a startup, gold remains one of the fastest ways to raise funds outside of bank financing.

This guide covers the tax angle, compliance, and practical process.

At a Glance

Gold sale → business use?Yes - sell gold, proceeds go to personal account, then transfer to business
Capital gains on gold sale?Yes - 12.5% LTCG if held 24+ months
Can you deduct gold sale in business books?No - gold sale is a personal capital transaction
GST on gold sale by individual?No - individuals selling personal gold do not charge GST
Section 269ST cash limit₹2,00,000 - large sales must be by bank transfer
Time to get fundsSame day - sell at branch, bank transfer within hours
Last UpdatedMay 2026

The Process: Gold to Business Capital

  1. Payment by bank transfer to your personal account (mandatory if sale > ₹2,00,000)
  2. Transfer funds from your personal account to your business current account
  3. Book the transfer appropriately in your business accounts (loan from proprietor/director, or capital injection depending on business structure)
  4. Keep both the gold sale receipt and the transfer record for audit trail

Tax Implications

  • Capital gains tax on the gold sale: personal tax - 12.5% LTCG (gold held 24+ months) on the profit
  • The gold sale and the subsequent business use are two separate transactions for tax purposes
  • The capital gain is reported in your personal ITR under Schedule CG
  • The business injection is recorded as a loan or capital contribution in business books - no additional tax

Gold Loan vs Selling: The Business Owner's Choice

FactorGold LoanSelling Gold
Cash received75–85% of gold value~98% of gold value
Gold reclaimed?Yes - if repaidNo - permanently sold
Interest cost12–28% p.a.Nil
Speed1–3 days (bank/NBFC processing)Same day at branch
Best forShort-term cash need with repayment planPermanent capital need

Proprietors vs Pvt Ltd Directors

  • Proprietorship: gold sale proceeds can be directly brought in as capital - straightforward
  • Partnership firm: each partner can inject personal gold sale proceeds as capital
  • Pvt Ltd director: proceeds are injected as a loan to the company (director loan) - recorded in books
  • In all cases: the gold sale is a personal transaction; the company or firm receives the money as a transfer

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell personal gold to fund my business?

Is the capital gains tax on gold sale a business expense?

No - it is a personal tax on the gold sale. It is not a business deduction.

Do I charge GST when selling personal gold?

No - individuals selling personal jewellery do not levy GST.

Is a gold loan better than selling gold for business capital?

If you can repay within 3–6 months, a gold loan lets you reclaim the gold. If you need permanent capital, selling gives more money upfront without interest burden.

How fast can I get money from selling gold for my business?

Same day - sell at branch in 30 minutes, bank transfer within a few hours.

Can I deduct the cost of selling gold in my business accounts?

The gold sale is a personal transaction. You cannot deduct the gold's cost in your business books. The proceeds are an injection of personal capital.

What is the Section 269ST limit for gold sales?

You cannot receive more than ₹2,00,000 in cash for a single gold sale. Large amounts must be via bank transfer.

html:
Gold vs Real Estate in India: Which Gives Better Returns?

The two most beloved asset classes for Indian families have long been gold and real estate. Both are tangible, both hold cultural significance, and both have delivered strong returns historically. But which is actually better as an investment - and why does the answer depend on factors most comparisons ignore?

Quick Comparison

Gold 10-year CAGR (INR)~12–14%
Real estate 10-year CAGR (India)~5–8% (varies hugely by city and micro-market)
Gold LTCG tax12.5% after 24 months
Real estate LTCG tax12.5% after 24 months (after indexation removal)
Gold liquidity30 minutes - sell at any branch
Real estate liquidityLow - weeks to months to sell
Entry investment (gold)Any amount - from 1g onwards
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Side-by-Side Comparison

FeatureGoldReal Estate
10-year CAGR (approx)12–14%5–8% (major cities, varies widely)
LiquidityVery high - 30 minutesLow - weeks to months
Entry amountAny amount (from ₹1,500 for 0.1g)₹20L+ (most urban markets)
Transaction cost1–3% buyer margin5–10% (registration, stamp duty, broker)
Annual holding costStorage (optional)Property tax, maintenance, HOA
Rental income?NoYes - but yields are 1.5–3% in most Indian cities
LTCG tax12.5% after 24 months12.5% after 24 months
DivisibilityYes - sell any portionNo - cannot sell 30% of a flat

Why Real Estate Returns Are Often Overstated

When people quote real estate returns, they often exclude:
• Stamp duty and registration (5–8%)
• Broker fees (1–2% on buy AND sell)
• Annual property tax, maintenance, HOA
• Renovation costs before selling
• Vacancy periods if rented
• Time and legal cost of transactions

After accounting for all these, real estate total returns in most Indian cities have been 5–8% CAGR over the last 10 years - well below gold's 12–14% CAGR in the same period.

When Real Estate Wins

  • In hyper-growing micro-markets (specific corridors in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune) - property appreciation can be 15–20% CAGR
  • For rental income - gold generates no cash flow; well-located real estate gives 2–3% annual yield (though low compared to mortgage cost)
  • For leverage - banks lend 70–80% for property; you cannot leverage gold as easily
  • For the sense of ownership and utility - real estate can be lived in or used directly

When Gold Wins

  • Liquidity - gold can be sold in 30 minutes; real estate can take months to complete a transaction
  • Divisibility - you can sell 10g of gold; you cannot sell 10% of a flat
  • Low transaction cost - 1–3% vs 7–12% for real estate
  • No maintenance cost - gold does not need annual repair, tax or HOA payment
  • Return consistency - gold returns in India have been more consistent across regions than real estate
  • Currency hedge - gold is globally priced; real estate return depends heavily on local demand

The Bottom Line

Across most of India over the last 10 years, gold has outperformed real estate on a total return basis after transaction costs. However, specific high-growth real estate micro-markets have significantly outperformed gold. The key difference is liquidity - gold can be sold in 30 minutes, real estate cannot. For investors who already own real estate, gold provides diversification and liquidity that property cannot.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is gold better than real estate in India?

Over the last 10 years, gold has generally outperformed real estate on a total-return basis after costs. However, specific high-growth real estate corridors have beaten gold.

What is the CAGR of real estate in India?

Approximately 5–8% CAGR for most major Indian cities over 10 years. Premium micro-markets can be 12–18% CAGR.

Is gold more liquid than real estate?

Yes - gold can be sold in 30 minutes at a gold buyer. Real estate typically takes weeks to months for a transaction to complete.

Are real estate and gold taxed the same?

Both attract 12.5% LTCG after 24 months. Real estate previously had indexation benefit; this was removed in the 2024 Budget.

Should I sell property and buy gold or vice versa?

Consult a financial advisor for personal advice. The decision depends on your specific need, the property's performance, and gold's current price.

Is gold or real estate better for long-term investment?

For most Indian investors, a mix of both provides the best outcome - gold for liquidity and hedging, real estate for larger capital allocation and potential rental income.

Can I use gold as collateral like real estate?

Gold can be used as collateral for gold loans (typically 75–85% LTV). Real estate can also be mortgaged. Gold collateral is faster to process.

html:
Gold vs Mutual Funds: Which Has Given Better Returns in India?

Gold or mutual funds - which is the smarter choice for Indian investors? Both have their advocates and both have delivered strong returns over certain periods. The answer depends on what you are trying to achieve.

This guide gives you the honest 10-year comparison without sales bias.

Quick Comparison

Gold 10-year CAGR (INR)~12–14% (2016–2026)
Nifty 50 10-year CAGR~13–15% (2016–2026)
Nifty midcap 10-year CAGR~17–20% (2016–2026)
Gold LTCG tax12.5% after 24 months
Equity MF LTCG tax12.5% on gains above ₹1.25L after 12 months
Gold volatilityLower than equity MFs
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Side-by-Side Comparison

FeaturePhysical GoldEquity Mutual Fund
10-year CAGR (approx)12–14%13–20% (index to midcap range)
Short-term riskModerateHigh (equity can fall 30–50% in a correction)
LTCG tax rate12.5% after 24 months12.5% after 12 months (above ₹1.25L)
STCG taxSlab rate (under 24 months)20% (under 12 months)
Liquidity30 minutes (sell at branch)T+2 days redemption (AMC)
Inflation hedgeStrongModerate (equity beats inflation long-term but volatile)
Currency hedgeYes - gold is globally priced in USDNo - INR-denominated
Best forPortfolio protection, inflation hedgeLong-term wealth growth

10-Year Return Reality Check

Physical gold (INR, 22K IBJA rate):
• 2016: ~₹2,800/g
• 2026: ~₹13,965/g
• Approximate CAGR: 14%

Nifty 50 Index Fund (total returns including dividends):
• 10-year approximate CAGR: 13–15%

Midcap Mutual Funds:
• 10-year approximate CAGR: 17–20% (with significantly higher volatility)

Conclusion: Gold and large-cap equity have delivered broadly similar returns over 10 years in India. Midcap/small-cap funds have outperformed gold in the same period, but with much higher volatility.

Tax Comparison

Gold LTCG (after 24 months): 12.5% on the entire gain
Equity MF LTCG (after 12 months): 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh (first ₹1.25L exempt per year)

For moderate gains, equity MFs have a tax advantage due to the ₹1.25L annual exemption. For large gains, both are taxed at the same 12.5% LTCG rate.

When Gold Is the Better Choice

  • During global uncertainty (pandemic, geopolitical crisis) - gold rises, equities fall
  • As a currency hedge - gold protects against rupee depreciation
  • For conservative investors who cannot stomach equity volatility
  • For diversification - gold has low correlation with equities
  • If you already have significant equity exposure and want balance

When Equity Mutual Funds May Be Better

  • For long-term wealth building (10+ years) - equity has historically outperformed gold
  • For younger investors with high risk tolerance
  • When equity markets are at depressed valuations
  • For systematic investment (SIP) - rupee cost averaging works better with volatile assets
  • For the ₹1.25L annual LTCG exemption benefit

The Bottom Line

Neither gold nor mutual funds is universally 'better' - they serve different roles. Gold is a hedge and store of value; equity MFs are growth engines with higher risk. Most advisors recommend 10–15% in gold as a portfolio hedge, with the majority in equity for long-term growth. If you are selling existing gold, consider the proceeds: reinvesting in diversified equity MFs is a common strategy for long-term investors.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is gold better than mutual funds?

Over the last 10 years, both have given similar returns (12–15% CAGR). Midcap MFs have outperformed gold, but with higher risk. Gold is less volatile and provides portfolio diversification.

What is better for SIP - gold or mutual fund?

Systematic investment works well for both. Gold SIPs (through digital gold or Gold ETFs) and equity MF SIPs are both valid strategies.

How is gold taxed vs mutual funds?

Gold: 12.5% LTCG after 24 months. Equity MFs: 12.5% LTCG after 12 months (with ₹1.25L annual exemption). For large gains, both are similar.

Should I sell gold and invest in mutual funds?

If you have no immediate need for the gold money and are a long-term investor, reinvesting in diversified equity MFs is a common strategy. Consult a financial advisor for personalised advice.

Is gold a safer investment than mutual funds?

Gold is generally less volatile than equity mutual funds. During market crashes, gold often rises while equities fall - providing portfolio protection.

Do gold prices correlate with the stock market?

Typically low or negative correlation - gold often rises when equity markets fall (investors shift to safe havens). This makes gold valuable for diversification.

What percentage of my portfolio should be in gold?

Financial advisors commonly recommend 10–15% in gold as a portfolio hedge. This varies based on individual risk appetite and goals.

html:
Gold vs Fixed Deposit: Which Is a Better Investment for Indians?

The classic debate among Indian investors: should you keep gold or put money in a fixed deposit? Both have merit - but they serve different purposes, carry different risks, and are taxed differently.

This comparison gives you the honest numbers without pushing you either way.

Quick Comparison

Gold 10-year return (approx)12–14% CAGR in INR (2016–2026)
Bank FD interest rate (2026)6.5–8% per annum
Gold tax on LTCG12.5% on gains after 24 months
FD interest taxAdded to income - taxed at slab rate (20–30%)
Gold liquidityHigh - sell at any buyer in 30 minutes
FD liquidityHigh - premature withdrawal usually allowed (with penalty)
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Side-by-Side Comparison

FeatureGoldFixed Deposit (Bank)
Typical annual return12–14% CAGR (10-year)6.5–8% p.a. (fixed)
Return guaranteed?No - market-dependentYes - fixed at entry
Tax on gains12.5% LTCG (after 24 months)Added to income (20–30% slab)
LiquidityHigh - sell in 30 minutesHigh - withdraw with penalty if early
RiskPrice volatility - can fallVery low - deposit is insured (up to ₹5L)
Physical holding riskTheft, storage costNone - held by bank
Best forInflation hedge, long-term wealthCapital protection, regular interest income

10-Year Return Comparison

Gold (22K IBJA rate, INR):
• 2016: approximately ₹2,800/g
• 2026: approximately ₹13,965/g
• Gain: approximately 5x in 10 years = approximately 14% CAGR

Bank FD (average 7% p.a., compounded annually):
• ₹1,00,000 in 2016 grows to: ₹1,00,000 × (1.07)^10 = approximately ₹1,96,715
• FD gives approximately 2x in 10 years = 7% CAGR

On a pure return basis, gold significantly outperformed FDs over the last decade. However, past performance does not guarantee future results - and gold is more volatile.

Tax Comparison

Gold (LTCG after 24 months): 12.5% on the capital gain
Example: Buy ₹1,00,000 of gold, sell for ₹1,80,000
Gain = ₹80,000 | Tax = ₹80,000 × 12.5% = ₹10,000

FD interest: Added to income and taxed at slab rate
Example: ₹1,00,000 FD at 7% = ₹7,000 interest per year
If slab rate is 30%: Tax = ₹7,000 × 30% = ₹2,100 per year

For high earners (30% slab), gold's 12.5% LTCG is significantly more tax-efficient than FD income tax.

When FD Is Better

  • You need predictable income - FD gives a guaranteed, fixed return
  • Your time horizon is under 2 years - short-term gold can be volatile
  • You are risk-averse - FD principal is protected (up to ₹5L DICGC insurance)
  • You want to avoid the complexity of physical gold storage
  • Your income is in a low tax slab (0% or 5%) - FD tax impact is minimal

When Gold Is Better

  • Long-term (5+ years) - gold has historically outperformed FDs over long periods in India
  • Inflation hedge - gold tends to rise with inflation; FD real returns erode during high inflation
  • Currency hedging - gold is priced globally and protects against rupee depreciation
  • High tax slab (30%) - LTCG at 12.5% is much more efficient than FD income at 30%
  • Emergency liquidity without bank paperwork - sell gold in 30 minutes

The Bottom Line

Gold and FDs are not direct competitors - they serve different roles in a portfolio. Gold is an inflation hedge and long-term wealth store; FDs provide guaranteed income and capital safety. Most financial advisors suggest holding both, with gold as 10–15% of a portfolio. If you are selling existing gold, the decision should be based on your need - not just the theoretical comparison.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is gold better than FD for investment?

Over the last 10 years in India, gold has significantly outperformed FDs in nominal returns. However, gold is volatile and FDs are guaranteed. The right choice depends on your time horizon and risk tolerance.

What is the tax on gold vs FD returns?

Gold LTCG (after 24 months): 12.5%. FD interest: added to income at your slab rate (20–30%). Gold is more tax-efficient for higher-income earners.

Is gold liquid like an FD?

Gold can be sold at a branch in 30 minutes. FDs can be prematurely withdrawn with a penalty (usually 0.5–1% less than the contracted rate).

Should I sell gold and put it in FD?

If you need guaranteed income and do not need an inflation hedge, yes. If you are planning to hold long-term (5+ years), gold may give better returns.

Is gold safer than FD?

FDs are safer in the short term - principal is guaranteed and insured up to ₹5L. Gold can fall 15–20% in a year. Long-term, both are considered reasonably safe.

Does gold beat inflation better than FD?

Historically yes - gold in INR has beaten inflation over 10-year periods. FD real returns (after inflation) are often 1–3% p.a.

What is the CAGR of gold in India over 10 years?

Approximately 12–14% CAGR in INR from 2016–2026. Past returns do not guarantee future performance.

html:
Is Now the Right Time to Sell Gold? A Framework for Deciding

'Should I sell now or wait?' is the single most common question from gold sellers. There is no universal answer - but there is a clear framework for making the decision. This guide gives you the five factors to weigh and helps you cut through the noise of daily gold price headlines.

Today's 22K rate: ₹13,965/g. Whether that is a good time to sell depends on your situation - not just the rate.

At a Glance

Current 22K rate₹13,965/g
Key questionDo you need the money now, or can you wait?
Gold as timing investmentUnreliable - price direction is unpredictable
Best time signalWhen gold is at/near a multi-year high AND you have a use for the money
Worst mistakeWaiting indefinitely for a "better" price while needs go unmet
Tax consideration24-month rule - sell after 24 months for LTCG (12.5%) not income slab rate
Last UpdatedMay 2026

The 5 Factors That Actually Matter

  1. Your immediate need: Do you have a specific financial need - debt repayment, education, medical? If yes, sell now at ₹13,965/g. Waiting for a marginally better rate risks your financial situation.
  2. The holding period: Have you held the gold for 24+ months? If yes, your capital gain is taxed at 12.5% LTCG instead of your income slab rate (20–30%). If you are close to 24 months, waiting a few weeks can save significant tax.
  3. Current rate vs your purchase price: If gold is significantly above your purchase price, you have already made a gain. If below, you are selling at a loss - consider whether waiting makes sense given the need.
  4. Your risk tolerance: Gold prices are unpredictable. They can rise further - or fall. Every month you wait is a bet on the direction. If you cannot afford to be wrong, sell now.
  5. The opportunity cost: If you sell now and invest the proceeds in a FD at 7% for 12 months, what would the gold price need to be in 12 months for the 'wait' to have been better? Calculate it.

When the Rate Is Historically High - Does It Matter?

Gold is near multi-year highs in 2026. Does this make it a 'good' time to sell? It depends:

• If you were planning to sell anyway → yes, a historically high rate is ideal
• If you are selling purely to capture the high → be cautious. Gold has surprised everyone before - it can go higher, or correct
• Historical highs often correct by 10–20% before rising again; they also sometimes continue rising for years

The only reliable rule: sell when you need to sell, and at a price that makes sense for your situation - not because a headline says 'gold hits all-time high'.

Timing Mistakes to Avoid

  • Waiting for 'one more month' indefinitely - the 'right moment' never comes
  • Selling on impulse because gold had a big day - daily moves are noise
  • Not selling when you have an urgent need because of a speculative hope for higher prices
  • Selling before 24 months when waiting a few weeks would switch you from STCG to LTCG tax
  • Comparing today's price to the all-time high and feeling you missed the peak - the peak is only visible in hindsight

A Simple Decision Framework

Your SituationRecommended Action
You need money urgentlySell now - financial need trumps price timing
You are within 2–3 months of the 24-month markWait - LTCG vs STCG tax saving is real money
Gold is significantly above your purchase price and you have a use for the moneySell - you have made a good return; locking it in is sensible
You have no specific plan for the moneyHold - no rush to sell without a purpose
Gold is below your purchase priceConsider holding unless you need the money; selling at a loss locks in the loss

Frequently Asked Questions

Is now a good time to sell gold?

At ₹13,965/g for 22K, gold is at strong levels. Whether it is the 'right' time depends on your financial need, holding period (24-month tax rule), and whether you have a purpose for the proceeds.

Should I wait for the gold price to go higher?

Only if you have no immediate need and can afford to wait without certainty. Prices can go up or down - waiting is a speculative bet.

What is the 24-month rule for selling gold?

If you sell gold held for 24+ months, capital gains are taxed at 12.5% (LTCG). Under 24 months, gains are added to income at your slab rate (20–30%). Waiting to cross the 24-month mark can save significant tax.

Is it better to sell gold now or invest it?

If you have a better-yielding investment in mind and gold is at a high, selling and reinvesting may be logical. Compare expected returns carefully.

How do I know if gold is at a historically high price?

Check gold price charts on financial news sites or ibja.co historical data. If the current rate is near the highest it has been in the last 5 years, it is elevated.

Does the season affect when to sell gold?

Dhanteras and Akshaya Tritiya see high gold demand - prices may be slightly elevated. However, the IBJA rate is market-driven and seasonal effects are usually small.

html:
The Difference Between 999 and 24K Gold: Are They the Same?

You see a gold coin stamped '999' and another coin stamped '24K'. Are they the same? Almost - but there is a small but important distinction between 24K (the karat system) and 999 (the millesimal fineness system) worth understanding before you buy or sell.

At a Glance

24K in the karat system24/24 parts gold - theoretically 100% pure
999 in millesimal fineness999 parts per 1,000 = 99.9% pure gold
Are they the same?Essentially yes - 24K is 99.9% pure, marked as 999
Even purer option999.9 (four nines) = 99.99% - used in some investment coins
999 / 24K rate today₹15,250/g
Common 24K productsInvestment coins, biscuits, bars
Last UpdatedMay 2026

The Two Systems: Karat vs Millesimal Fineness

System999 Gold24K Gold999.9 Gold
Purity expressed asParts per 1,000Parts per 24Parts per 10,000
Purity percentage99.9%99.9% (defined)99.99%
Hallmark stamp99924K or 24ct999.9
Same thing?YesYesSlightly purer
Common usesBars, coins, biscuitsCoins, barsPremium bullion (Maple Leaf, Britannia)
Rate today₹15,250/g₹15,250/g₹15,248/g

Why 24K Is Never Truly 100% Pure

In the karat system, 24K is defined as 24 out of 24 parts gold - theoretically 100%. However, in practice, achieving absolute purity is technically impossible. The highest achievable industrial purity is 99.999% (five nines), and most '24K' gold is 99.9% (999) with trace impurities.

The BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) recognises 999 as the highest purity for domestic gold products. The IBJA uses 999 as the rate basis for 24K calculations.

What This Means When You Sell

For practical selling purposes, 999 and 24K are identical:
• Both are valued at the IBJA 24K rate: ₹15,250/g
• XRF testing will confirm any piece claiming to be 999/24K
• The 0.1% difference between 999 (99.9%) and 999.9 (99.99%) is worth only ₹15 per gram - negligible for most sellers

If your coin is stamped 999.9 (four nines) instead of 999, the payout difference is minimal at retail level.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is 999 gold the same as 24K?

Yes - 999 millesimal fineness equals 99.9% purity, which is the standard for 24K gold. They are interchangeable for pricing and selling purposes.

Is 999.9 gold better than 999?

999.9 (four nines) is 99.99% pure - slightly purer than 999 (99.9%). The difference is 0.09% and translates to a negligible price difference per gram at retail.

What hallmark does 24K gold have?

In India, 24K gold is marked 999 under the BIS system. Some imported pieces may say 24K, 24ct, or 999.9.

Why can't gold be 100% pure?

Absolute 100% purity is physically impossible - trace impurities are always present. 99.99% (999.9) is the highest achievable standard commercially.

What is 10g of 24K (999) gold worth today?

₹1,52,500.

Is 24K gold good for jewellery?

24K is too soft for everyday jewellery - it scratches and deforms easily. Jewellery uses 22K (916) or 18K (750). 24K is primarily for investment (coins, bars, biscuits).

Gold Findings Jewellery: Can Jump Rings, Clasps & Chains Be Sold?

Gold findings are the small functional components used in jewellery making - jump rings, clasps, ear wires, pin backs, chain ends, crimp beads and bails. If you have accumulated gold findings from craft projects or jewellery repairs, you may be wondering: are they real gold? Can they be sold?

The answer depends on the finding's material. Here is how to determine what you have and what it is worth.

At a Glance

What are gold findings?Small jewellery components: clasps, jump rings, ear hooks, chain ends
Real gold findings?Yes - if labelled 14K, 18K, or 22K gold filled/solid
Gold-filled findings?Gold layer only (~5% gold) - low resale value
Solid gold findings?Valuable - same rate per gram as jewellery
Minimum weight to sell?No minimum - but very small amounts may not be worth the trip individually
Best approach?Accumulate findings, then sell all at once by total weight
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Types of Gold Findings and Their Real Gold Content

Finding TypeTypical MarkingReal Gold ContentResale Value
Solid gold clasp/jump ring14K, 18K, 22KFull gold alloy throughoutPaid at IBJA rate for karat
Gold-filled clasp14K GF, 1/20 14K~5% of total weight in goldVery low - base metal dominated
Gold plated findingGP, GEP<0.1% gold by weightNil - gold layer negligible
Gold vermeil finding925 GVThin gold over sterling silverSilver scrap value only
Brass / base metal findingNo gold marking0% goldNo gold value

How to Identify Solid Gold Findings

  • Look for a karat stamp: 14K, 18K, or 22K (without 'GF' or 'GP') indicates solid gold
  • Gold-filled findings always have 'GF', '1/20 14K', or similar notation
  • Very small findings may not be stamped - XRF testing at the branch will confirm
  • Solid gold findings feel heavier than base metal or gold-filled ones of the same size
  • Acid test (for large pieces): real gold shows no reaction to 18K acid; base metals react quickly

Selling a Mixed Bag of Gold Findings

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell gold clasps and jump rings in India?

What is the minimum amount of gold I can sell?

No strict minimum, but very small amounts (under 1g) may not be practical to sell separately. Accumulate findings before visiting.

How do I know if my findings are solid gold or gold-filled?

Look for GF in the marking (gold-filled) vs just 14K/18K (solid). XRF testing at the branch gives a definitive answer.

What are gold-filled findings worth?

Very little - the gold layer represents only about 5% of the total weight.

Can I mix findings from different karats?

Yes - they will be XRF tested and the mixed weight will be assessed by average purity, or separated by karat if very different.

Do earring hooks need to be 18K to have gold value?

If stamped 18K (or 22K/14K without GF/GP), yes - they are solid gold and have resale value at the IBJA rate.

What about loose gold chain links?

Same rules - if solid gold (hallmarked 14K-22K without GF/GP), they are valued by weight and purity at the IBJA rate.

html:
Black Gold Jewellery: What It Is & Can You Sell It in India?

Black gold jewellery has become increasingly popular in India, especially for men's rings, cufflinks and contemporary jewellery. The dramatic matte-black appearance looks striking - but many owners wonder: is black gold real gold? And what is it worth when you want to sell?

The answer: it is real gold underneath, and at resale it is valued exactly like yellow or white gold of the same karat.

At a Glance

What is black gold?Real gold with a black surface treatment (oxidation, rhodium or DLC coating)
Gold contentSame as the underlying karat (18K = 75% gold)
Most common karat for black gold18K (750) - sometimes 14K (585)
18K black gold rate today₹11,438/g
Does the black finish add value?No - only gold content is paid at resale
XRF testing on black gold?Yes - works through the surface treatment
Last UpdatedMay 2026

How Black Gold Gets Its Colour

  • Oxidation / patination: chemical treatment with sulphur compounds - darkens the gold surface
  • Black rhodium plating: rhodium electroplated in black finish - same gold core as white gold
  • DLC (Diamond-Like Carbon) coating: ultra-thin carbon film applied for deep matte black - very durable
  • Ruthenium plating: dark grey-black plating similar to rhodium - used in luxury watches and jewellery
  • All methods produce a black finish over real gold - the gold core is unchanged

Resale Value of Black Gold

The black surface treatment has no intrinsic value at resale. At a gold buyer:

• XRF testing penetrates the surface coating and identifies the gold content
• A 10g 18K black gold ring tests at 75% gold - the same as any 18K yellow or white gold ring
• Payout = 10 × 0.750 × ₹15,250 = ₹1,14,375

The black coating is removed during refining and is irrelevant to the resale calculation.

Black Gold vs Regular Gold at Resale

All three receive the same payout - the surface finish is irrelevant.

PieceWeightKaratSurfaceResale Value
Black gold ring10g18KBlack rhodium coating₹1,14,375
Yellow gold ring10g18KNatural yellow₹1,14,375
White gold ring10g18KWhite + rhodium plating₹1,14,375

Frequently Asked Questions

Is black gold real gold?

Yes - black gold is real gold with a black surface treatment. The gold core is the same as any other piece of the same karat.

Is black gold worth more than yellow gold?

Not at resale - you are paid the same rate per gram for the same karat, regardless of the surface colour.

What karat is most black gold jewellery?

Usually 18K (750) or 14K (585). The karat is typically stamped on the piece.

Does the black finish affect XRF testing?

No - XRF technology penetrates the surface coating and identifies the gold content accurately.

What is the resale value of a 10g black gold ring?

If it is 18K: ₹1,14,375. If 14K: ₹89,212. Check the hallmark or XRF test to confirm.

Is black gold a permanent colour?

Depends on the treatment. DLC coating is very durable. Rhodium plating and oxidation can wear over time, especially with regular use.

html:
White Gold vs Silver: Key Differences & Resale Value in India

White gold and silver look similar to the naked eye, especially in older or worn pieces that have lost some of their finish. Knowing which one you have is critical - because the resale value is dramatically different.

At a Glance

White gold purity75% gold (18K, 750 hallmark) - gold based
Silver purity92.5% silver (sterling, 925 hallmark) - silver based
White gold 18K rate today₹11,438/g
Silver rate today~₹95–100/g (varies daily)
10g white gold today vs 10g silver₹1,14,375 vs ~₹950–1,000
Value difference for same weightWhite gold is ~120x more valuable per gram than silver
How to tell apartHallmark (750 vs 925) or XRF test - definitive
Last UpdatedMay 2026

White Gold vs Silver: Side-by-Side Comparison

FeatureWhite Gold (18K)Sterling Silver
Base metalGold (75% gold + alloys)Silver (92.5% silver)
Hallmark750925
Weight for same sizeDenser - heavier per visual sizeLighter per visual size
Rate today₹11,438/g~₹95–100/g
10g value today₹1,14,375~₹950–1,000
Rhodium plated?Often yes - gives bright whiteNot typically plated
Tarnishes?No (gold core does not tarnish)Yes - silver tarnishes over time
Sold at gold buyer?Yes - at gold rateAt silver rate (lower value)

How to Tell White Gold from Silver at Home

  • Hallmark check: look inside the ring band or on the clasp. 750 = white gold (18K). 925 = sterling silver. 999 = fine silver.
  • Weight: white gold is denser than silver. Same-sized ring: white gold is noticeably heavier.
  • Tarnish: if the piece has dark tarnish spots, it is likely silver. White gold does not tarnish.
  • Magnet: neither gold nor silver is magnetic. This test rules out base metals but does not differentiate between gold and silver.
  • XRF test: the definitive method - identifies exactly what percentage is gold vs silver within 60 seconds at the branch.

Why It Matters So Much

The difference is enormous: 10g of white gold (18K) is worth ₹1,14,375. 10g of sterling silver is worth approximately ₹950–1,000. That is a 120-150x difference in value.

If you are unsure, always get XRF tested before selling - assuming a piece is silver when it is actually 18K white gold means leaving thousands of rupees on the table.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I tell white gold from silver?

Is white gold worth more than silver?

Significantly more. 10g of 18K white gold = ₹1,14,375. 10g of sterling silver = ~₹950. White gold is approximately 120x more valuable per gram.

Does white gold tarnish?

The gold core does not tarnish. However, the rhodium plating on the surface may wear over time, exposing the slightly yellowish gold alloy underneath.

What is the hallmark for white gold?

750 for 18K white gold. 916 for 22K (less common in white gold). 585 for 14K.

Why does white gold look silver?

White gold gets its colour from the alloy metals mixed with gold - usually nickel, palladium or manganese. Rhodium plating enhances the white appearance.

Palladium Gold Jewellery: What It Is, Purity & Resale Value in India

Palladium-alloyed gold (often called 'palladium white gold') is a premium white gold alloy that uses palladium instead of nickel to achieve its white colour. It is used in high-end jewellery and is increasingly common in imported European and Japanese pieces.

If you have palladium gold jewellery and want to know its resale value in India, this guide explains what it is and what to expect.

At a Glance

What is palladium white gold?Gold alloyed with palladium for a natural white colour - no rhodium plating needed
Common composition18K: 75% gold + 12–15% palladium + other metals
Hallmark750 (18K) - same as other 18K white gold
Palladium value?Precious metal - but standard gold buyers pay for gold content only
Resale at gold buyer₹11,438/g for the gold content - palladium not separately paid
XRF testShows both gold and palladium content clearly
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Palladium Gold vs Nickel White Gold vs Rhodium-Plated White Gold

TypeCompositionAppearanceResale Value
Palladium white gold75% gold + palladiumNaturally white - no plating neededGold content paid (18K rate)
Nickel white gold75% gold + nickelWhite but may cause skin allergyGold content paid (18K rate)
Rhodium-plated white goldYellow/white gold + rhodium coatingVery white initially, plating wears offGold content paid
Platinum (not gold)95% platinumWhite, very denseDifferent - platinum rate, not gold rate

What Palladium White Gold Is Worth at Resale

At a gold buyer, palladium-alloyed gold is assessed for its gold content - not its palladium content. The XRF machine will show:
• Gold: ~75% (for 18K palladium white gold)
• Palladium: 12–15%
• Other metals: balance

You are paid for the gold content only:
Payout = Weight × 0.750 × ₹15,250/g = ₹11,438/g for 18K

For a 10g palladium white gold ring:
10 × 0.750 × ₹15,250 = ₹1,14,375

Note: Palladium itself is a precious metal. For very large quantities, a specialist precious metals refiner may offer a better total return by valuing both metals.

Is Palladium White Gold BIS Hallmarked in India?

BIS hallmarking covers gold alloys at 14K (585), 18K (750) and 22K (916). Palladium white gold at 18K carries the 750 hallmark - the same as any other 18K gold. The BIS hallmark does not specify whether the alloy uses palladium or nickel.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is palladium gold jewellery?

Gold alloyed with palladium to create a natural white colour. Common in 18K white gold - 75% gold and 12–15% palladium.

Is palladium white gold worth more than regular white gold?

The additional palladium has value, but standard gold buyers pay for gold content only. For large pieces, a specialist refiner may pay for the palladium separately.

How do I know if my white gold has palladium?

XRF testing identifies the exact alloy composition. You cannot tell visually whether a white gold piece uses palladium or nickel.

Is palladium white gold better than nickel white gold?

Palladium white gold is hypoallergenic (no nickel allergy risk) and naturally white. It is considered superior but more expensive.

What is 18K palladium gold worth today?

₹11,438/g based on the gold content. A 10g piece = ₹1,14,375.

Is palladium the same as platinum?

No - palladium (Pd) and platinum (Pt) are different precious metals. Platinum is heavier and more expensive. Do not confuse platinum jewellery with palladium-alloyed gold.

14K Gold Rate Today: Price per Gram & Resale Value in India

14 karat gold (585 hallmark) is less common than 22K in India, but it is widely found in imported jewellery, men's rings, industrial gold and diamond-set pieces. If you have 14K gold, here is today's live rate and everything you need to know before selling.

At a Glance

14K gold purity58.5% pure gold
BIS hallmark stamp585
14K gold rate today₹8,921/g
10g of 14K gold today₹89,212
20g of 14K gold today₹1,78,425
Compared to 22K₹13,965/g - ₹5,044/g more per gram

Last UpdatedMay 2026

14K Gold Rate vs Other Purities Today

KaratHallmarkPurityRate Today10g Value
24K99999.9%₹15,250/g₹1,52,500

Where Is 14K Gold Common in India?

  • Imported jewellery from Europe, the USA and some Middle Eastern countries
  • Men's rings and bands - 14K is popular for its durability (harder than 22K)
  • Diamond-set jewellery - diamond settings often use 14K or 18K for durability
  • Industrial gold uses - some electronic connectors and contacts
  • Dental gold - older dental crowns may be 14K
  • Jewellery purchased abroad and brought to India as gifts or personal items

Selling 14K Gold in India

The process is exactly the same as selling any other karat:
1. XRF test confirms 14K (58.5% gold content)
2. Weighed on precision digital scale

The sovereign is the standard unit for gold pricing across South India - especially in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Kerala. When a Tamil bride's dowry is quoted in sovereigns, or a jeweller prices a chain in pavans, the calculation is always the same: 1 sovereign = 8 grams.

This page gives you today's live sovereign gold rate and explains how to verify it.

Also calledPavan (Tamil Nadu, Kerala) | Savaran (Karnataka)

Sovereign vs Pavan vs Savaran - Same Thing

All three terms refer to the same weight - 8 grams of gold:
• Sovereign: the colonial English term, still used across South India
• Pavan: Tamil Nadu and Kerala - from the Tamil 'pavan' (meaning pure/gold)
• Savaran: Karnataka - the Kannada term for sovereign

All three = 8 grams exactly. The IBJA rate per gram is the same for all.

How to Calculate the Sovereign Rate

Sovereign rate = IBJA per-gram rate × 8 × Purity fraction

For 22K:
₹13,965/g × 8 = ₹1,11,752 per sovereign

For 24K:
₹15,250/g × 8 = ₹1,22,000 per sovereign

Check ibja.co for the live per-gram rate, then multiply by 8 to get today's sovereign rate.

Selling Sovereign Gold Coins

  • Each coin is XRF tested - confirming purity
  • The old British Gold Sovereign coin weighs 7.988g of 22K (916) gold - not exactly 8g like Indian sovereigns
  • Indian sovereign coins are exactly 8g and typically 22K
  • No original packaging or certificate needed to sell - XRF testing is the verification method

Frequently Asked Questions

How many grams is 1 sovereign of gold?

1 sovereign = 8 grams exactly. This is the standard used in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Kerala.

What is 1 sovereign of 22K gold worth today?

₹1,11,752 at today's IBJA rate of ₹13,965/g for 22K.

Is pavan the same as sovereign?

Yes - pavan and sovereign both refer to 8 grams of gold. Pavan is the Tamil term, sovereign is the English term.

Is savaran the same as sovereign?

Yes - savaran is the Kannada term for the same 8-gram weight.

How do I sell sovereign gold coins?

Is the British Gold Sovereign coin 8 grams?

No - the British Gold Sovereign is 7.988 grams of 22K (916) gold. Indian sovereigns are defined as exactly 8 grams.

What is the sovereign gold rate today vs the IBJA rate?

The IBJA rate is ₹13,965/g for 22K. Multiply by 8 to get the sovereign rate: ₹1,11,752.

title: How to Estimate Gold Weight Without a Scale: Methods & Accuracy
metaTitle: How to Estimate Gold Weight Without a Scale: Methods & Accuracy | Aryan Gold Buyers
description: You want to know roughly what your gold is worth before visiting a branch - but you do not have a jewellery scale at home. Is there any way to estimate the…
html:
How to Estimate Gold Weight Without a Scale: Methods & Accuracy

You want to know roughly what your gold is worth before visiting a branch - but you do not have a jewellery scale at home. Is there any way to estimate the weight?

Yes - there are several estimation methods, though none are as accurate as a calibrated digital scale. This guide shows you what works, what does not, and how to get a good enough estimate to walk in informed.

At a Glance

Most reliable home methodWater displacement (Archimedes method) for solid pieces
Quick estimate methodCoin comparison or typical-weight reference tables
Accuracy of home estimation±10–20% typically - enough for a rough estimate
Official weight?Always determined at the branch on a calibrated scale
Bring your own scale?Yes - a kitchen or jewellery scale (0.01g precision) is inexpensive
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Method 1: Water Displacement (Most Accurate Without a Scale)

This works for solid, non-hollow gold pieces (rings, bangles without lac filling, pendants).

What you need: A measuring cup with ml markings, water

Steps:
1. Fill the measuring cup with a known amount of water (e.g. 100ml)
2. Note the water level precisely
3. Gently place your gold piece completely submerged
4. Note the new water level
5. The difference (in ml) equals the volume of the gold piece (1ml water displaced = 1cm³)

Density of 22K gold: ~17.7 g/cm³
Weight estimate = Displaced volume (cm³) × 17.7

Example: Piece displaces 1.2ml → weight ≈ 1.2 × 17.7 = 21.2g

Limitation: Works poorly for hollow bangles, lac-filled pieces, or stone-set jewellery.

Gold KaratDensity (g/cm³)Use This to Convert Volume to Weight
24K19.3Displaced cm³ × 19.3
22K17.7–18.0Displaced cm³ × 17.8
18K15.2–15.6Displaced cm³ × 15.4
14K12.9–13.3Displaced cm³ × 13.1

Method 2: Typical Weight Reference (Fastest)

Use known typical weights for your jewellery type (see the reference tables in our bangle and chain weight guides). Cross-reference your piece's visual size with the typical range.

Quick reference:
• Plain thin ring: 2–5g
• Medium chain (45cm): 8–15g
• Plain bangle: 6–15g
• 1 sovereign coin: 8g (exactly)

This is a rough estimate - actual weight may vary by 20–40% depending on design.

Method 3: Compare to Coins (Coin Calibration)

If you have a coin whose weight you know (e.g. a 10-rupee coin weighs 7.74g, a 5-rupee coin weighs 6g), you can use a simple balance improvised from a ruler and pivot point.

Place the known coin on one end and your gold piece on the other. Adjust until balanced. If the gold piece balances with two 10-rupee coins (15.48g), your gold is approximately 15g.

Accuracy: ±2–4g - only useful for rough estimates.

The Most Practical Solution: Buy an Inexpensive Jewellery Scale

A digital jewellery scale accurate to 0.01g costs ₹300–₹1,000 online (search for '0.01g digital jewellery scale'). This is the single best investment for anyone who regularly wants to check gold weights at home.

With an accurate scale, you can verify weights before visiting a buyer - which protects you from discrepancies and lets you calculate the expected payout:

Formula: Weight (g) × Purity fraction × ₹15,250/g (IBJA 24K rate today)

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I accurately weigh gold at home without a scale?

Approximately - water displacement gives ±5–10% accuracy for solid pieces. For hollow or stone-set pieces, accuracy is worse. Only a calibrated scale gives the true weight.

What kind of scale should I buy for weighing gold?

A digital jewellery scale accurate to 0.01g. Available online for ₹300–₹1,000.

How accurate is the water displacement method for gold?

For solid, unfilled pieces: ±5–10%. For hollow or lac-filled pieces: significantly less accurate.

Does a kitchen scale work for weighing gold?

Kitchen scales typically measure to 1g accuracy - not precise enough for small pieces. A jewellery scale (0.01g) is much better.

How do I know my sovereign coin weighs 8g?

A 22K gold sovereign (pavan) is defined as exactly 8 grams - this is a fixed standard. Use it as a reference weight.

Why does the branch weight differ from my estimate?

Calibrated branch scales are accurate to 0.01g. Home estimation methods can be off by 1–4g. The branch weight is the official one for payment purposes.

Can I challenge the branch weight if I think it is wrong?

Yes - ask for it to be re-weighed on a zeroed scale in front of you. You can also bring your own calibrated scale for comparison.

Gold Valuation Certificate: What It Is & When You Need One

A gold valuation certificate (also called a gold appraisal or assay certificate) is a written document from a qualified professional stating the weight, purity and estimated market value of your gold jewellery or bullion.

You may need one for insurance, a bank loan, probate, or a legal dispute. This guide explains when it is required, who issues it, and whether it affects how much you receive when you sell.

At a Glance

What is it?A certified document stating gold weight, purity and market value
Who issues it?BIS-certified hallmarking centres, licensed jewellery appraisers, some banks
When needed?Insurance claims, bank gold loans, probate, legal disputes, customs
Cost₹100–₹500 per piece typically
Does it affect resale price?No - XRF testing at a buyer determines purity independently
Is it mandatory to sell gold?No - not required at a gold buyer
Last UpdatedMay 2026

When Do You Need a Gold Valuation Certificate?

PurposeCertificate Required?Notes
Home/jewellery insurance claimYesRequired to prove value at time of loss
Bank gold loan applicationUsually yesBank assesses independently but certificate helps
Probate / estate settlementSometimesCourts or lawyers may require it for estate division
Legal dispute over gold ownershipPossiblyAs evidence of value at a specific date
Customs clearance (import)PossiblyFor valuation of imported gold above duty-free limit
Selling gold at a buyerNoXRF at branch replaces it - no certificate needed
Insurance purchase (new jewellery)RecommendedHelps establish insured value

Who Issues Gold Valuation Certificates in India?

  • BIS-certified Hallmarking Centres: the most authoritative for purity certification
  • Licensed jewellery valuers registered with SEBI/banks: for financial/legal purposes
  • Reputable jewellery stores: informal valuations - not always accepted by insurance or courts
  • Banks: some banks have internal assessors for gold loan purposes
  • Government-approved assay offices: for commercial/customs purposes

Does a Valuation Certificate Affect Your Selling Price?

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need a gold valuation certificate to sell gold?

What is a gold valuation certificate used for?

Primarily for insurance claims, bank gold loans, probate proceedings and legal disputes. Not needed for a standard gold sale.

Where can I get a gold valuation certificate in India?

BIS-certified hallmarking centres, licensed jewellery valuers, and some reputable jewellery stores.

How much does a gold valuation certificate cost?

Typically ₹100–₹500 per piece, depending on the issuer and the complexity of assessment.

Does a valuation certificate guarantee I get that price when selling?

No - buyers use XRF testing to determine their own purity assessment, which may differ from the certificate.

Is a valuation certificate the same as a hallmark?

No - a hallmark is stamped on the jewellery itself and certifies purity at manufacture. A valuation certificate is a separate document that includes a market value estimate.

Does jewellery insurance require a valuation certificate?

Most policies require one for valuable pieces. Check your policy terms for the specific requirement.

html:
SGB Early Exit: How to Sell Sovereign Gold Bonds Before Maturity

Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) are issued by the Government of India with an 8-year maturity. But what if you need to exit before 8 years? You have two options: early redemption through the RBI, or selling on the stock exchange.

This guide explains both routes, the tax implications of each, and whether early exit makes financial sense.

At a Glance

SGB maturity8 years from issue date
Early redemption windowAfter 5th year - on coupon payment dates
Stock exchange exitAny time after listing (typically 2–6 weeks from issue)
Tax on RBI redemption (after 8 yr)Capital gains tax-exempt if held to maturity
Tax on early RBI redemptionLTCG at 12.5% if held 24+ months
Tax on stock exchange saleLTCG at 12.5% (if held 24+ months); stamp duty applies
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Two Ways to Exit SGBs Early

Exit MethodWhen AvailablePriceTax
RBI Early RedemptionAfter 5th year (on coupon dates)RBI redemption price (market-linked)LTCG 12.5%
Stock Exchange SaleAfter listing (any time)Market price on exchangeLTCG 12.5% if held 24+ months
Hold to MaturityAfter 8 yearsRBI redemption priceTax-exempt on capital gains

Early Redemption Through RBI

The RBI allows premature redemption of SGBs starting from the 5th year after the issue date. Redemption is only possible on coupon payment dates (twice yearly).

Process:
1. Contact your bank or DMAT account provider
2. Submit an early redemption request before the deadline (typically 10 days before the coupon date)
3. The RBI fixes the redemption price based on average IBJA closing price of the preceding 3 business days
4. Payment credited to your bank account

Note: You lose the remaining 3 years of 2.5% annual coupon payments.

Selling on the Stock Exchange

SGBs are listed on NSE and BSE. You can sell them at any time after listing through your broker or DMAT account.

Advantages:
• More flexible than waiting for coupon dates
• Market price may be above or below the RBI redemption price

Disadvantages:
• Liquidity varies - some older SGB tranches have very low trading volumes
• You pay brokerage and exchange charges
• Market price may be at a discount to the underlying gold value in thin markets

Tax on SGB Early Exit

  • RBI early redemption (after 5 years): Capital gain = redemption price − issue price. LTCG at 12.5% (well past 24 months).
  • Stock exchange sale (after 24 months): LTCG at 12.5% on the gain
  • Stock exchange sale (within 24 months of SGB purchase): STCG at slab rate
  • Hold to maturity (8 years): Capital gains are completely exempt - the biggest tax advantage of SGBs
  • Annual coupon of 2.5%: taxable as 'other income' regardless of exit route

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell my SGB before 8 years?

Yes - via RBI early redemption (after 5 years) or on the stock exchange (any time after listing).

When can I redeem SGBs from the RBI?

After the 5th year from the issue date, on coupon payment dates (twice yearly). Not before.

Is SGB early exit taxed?

Yes - capital gains tax applies (12.5% LTCG if held 24+ months). Only maturity redemption after 8 years is capital gains tax-exempt.

How do I sell SGB on the stock exchange?

Through your broker or DMAT account. SGBs are listed on NSE and BSE.

What price do I get on SGB early redemption?

The RBI uses the average IBJA gold price for the preceding 3 business days as the redemption price.

Is it better to exit SGB early or hold to maturity?

Holding to maturity saves 12.5% LTCG tax. Early exit makes sense only if you need immediate cash or expect gold prices to fall significantly.

What is the SGB coupon rate?

2.5% per annum on the nominal (issue) value, paid twice yearly. This is taxable as other income regardless of when you exit.

Is Selling Gold Anonymous in India? Privacy, PAN & What Is Recorded

A common question: can I sell gold without anyone knowing? In India today, the answer is: no - not above minimal amounts. KYC (Know Your Customer) requirements mean your identity is always linked to a gold sale, and certain transactions are reported to income tax authorities.

This guide explains exactly what is recorded, when, and what that means for you.

At a Glance

Aadhaar required?Yes - for all gold sales, no exceptions
PAN required?Yes - if sale > ₹2,00,000
Cash limit₹2,00,000 per Section 269ST - above this must be bank transfer
Is the sale reported to IT?High-value transactions may be flagged - see below
Can you sell anonymously?No - KYC links all gold sales to your identity
Last UpdatedMay 2026

What Is Recorded When You Sell Gold

InformationAlways Recorded?When PAN Also Required
Aadhaar numberYes - all salesAll sales
Name and addressYes - from AadhaarAll sales
Weight soldYesAll sales
PurityYesAll sales
Amount receivedYesAll sales
PAN numberOnly if sale > ₹2,00,000Sale > ₹2L
Bank account (for transfer)If paid by bank transferLarge amounts

What Is Reported to Income Tax Authorities

  • Section 269ST prohibits cash transactions above ₹2,00,000 - all large payments must be bank transfer
  • SFT (Statement of Financial Transactions): gold buyers may be required to report high-value transactions to the IT department
  • Form 26AS: if TCS (Tax Collected at Source) is applicable, it appears in your Form 26AS
  • If your total gold sale in a year exceeds ₹10 lakh, it may trigger an IT query
  • IT departments use financial intelligence to flag unusual cash transactions or large asset disposals

What This Means for Sellers

  • All legitimate gold sales in India are identity-linked - this is not unusual or alarming; it is standard KYC compliance
  • If your sale is within your CBDT gold allowance and from declared income, there is nothing to worry about
  • Declare capital gains in your ITR for the year of sale - this is the legitimate path
  • Attempting to avoid identification (splitting sales across multiple buyers, false IDs) is illegal and carries serious penalties

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell gold without showing my Aadhaar?

No - Aadhaar is mandatory for all gold sales at reputable buyers. This is a regulatory requirement under KYC/PMLA guidelines.

Is my gold sale reported to the income tax department?

High-value transactions may be reported. Sales above ₹2L require PAN which links to your tax records. TCS may appear in Form 26AS.

Can I split a large gold sale into smaller amounts to avoid PAN?

Intentionally splitting a single sale to avoid the ₹2L PAN threshold is illegal under PMLA. Do not attempt this.

What happens if I sell without Aadhaar?

A reputable gold buyer will not complete the sale without Aadhaar - this is regulatory compliance. Avoid buyers who offer to skip ID requirements.

Are gold sales confidential?

Your transaction data is subject to KYC confidentiality standards but is accessible to regulatory authorities (IT department, PMLA) when required.

Do I need to tell anyone I sold gold?

You need to declare the capital gain in your annual ITR. No other voluntary disclosure is required for ordinary sales.

Is there any way to sell gold without documentation?

No legitimate way. Unregulated cash buyers who offer this are operating illegally - avoid them entirely.

html:
Pawn Gold vs Sell Gold: Which Is Better for You in India?

When you need cash against your gold, you have two options: pawn it (gold loan) or sell it outright. Many people default to a gold loan assuming it is safer - but the maths often tells a different story.

This guide compares both options with real numbers at today's rates, so you can make an informed choice.

Quick Comparison

Gold loan interest rate12–28% per annum (varies by lender)
Gold loan LTV75–85% of gold value
Selling price₹13,965/g for 22K (IBJA rate, ~98% received)
Pawning gives75–85% now; you pay interest to get your gold back
Selling gives~98% now; gold is gone permanently
Break-even holding period4–8 months before loan interest exceeds the selling discount
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Gold Loan (Pawning) - How It Works

A gold loan (also called pledging or pawning gold) involves leaving your gold as collateral at a bank, NBFC or licensed moneylender in exchange for an immediate cash loan. Typical terms:

• LTV (Loan-to-Value): 75–85% of the gold's market value
• Interest rate: 12–28% p.a. depending on lender
• Tenure: 3–24 months typically
• If you repay: gold is returned; total repayment = principal + interest
• If you default: gold is auctioned to recover the outstanding amount

For a 20g 22K gold piece worth ₹2,79,380:
• Loan amount (at 80% LTV): ₹2,23,504
• Monthly interest (at 18% p.a.): ₹3,353/month
• After 6 months interest cost: ₹20,115

Selling - How It Compares

When Pawning Makes Sense

  • You need cash for a short period (under 3 months) and are confident you can repay
  • Gold price is rising and you expect to reclaim and sell at a higher rate later
  • The gold has high sentimental value and you are not ready to permanently part with it
  • You have a specific, timed need (business cash flow gap, seasonal agriculture expense) with predictable repayment

When Selling Makes More Sense

  • You do not need to reclaim the gold - it is sitting unused
  • The loan tenure is likely to extend beyond 6 months (interest cost becomes significant)
  • You are carrying other high-interest debt - better to sell, clear debt, start fresh
  • The gold is broken, damaged, or unhallmarked - less likely to get a good LTV from a lender
  • You want certainty - no risk of auction, no monthly interest pressure

The Bottom Line

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it better to pawn gold or sell gold?

It depends on your timeline. Under 3 months with confident repayment: pawn. Beyond 4–6 months or if repayment is uncertain: sell.

How much do I get for pawning gold?

75–85% of gold value as a loan. Selling gets you approximately 97–99% of the IBJA rate - significantly more upfront.

What interest rate do gold loans charge?

12–28% per annum depending on the lender (bank NBFCs are lower; pawnshops can be higher).

Can I get my gold back after pawning?

Yes - if you repay the principal plus interest within the loan tenure. If you default, the lender auctions the gold.

What is the LTV on a gold loan?

Typically 75–85% of the gold's current market value, as per RBI guidelines for banks and NBFCs.

How does pawning gold affect my credit score?

Gold loans are secured loans. Repaying on time can help your credit score. Defaulting can harm it.

html:
Gold Gifted by Your Employer: Tax Rules When You Sell It

Gold coins, biscuits and jewellery are common gifts given by employers in India - at Diwali, on performance milestones, or at retirement. While the gift itself is a welcome recognition, many employees are unsure whether it is taxable when received, and what tax applies when they later sell it.

The answer is different from family gold gifts - employer gifts have less generous tax treatment.

At a Glance

Is employer gold gift taxable on receipt?Yes - if value exceeds ₹5,000 per year, it is perquisite income
Tax on receiptAdded to salary income - taxed at your income slab
Capital gains when you sell?Yes - based on fair market value on date of gift
Holding period startDate the gift was received
LTCG if held 24+ months from gift date12.5% on the gain
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Tax on Gold Received as an Employer Gift

Under Section 17(2)(viii) of the Income Tax Act, gifts from an employer are treated as perquisites - part of your salary income. The rules:

• If total gifts from the employer in a financial year are ₹5,000 or less: fully exempt
• If total gifts exceed ₹5,000: the entire value (not just the excess) is added to your taxable salary

Example: Your company gifts you a 10g gold coin at Diwali. At today's rate, it is worth ₹1,52,500. As this exceeds ₹5,000, the entire ₹1,52,500 is added to your salary income and taxed at your slab rate (20%, 30%, etc.).

The employer will typically report this in Form 16, and TDS may be deducted.

Capital Gains When You Sell Employer-Gifted Gold

When you later sell the gold:
• Cost of acquisition = Fair Market Value (FMV) on the date you received the gift
• Holding period = from the date the gift was received
• If held 24+ months from receipt: 12.5% LTCG on the gain
• If held under 24 months: profit added to income at slab rate

Note: The FMV is typically the IBJA market rate on the date the gift was given. Keep a record of the FMV on the date of receipt for your tax calculation later.

Worked Example

You received a 10g 24K gold coin from your employer on Diwali 2023. The IBJA 24K rate on that date was ₹6,200/g. FMV = 10 × ₹6,200 = ₹62,000.

You sell it today at ₹1,52,500 (₹15,250/g × 10g).

Capital gain = ₹1,52,500 − ₹62,000 = ₹90,500
Holding period: Diwali 2023 to now = 24+ months → LTCG
Tax: ₹90,500 × 12.5% = ₹11,312

Also, the ₹62,000 was already taxed as salary perquisite when you received it - so you are not double-taxed on the base value.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is gold received from my employer taxable?

Yes - if the total value of gifts from the employer exceeds ₹5,000 in a year, the full gift value is added to your taxable salary.

What is the cost basis for selling employer-gifted gold?

The fair market value (IBJA rate) on the date you received the gift.

How long must I hold employer-gifted gold for LTCG?

24 months from the date you received the gift. After that, 12.5% LTCG applies.

Does my employer deduct TDS on gold gifts?

They may deduct TDS if the gold gift is treated as a perquisite exceeding ₹5,000. It will appear in Form 16.

Is this different from gold gifted by family members?

Yes - family gifts at marriage are exempt from perquisite tax. Employer gifts above ₹5,000 are taxable as salary.

Do I need to report employer gold gifts in my ITR?

Yes - if TDS was deducted, it appears in Form 26AS. Report the perquisite in your salary income. Report the capital gain when you sell.

html:
Selling Gold Before Leaving India: Process, Tax & What to Consider

If you are leaving India - for work abroad, emigration or a long stay overseas - you may be wondering whether to sell your gold before departure or take it with you. Each option has financial and practical implications.

This guide helps you make an informed decision and covers the selling process if you decide to sell.

At a Glance

Can you take gold out of India?Yes - with customs duty on excess; jewellery within limits is allowed
Duty on taking gold outNot applicable - export of personal gold has no exit duty
Tax if you sell before leavingCapital gains tax applies if you have made a gain
Tax if you sell after returningSame capital gains rules - based on holding period and purchase price
When to sell?Before leaving if you need INR; after returning if you want to keep it
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Should You Sell Before Leaving or Keep the Gold?

SituationRecommended Action
You need INR cash before departureSell before leaving - straightforward branch visit
You are emigrating permanentlyConsider selling if you will not use it abroad
You are going for 2–3 years (work)Keep it - you can sell when you return
Gold is in a bank lockerSell before leaving to avoid locker charges during absence
Gold is jewellery you wear regularlyTake it within customs limits as personal jewellery
Large holding (500g+)Sell before leaving - large amounts are hard to transport

The Selling Process Before Departure

  1. Bring Aadhaar card (mandatory) and PAN (if sale > ₹2,00,000)
  2. XRF purity testing + weighing - 15–20 minutes
  3. Payment via bank transfer (recommended before departure - avoids carrying cash)
  4. Keep the sale receipt for your ITR filing in India (even if non-resident)
  5. Declare the capital gain in your ITR for the financial year of sale

Tax on Gold Sold Before Leaving India

  • Capital gains tax applies if the gold has appreciated since purchase
  • Held 24+ months: 12.5% LTCG on the gain
  • Held under 24 months: profit added to income at slab rate
  • Your residential status (resident vs NRI) for the financial year of the sale determines which ITR form to use
  • If you become non-resident mid-year, a chartered accountant can help with the appropriate tax filing
  • Keep sale receipts to substantiate the transaction if queried later

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I take my gold jewellery out of India?

Yes - personal jewellery being worn or carried for personal use can be taken out. Large quantities or commercial gold requires export documentation.

Should I sell gold before emigrating from India?

If you need INR funds or are leaving permanently, selling makes sense. If leaving temporarily, keeping the gold invested may be better long-term.

Is there any exit tax on gold leaving India?

No - personal gold taken as jewellery within customs limits does not attract an exit tax or duty.

What happens if I sell gold and then leave India?

You must file an ITR for the financial year of the sale. As a non-resident for part of the year, your CA can advise on the appropriate form.

What if my PAN is linked to India - can I still file ITR from abroad?

Yes - ITR can be filed online through the Income Tax e-filing portal from anywhere in the world.

What documents do I need to sell gold before leaving?

Aadhaar and PAN (if sale > ₹2,00,000). No emigration or travel documents are needed at the gold buyer.

html:
Gold at Indian Airports: Customs Rules, Limits & What Happens If You Exceed Them

Every year, thousands of travellers arrive at Indian airports carrying gold - as jewellery, gifts, coins or bars. Customs rules govern how much is allowed duty-free, what duty applies on the excess, and what happens if gold is not declared.

This guide explains the rules clearly so you know exactly what to do.

At a Glance

Green channelDuty-free allowance only - jewellery within limits
Red channelDeclare all gold bars/coins, excess jewellery
Duty-free for male travellers20g jewellery, max ₹50,000 (if abroad ≥ 6 months)
Duty-free for female travellers40g jewellery, max ₹1,00,000 (if abroad ≥ 6 months)
Duty on excess / bars~18% of assessed value
Penalty for non-declarationSeizure + fine of 100–300% of duty
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Green Channel vs Red Channel: Which to Use

What You Are CarryingChannel to Use
Jewellery within duty-free limit (20g/40g), no bars or coinsGreen Channel
Jewellery above duty-free limitRed Channel - declare and pay duty
Any gold bars, coins or biscuits (regardless of quantity)Red Channel - duty from first gram
Foreign currency above $5,000 USD + gold combinationRed Channel
Not sure?Always use Red Channel when in doubt

What Happens During Customs Inspection

  • Customs officers may use X-ray scanners and physical inspection at both Green and Red channels
  • If gold is detected in Green Channel that should have been declared, it may be seized
  • At the Red Channel, you declare, present purchase receipts if available, and pay assessed duty
  • Customs calculates duty on the CIF (Cost + Insurance + Freight) value of the gold
  • Payment is accepted in INR, major foreign currencies, or card at the airport customs counter
  • You receive a receipt for duty paid - keep this for your records

Penalties for Non-Declaration

If gold above the duty-free limit is found at the Green Channel:
• The gold may be seized
• A fine of 100–300% of the evaded duty may be imposed
• In serious cases, COFEPOSA (Conservation of Foreign Exchange and Prevention of Smuggling Activities Act) may be invoked

The penalties far exceed the duty that would have been payable - always declare.

After Clearing Customs: Selling the Gold

Frequently Asked Questions

How much gold can I bring into India at the airport?

Jewellery: 20g (male) or 40g (female), max ₹50,000 or ₹1,00,000 respectively, if you have been abroad ≥ 6 months. Gold bars and coins attract duty from the first gram.

Do I need to declare gold at the airport?

Yes, if above the duty-free limit or if carrying any gold bars/coins. Use the Red Channel.

What is the duty rate on gold at Indian airports?

Approximately 18% of the assessed value (15% basic duty + AGIF cess + surcharge).

Can I be caught with undeclared gold?

Yes - X-ray scanners detect gold. Penalties include seizure and fines of 100–300% of the evaded duty.

Can I bring gold as a gift for someone in India?

The duty-free allowance covers your personal jewellery. Gifts above this limit attract duty.

Do I need to declare gold I am wearing?

Bonafide personal jewellery being worn is generally not required to be declared if within the duty-free limit. Excess must be declared.
