How Much Gold Can an NRI Bring to India? Customs Rules & Limits

Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) visiting India often bring gold jewellery, coins and biscuits from abroad - as gifts, personal jewellery or as investments. Customs rules set specific limits on how much gold you can bring duty-free, and what duty applies above those limits.

This guide explains the current rules, what to declare at the airport, and what to do with the gold once you are in India.

At a Glance

Duty-free limit - male NRI20g jewellery, max ₹50,000 value
Duty-free limit - female NRI40g jewellery, max ₹1,00,000 value
Duty on excess gold bars/biscuits15% customs duty + AGIF cess
Minimum stay abroad for allowance6 months
Can you bring gold bars duty-free?No - only jewellery qualifies for duty-free allowance
Declare above limit?Yes - at customs Green/Red channel
Last UpdatedMay 2026

NRI Gold Allowance: Current Customs Rules

CategoryDuty-Free LimitCondition
Male NRI (jewellery)20g, max ₹50,000Must have been abroad ≥ 6 months
Female NRI (jewellery)40g, max ₹1,00,000Must have been abroad ≥ 6 months
Gold bars / coins / biscuitsNIL duty-freeDuty applies from first gram
Personal wearing jewelleryNo limit if bonafide personal useDeclaration may still be needed

Customs Duty on Gold Above the Allowance

For gold above the duty-free limit (or any gold bars/coins):
• Basic Customs Duty: 15%
• AGIF cess: 3% of duty = 0.45%
• Social Welfare Surcharge: 10% of duty = 1.5%
• Effective total duty: approximately 16.5–18% of value

For every 10g of 24K gold brought in above the duty-free limit:
Duty payable = ₹1,52,500 × 18% = approximately ₹27,450

What to Do at the Airport

  • If carrying within the duty-free limit: proceed through the Green Channel
  • If carrying above the limit or bringing bars/coins: proceed through the Red Channel and declare
  • Do not attempt to conceal excess gold - penalties include seizure plus fine of 100–300% of duty
  • Customs officers may ask for the original purchase receipt for gold brought in
  • Keep all purchase receipts from the country of purchase for duty calculation

Selling Gold Brought from Abroad in India

Frequently Asked Questions

How much gold can an NRI bring to India?

Male NRIs: 20g jewellery duty-free (max ₹50,000). Female NRIs: 40g jewellery duty-free (max ₹1,00,000). Gold bars/coins attract duty from the first gram.

What is the duty on gold brought to India above the limit?

Approximately 18% of value (15% basic duty + cess + surcharge).

Can an NRI bring gold bars duty-free?

No - duty-free allowance applies only to gold jewellery. Bars and coins attract duty from the first gram.

Do I need to declare gold at the airport?

Yes, if above the duty-free limit or if bringing bars/coins. Use the Red Channel for declaration.

Can I sell foreign gold in India?

Yes - once legally imported (duty paid or within allowance), you can sell it at any gold buyer. XRF testing determines purity and you are paid the IBJA rate.

How long must I have been abroad to claim the NRI gold allowance?

At least 6 months abroad.

What documents do I need at a gold buyer for foreign gold?

Aadhaar and PAN (if applicable). No customs receipt is required at the buyer.

Gold Chain Weight per cm: How to Estimate Your Chain's Value Before Selling

People often ask: 'My chain is 45 cm - how much is it worth?' The answer depends on the chain's design (some chains are much heavier per cm than others), the karat (22K vs 18K), and today's gold rate.

This guide gives you per-cm weight references for common chain types and a quick way to estimate value before you visit the branch.

At a Glance

Lightest chains (per cm)Box chain, cable chain: 0.1–0.2g/cm
Medium chains (per cm)Rope chain, figaro: 0.3–0.6g/cm
Heavy chains (per cm)Cuban, Franco: 0.8–2.0g/cm
Average 45cm ladies chain6g – 15g (design-dependent)
22K rate today₹13,965/g
10g chain (22K) today₹1,39,690
Best methodWeigh at home or at branch - length is a guide only
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Gold Chain Weight per cm by Design

Chain TypeWeight/cm (approx)45cm Chain Weight45cm Value (22K)
Box chain (fine)0.08–0.15g3.5–7g₹69,845 – ₹97,783
Cable / link chain (fine)0.1–0.2g4.5–9g₹69,845 – ₹1,25,721
Singapore / twisted rope0.15–0.25g7–11g₹97,783 – ₹1,53,659
Rope chain (medium)0.25–0.5g11–22g₹1,53,659 – ₹3,07,318
Figaro chain0.3–0.6g13–27g₹1,81,597 – ₹3,77,163
Snake chain (medium)0.3–0.5g13–22g₹1,81,597 – ₹3,07,318
Ball chain0.4–0.7g18–31g₹2,51,442 – ₹4,33,039
Cuban / curb chain (medium)0.7–1.5g31–67g₹4,33,039 – ₹9,35,923
Franco / box curb (heavy)1.0–2.5g45–112g₹6,28,605 – ₹15,64,528

Why Length Alone Does Not Determine Value

Two 45cm chains can have radically different weights and values:
• A fine cable chain at 0.15g/cm = 6.75g
• A medium Cuban chain at 1.2g/cm = 54g

At today's 22K rate:
• Fine cable: ₹97,783
• Cuban chain: ₹7,54,326

This is why the actual weight at the scale is the only reliable measure. Length is useful for a rough estimate, but always verify at the branch.

How to Estimate Your Chain's Value

Step 1: Measure the length in cm
Step 2: Identify the chain type from the table above
Step 3: Apply a mid-range weight per cm
Step 4: Multiply by 0.916 (for 22K) × ₹15,250

Example: 50cm medium rope chain at 0.35g/cm = ~17.5g
17.5 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = approximately ₹2,37,473

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a gold chain weigh per cm?

It varies widely by design. Fine cable chains: 0.1–0.2g/cm. Medium rope chains: 0.3–0.5g/cm. Heavy Cuban chains: 0.7–1.5g/cm.

How do I know how much my 45cm chain is worth?

Estimate the weight using the per-cm table, then apply: weight × 0.916 (for 22K) × ₹15,250.

Why does my chain weigh less than I expected?

Many chain styles are hollow or very fine. Italian chain designs especially tend to look longer/heavier than their actual gold weight.

Does chain length affect the resale price?

Only insofar as length determines total weight. A longer chain weighs more and is worth more - but the rate per gram is the same.

What is the value of a 10g gold chain today?

10g of 22K gold = ₹1,39,690.

Should I detach the pendant before weighing?

Yes, if the pendant is sold separately. If selling chain and pendant together, they are weighed as a unit.

What chain type gives the most gold per cm?

Heavy chains like Cuban, Franco and Wheat chains have the highest gold content per cm.

html:
Gold Bangle Weight: How to Estimate Before Visiting the Branch

One of the most common questions before a gold sale is: 'How much is my bangle worth?' Getting a rough estimate before walking into a branch helps you compare offers, understand the value of what you own, and approach the sale confidently.

This guide gives you typical gold bangle weights by design type, today's rate, and estimated cash value.

At a Glance

Typical plain bangle weight6g - 15g per bangle
Typical bridal bangle weight15g - 30g per bangle (heavier designs)
Set of 4 plain bangles (22K)~24-48g total
22K rate today₹13,965/g
10g bangle (22K) today₹1,39,690
20g bangle (22K) today₹2,79,380
Actual weightConfirmed by scale at branch - estimate before, verify there
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Typical Gold Bangle Weights by Type

Bangle TypeTypical Weight per BangleValue Today (22K)
Thin plain wire bangle4g - 7g₹55,876 - ₹97,783
Medium plain round bangle8g - 12g₹1,11,752 - ₹1,67,628
Heavy plain bangle12g - 20g₹1,67,628 - ₹2,79,380
Openable (openable lock) bangle10g - 18g₹1,39,690 - ₹2,51,442
Stone-set bangle8g - 20g (gold wt after stone removal)₹1,11,752 - ₹2,79,380
Hollow bangle5g - 10g (lighter than appearance)₹69,845 - ₹1,39,690
Bridal kangan / broad bangle20g - 50g₹2,79,380 - ₹6,98,450
Kada (thick round bangle)25g - 80g₹3,49,225 - ₹11,17,520

How to Estimate Your Bangle's Value at Home

If you have a kitchen scale or jewellery scale at home:
1. Weigh the bangle - note the weight in grams
2. Check the hallmark: 916 (22K), 750 (18K), 585 (14K)
3. Apply the formula: Weight (g) × Purity fraction × IBJA rate

Example - 15g bangle, 22K hallmark:
15 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹2,09,535

Note: This is the reference figure. The branch will apply a small deduction of 1-2% as their margin, and any stones or lac filling will be assessed and excluded from the weight.

Important Notes on Bangle Weight

  • Hollow bangles weigh less than they appear - the hollow space adds no gold value
  • Stone-set bangles: stones are removed or estimated and deducted from the weight
  • Lac filling inside bangles: weight is estimated and deducted
  • Openable bangles with lock mechanisms: the lock is included in gold weight if it is the same alloy
  • Pairs: if selling a pair, weigh both together - the total matters, not which is heavier
  • Damaged or bent bangles: same rate - gold value is by weight and purity, not condition

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a gold bangle weigh?

Plain bangles typically weigh 6-15g each. Bridal or heavy bangles can be 20-50g. Weigh yours at home for an accurate estimate.

How do I calculate the value of my gold bangle?

Weight (g) × purity fraction × ₹15,250/g (today's IBJA 24K rate). For 22K: × 0.916.

Does a hollow bangle give less money?

Yes - hollow bangles weigh less per visual size, so you receive less. The rate per gram is the same, but there are fewer grams.

Are stone-set bangles worth less?

The gold portion pays the same rate. But stones are excluded from the weight calculation.

What if I have a set of 4 bangles?

Weigh all four together - the total weight × purity × IBJA rate gives the combined value.

Does bangle design affect the price?

No - only weight and purity matter at resale. Intricate designs are irrelevant.

How do I know if my bangle is 22K or 18K?

html:
How Gold Weight Is Measured: Scales, Units & Accuracy at the Branch

The weight of your gold is one of the two most critical numbers in any gold sale (the other is purity). Even a small error in weight measurement can cost you thousands of rupees.

This guide explains how reputable gold buyers weigh gold, what kind of scale to look for, and what to check to ensure the reading is correct.

At a Glance

Scale type usedPrecision digital jewellery scale
Required accuracy0.01g (10 milligram) precision minimum
CalibrationLegal-for-trade scales are government-calibrated annually
Unit usedGrams (g) - some branches may also show tola/sovereign
Should you watch the scale?Yes - always insist on seeing the display
Can you bring your own scale?Yes - compare readings; small differences are normal
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Types of Scales Used in Gold Weighing

Scale TypePrecisionUsed ForLegal Status
Precision digital (0.001g)0.001gLab / refinery gold testingLegal for trade if calibrated
Jewellery digital (0.01g)0.01gBranch gold buying - standardLegal for trade if calibrated
Counter digital (0.1g)0.1gLess precise - not ideal for small piecesShould not be used for gold
Balance (traditional)VariesOld-style / pawn shopsPhased out in most reputable buyers

What to Watch at the Branch

  • The scale display should be visible to you at all times - ask to see it if it is turned away
  • The scale should read 0.00g when empty before your pieces are placed (tare/zero function)
  • Stones, lac fillings and non-gold components are removed before weighing or their weight is deducted
  • If multiple pieces are weighed together, ask for individual weights - so you can verify the total
  • The receipt should show the exact weight used in the calculation - compare to what the scale showed you

Gold Weight Units in India

UnitGram EquivalentUsed In
Gram (g)1gUniversal - used by IBJA and all reputable buyers
Tola11.6638gNorth India, traditional jewellers
Sovereign / Pavan8gSouth India - Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala
Savaran8gSame as sovereign - regional term
Troy ounce31.1035gInternational gold market
Bhori11.664gWest Bengal, eastern India

Can You Verify the Weight Yourself?

Yes - you can bring a calibrated digital kitchen or jewellery scale from home to cross-check. Acceptable variation between well-calibrated scales is ±0.05g (less than 0.5% difference for most pieces).

If there is a significant discrepancy (more than 0.2g on a small piece), ask the branch to use the scale in front of you and note the reading.

Frequently Asked Questions

What type of scale is used to weigh gold?

Precision digital jewellery scales with 0.01g accuracy - calibrated annually under the Weights and Measures Act.

Can I watch while my gold is being weighed?

Always - a reputable buyer will weigh gold in front of you. Ask to see the scale display if it is not visible.

What if the scale reading seems wrong?

Ask for it to be re-weighed, or bring a calibrated scale from home to compare. Small differences (±0.05g) are normal between scales.

Does the chain lock or clasp get included in the weight?

Yes - the full physical piece is weighed. However, if the clasp or lock is clearly a different material, this may be flagged.

What is the difference between grams and tola?

1 tola = 11.6638 grams. For selling purposes, grams are the standard - all IBJA rates are per gram.

What is a sovereign in gold weight?

1 sovereign = 8 grams. Commonly used in South India. 1 sovereign of 22K gold is worth approximately ₹1,11,752 at today's rate.

Should I clean my gold before weighing?

No - cleaning is not required. Dried dirt adds minimal weight (under 0.02g typically) and does not affect the final calculation meaningfully.

html:
How Much Do You Actually Get Per Gram When Selling Gold in India?

Many sellers check the IBJA gold rate (₹13,965/g for 22K today) and expect to receive exactly that amount. In practice, what arrives in your hand is slightly less - and understanding why helps you avoid confusion and comparison.

This guide shows you the real per-gram figure you receive after all deductions, with actual worked examples.

At a Glance

IBJA 22K rate today₹13,965/g
What you typically receive97–99% of IBJA rate - i.e. ₹13,546–₹13,825/g
Stone/lac deductionsStones and fillings excluded from weight - not from rate
Making chargesNot deducted at resale - irrelevant when selling
Net payout formulaNet weight × Purity fraction × IBJA rate × (1 − buyer margin)
Last UpdatedMay 2026

The Journey from IBJA Rate to Your Actual Payout

The IBJA publishes the 22K rate as ₹13,965/g. Here is what happens between that number and what you receive:

StepWhat HappensExample on 20g 22K piece
IBJA 22K rateNational benchmark₹13,965/g
Gross weightWhat the scale shows20g
Purity fractionXRF confirms 22K = 91.6%× 0.916
Pure gold weightNet gold content18.32g of fine gold
Gross calculationBefore buyer margin₹2,79,380
Buyer margin deducted1–2% typical−₹4,191
You receiveFinal payout₹2,75,189

Real Payout Examples at Today's Rates

WeightKaratGross ValueAfter 1.5% MarginYou Receive (approx)
5g22K₹69,845₹68,797₹68,797
10g22K₹1,39,690₹1,37,595₹1,37,595
20g22K₹2,79,380₹2,75,189₹2,75,189
50g22K₹6,98,450₹6,87,973₹6,87,973
10g18K₹1,14,375₹1,12,659₹1,12,659
10g24K₹1,52,500₹1,50,062₹1,50,062

What Deductions Actually Apply at the Branch

  • Buyer margin: 1–3% below IBJA - this is the only deduction from the rate itself
  • Stone deductions: stones are removed from the weight (not the rate) - only net gold weight is paid for
  • Lac/resin filling: estimated weight deducted from gross weight
  • Making charges: NOT deducted - making charges are a purchase-time cost, irrelevant at resale
  • Melting charges: NOT charged by reputable gold buyers - refinery cost is covered by their margin

What Makes the Payout Vary Between Buyers

  • The buyer's margin - 1% is excellent, 3% is acceptable, 5%+ is above average
  • The XRF reading - different machines may give slightly different readings for the same piece; calibrated machines are more consistent
  • Lac and stone assessment - subjectivity in how much lac is estimated; reputable buyers are conservative in deductions
  • Hollow jewellery assessment - the hollow space adds no gold weight; well-calibrated scales should account for this

Frequently Asked Questions

How much per gram do I get when selling 22K gold?

At today's IBJA rate of ₹13,965/g and a typical 1–2% margin, you receive approximately ₹13,756–₹13,825/g.

Why do I get less than the IBJA rate?

The IBJA rate is the wholesale benchmark. Buyers deduct 1–3% to cover their operating costs and margin. This is standard and universal across reputable buyers.

Are making charges deducted when I sell gold?

No - making charges are only relevant when you purchase gold. At resale, only the gold content (weight × purity) is paid for.

Do stones reduce the per-gram rate?

No - stones are excluded from the weight, not from the rate. You are paid the full per-gram rate for the net gold weight.

How do I know if I am getting a fair rate per gram?

Check ibja.co for the IBJA rate. Calculate your expected payout (weight × purity × IBJA rate). Compare to what the buyer offers - if the gap is more than 3%, ask why.

Can the per-gram payout differ between buyers?

Does selling a larger weight give a better per-gram rate?

Not typically - reputable buyers have a consistent rate. However, for very large transactions (500g+), there may be room to negotiate.

html:
London Gold Fix: What It Is & How It Affects India's Gold Price

When you hear financial news mention 'the London gold price' or 'the LBMA gold fix', you are hearing about the global benchmark that ultimately flows through to the IBJA rate you use when selling gold in India.

Understanding this chain helps you make sense of why India's gold rate moves when it does - and what global events to watch if you are timing your gold sale.

At a Glance

London Gold Fix nameLBMA Gold Price (formerly London Gold Fix)
PublishedTwice daily: AM (~1:30 PM IST) and PM (~7:30 PM IST)
CurrencyUS Dollars per troy ounce
Who sets itICE Benchmark Administration (IBA) via electronic auction
How it reaches IndiaUSD price × USD/INR rate + import duty = IBJA rate
Why it mattersAll Indian IBJA rates trace back to this benchmark
Last UpdatedMay 2026

What Is the London Gold Fix?

The London Gold Fix (now officially called the LBMA Gold Price) is the global benchmark price for gold, set twice daily in London. It is administered by ICE Benchmark Administration (IBA) through an electronic auction process involving major bullion banks and gold trading firms.

Two fixings occur daily:
• AM Fix: approximately 10:30 AM London time (3:00–4:00 PM IST)
• PM Fix: approximately 3:00 PM London time (8:30–9:30 PM IST)

The fixing price represents the price at which buyers and sellers of physical gold are willing to transact in the London wholesale market.

How the London Fix Affects India's IBJA Rate

The IBJA (India Bullion and Jewellers Association) uses the London Gold Price as the starting point for calculating India's domestic gold rate:

Simplified formula:
IBJA rate = London price (USD/troy oz) ÷ 31.1 × USD/INR exchange rate × (1 + import duty rate)

The IBJA publishes its rate twice daily on working days - broadly aligned with the two London fixings, adjusted for the India-specific factors. When the London price rises at the AM fix, the IBJA's next publication reflects this increase.

Key Events That Move the London Gold Price

  • US Federal Reserve interest rate decisions - lower rates typically boost gold
  • US dollar strength/weakness - gold and USD have an inverse relationship
  • Geopolitical crises - gold is a safe-haven asset, demand rises during uncertainty
  • Inflation data - high inflation boosts gold as a hedge
  • Central bank buying/selling - large-scale central bank purchases lift the gold price
  • ETF inflows/outflows - gold ETF demand affects the London price
  • Economic recession fears - investors move to gold as a safe haven

What This Means for Indian Gold Sellers

  • When US interest rate decisions are announced, expect gold price movement in the hours that follow
  • Geopolitical crises (wars, sanctions, banking failures) typically lift gold
  • Watch the London AM fix timing (3:00–4:00 PM IST) - this is often when the day's direction becomes clear
  • The IBJA publishes at approximately 11:30 AM and 5:00 PM IST - both reflect the London market's direction
  • For most sellers, the difference between selling on Tuesday vs Wednesday is small - major directional moves take weeks to develop

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the London Gold Fix?

The London Gold Fix (now LBMA Gold Price) is the global benchmark gold price, set twice daily via an electronic auction in London. It is the starting point for gold pricing worldwide.

How does the London fix affect India's gold price?

The London price in USD is converted to INR and India's import duty is added, resulting in the IBJA domestic rate.

When is the London Gold Fix published?

Twice daily: AM around 10:30 AM London time (3 PM IST) and PM around 3:00 PM London time (8:30 PM IST).

Why does India's gold price change when the London price changes?

Because India imports most of its gold, and the import price is based on the London benchmark.

Should I wait for the London AM fix before selling gold?

For most retail sellers, no - the intraday difference is small. Major price trends matter more than the specific fixing time.

Is the London Gold Fix the same as the LBMA Gold Price?

Yes - the name changed in 2015 from London Gold Fix to LBMA Gold Price after the administration was restructured.

Where can I check the London gold price?

lbma.org.uk shows official LBMA Gold Prices. Financial news sites also report it daily.

html:
Spot Gold Price India: What It Is & How It Differs from the IBJA Rate

If you check the gold price online, you will often see two different numbers: the 'spot price' in US dollars per troy ounce, and the IBJA rate in Indian rupees per gram. These two numbers are related but not the same - and confusing them can lead to significant miscalculations when you try to estimate what your gold is worth.

This guide explains both clearly.

At a Glance

Spot gold priceInternational price in USD per troy ounce (31.1g)
IBJA rateIndian benchmark in INR per gram - what you use to sell
DifferenceSpot + import duty + USD/INR conversion + handling = IBJA
Which to use when selling?Always the IBJA rate - not the international spot price
Where to check IBJAibja.co - published twice daily on working days
Last UpdatedMay 2026

What Is the Spot Gold Price?

The spot gold price is the current price of gold in the international wholesale market - expressed in US Dollars per troy ounce. It is set continuously by trading on the LBMA (London Bullion Market Association) and COMEX (New York) futures exchange.

One troy ounce = 31.1035 grams.

If the international spot price is $2,400/oz, that equates to $2,400 ÷ 31.1 = approximately $77/g in USD.

How the IBJA Rate Is Derived from the Spot Price

The IBJA rate is not simply a direct conversion of the spot price. It adds several India-specific factors:

1. USD/INR exchange rate (live)
2. Basic customs duty: 15%
3. AGIF (Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess): 3%
4. Social Welfare Surcharge: ~10% on customs duty
5. Refining and handling margins

Result: Indian gold prices are systematically higher than the raw USD spot price would suggest after simple currency conversion. This is why India's gold price often seems high compared to international benchmarks - the import duty structure adds approximately 18–20% above the pure conversion rate.

ComponentExampleRunning Total
International spot (USD/troy oz)$2,400-
Convert to INR/g (at ₹84/USD)$77/g × ₹84 = ₹6,468/g₹6,468/g
Basic customs duty (+15%)₹970/g₹7,438/g
AGIF cess (+3% on duty)₹194/g₹7,632/g
Other levies & handling~₹200–400/g~₹7,800–8,000/g
IBJA 24K rate (approximate)₹15,250/gActual IBJA rate

Why You Should Use the IBJA Rate, Not the Spot Price

  • The spot price is for institutional wholesale gold - not the rate at which Indian buyers purchase or sell
  • The IBJA rate is the actual Indian benchmark that gold buyers use to pay sellers
  • If you convert the spot price directly to INR/g, you will underestimate the Indian gold price by 15–20%
  • Always use ibja.co for the correct Indian per-gram rate before going to sell
  • Financial news apps (Moneycontrol, ET Money) typically show the IBJA rate - but always verify the source

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the spot gold price today in India?

The spot price is an international USD figure. Use the IBJA rate (on ibja.co) for the Indian selling rate.

Why is India's gold price higher than the international spot price?

India adds approximately 18–20% in import duty, cess and handling costs to the international price.

Does the Indian gold rate always follow the international spot price?

Yes, directionally - when the international price rises, India's IBJA rate rises too. But the exact conversion includes duty and exchange rate factors.

Where can I check the real gold price for selling in India?

ibja.co for the official IBJA rate, published twice per working day.

If the international gold price falls, does India's gold price also fall?

Generally yes - but the magnitude depends on the USD/INR exchange rate and whether any duty changes occur.

What is a troy ounce?

A troy ounce is 31.1035 grams - the international standard unit for gold pricing. It is different from a standard (avoirdupois) ounce of 28.35g.

Is the IBJA rate the same as the spot gold price?

No - the IBJA rate is India's domestic benchmark derived from the international spot price after adding import duty, exchange rate conversion and other charges.

24K Gold Coin in India: Types, Prices & How to Sell for Best Value

24K gold coins are one of the most popular forms of physical gold investment in India. They are sold by banks, MMTC-PAMP, and authorised dealers - and they are easy to sell because they come with certified purity and standard weights.

This guide covers the main 24K gold coin types available in India, today's prices, and how to get the best value when you sell.

How to Sell 24K Gold Coins in India

  1. XRF testing confirms 24K purity - takes 60 seconds
  2. Coin is weighed on precision digital scale
  3. Payout = Weight (g) × ₹15,250/g (IBJA 24K rate)
  4. Payment same day - cash or bank transfer
  5. Documents: Aadhaar mandatory, PAN if sale > ₹2,00,000

Does the Original Certificate or Packaging Matter?

For the resale calculation, no - XRF testing replaces the certificate. You will receive the same per-gram IBJA rate whether or not you have the original MMTC-PAMP card or bank receipt.

However, for your own tax records (establishing cost basis for capital gains), keeping the original purchase receipt is advisable.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the price of a 24K gold coin in India today?

A 10g 24K gold coin is worth ₹1,52,500 today. A 5g coin is ₹76,250.

Which is the best gold coin to buy in India?

MMTC-PAMP coins are widely considered the most trustworthy - Swiss-certified, tamper-proof packaging, and easy to sell. India Gold Coin (RBI) is also well-recognised.

Can I sell a gold coin without the original packaging?

Yes. XRF testing confirms purity regardless of packaging. You receive the IBJA rate for the tested purity and weight.

Do I get more for a coin than for jewellery?

Yes - coins have no making charges to worry about and no stone deductions. You receive the full per-gram gold value based on purity.

Are foreign gold coins (Krugerrand, Maple Leaf) accepted?

Yes - XRF testing confirms the gold content. You are paid at the IBJA rate for the confirmed purity and weight.

What is the difference between a gold coin and a gold biscuit?

Shape only - both are 24K gold. Coins are round, biscuits/bars are rectangular. The per-gram price is the same for the same purity.

Do I pay tax when selling a gold coin?

Yes - capital gains tax applies. If held 24+ months, 12.5% LTCG on the gain. If under 24 months, added to income at your slab rate.

html:
Gold Over Silver: What It Means, How to Identify It & Resale Value

'Gold over silver' or 'GOS' is a marking you might find on imported jewellery - it simply means a silver base metal with a gold layer applied on top. It is essentially the same as gold vermeil in construction, though the term is more commonly used in American and European jewellery markets.

If you own a piece marked GOS and want to know its resale value, this guide explains what you are dealing with.

At a Glance

Gold over silver meansSilver base with gold layer - not solid gold
Common stampGOS, 925 GOS, or Gold over Silver
Gold contentVery thin gold layer over silver core
Resale valueSilver scrap value - gold layer negligible
Same as vermeil?Essentially yes - silver base, gold plating
Last UpdatedMay 2026

What Does GOS Mean on Jewellery?

GOS stands for 'Gold Over Silver'. It indicates that the piece is made of sterling silver (92.5% silver) as the base, with gold electroplated or bonded on the surface.

Common stamps include:
• GOS
• 925 GOS
• Gold Over Silver
• Sterling Silver with Gold

In practical terms, GOS is interchangeable with gold vermeil - both are silver pieces with a gold coating.

Resale Value of Gold Over Silver

At a gold buyer, GOS pieces are valued for their silver content - not the gold layer. The gold coating is too thin to have meaningful gold recovery value.

For a 10g GOS piece:
• Silver value (92.5% = 9.25g fine silver) at ~₹75/g = approximately ₹694
• Gold layer: negligible

Compare this to a 10g solid 22K piece which is worth ₹1,39,690 - more than 100x the value of the GOS piece.

How to Distinguish GOS from Solid Gold

  • Stamp: GOS pieces are typically stamped 925 (sterling silver purity) alongside the GOS marking
  • Weight: silver is denser than gold per apparent volume for large pieces - but this is hard to judge visually
  • Magnet test: silver and gold are both non-magnetic, so this does not differentiate
  • XRF testing: the definitive test - shows silver core and thin gold layer immediately
  • Acid test: will show silver reaction at any exposed edge
  • Hallmark: solid gold pieces will have 916, 750, or 585 BIS stamps - GOS will have 925

Frequently Asked Questions

Is gold over silver real gold?

It has a real gold coating, but the core is sterling silver. It is not solid gold throughout - the gold layer is very thin.

What is GOS on jewellery?

GOS stands for Gold Over Silver - a sterling silver piece with a gold layer on the surface.

What is the resale value of gold over silver jewellery?

Essentially silver scrap value. The gold layer is too thin to recover economically at a standard gold buyer.

Is GOS the same as gold vermeil?

Yes - essentially. Both are sterling silver with a gold layer. GOS is the American term; vermeil is the French/European term.

How do I know if my piece is GOS or solid gold?

Look for the stamp: solid gold has 916, 750, or 585. GOS has 925 or GOS marking. XRF testing at the branch confirms definitively.

Does GOS jewellery tarnish?

The gold surface does not tarnish easily, but the silver base can tarnish at worn areas where the gold layer has thinned.

What Is Gold Vermeil? Meaning, Purity & Resale Value in India

Gold vermeil (pronounced 'ver-MAY') is a type of jewellery that is gaining popularity in India through online shopping and imported fashion accessories. It is often sold as a premium alternative to gold plating - but it is important to understand exactly what it is before assuming it has resale value like solid gold.

At a Glance

What is vermeil?Sterling silver (92.5%) base with thick gold plating (2.5+ microns)
Gold contentVery thin gold layer - silver is the main metal
Common karat14K or 18K gold plating over silver
Resale value at gold buyerSilver scrap value - not solid gold
Difference from solid goldCore is silver, not gold throughout
Difference from gold platedThicker gold + sterling silver base (not brass)
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Vermeil vs Gold Plated vs Solid Gold

TypeBase MetalGold LayerResale at Gold Buyer
Solid 22K GoldN/A - gold throughoutN/AFull IBJA rate
Gold VermeilSterling silver (92.5%)2.5+ microns (thick plating)Silver scrap value only
Gold PlatedBrass or copper0.05–0.5 micronsNil
Gold-FilledBrass5% of total weight by bondingVery low

What Vermeil Is Worth at Resale

Because the gold layer in vermeil is extremely thin (measured in microns), the actual gold content is negligible - less than 0.01g for most pieces. The valuable metal in vermeil is the silver base.

A 10g vermeil piece is essentially a 10g sterling silver piece with gold cosmetics:
• Silver value (92.5% = 9.25g fine silver): approximately ₹694 at current silver prices (~₹75/g)
• Gold layer: too thin to recover economically

At a gold buyer, vermeil is typically not purchased at the gold rate. If it is purchased at all, it is as silver scrap.

How to Identify Vermeil

  • Stamps: '925 Gold Vermeil', '925 14K' or just '925' (sterling silver hallmark) with a gold appearance
  • Lighter than solid gold of the same visual size
  • Often used in designer fashion jewellery, online marketplace jewellery
  • XRF testing at a branch will confirm: the silver core and thin gold layer are immediately distinguishable from solid gold
  • Common in imported jewellery from the US, Europe and some online platforms

Frequently Asked Questions

Is gold vermeil real gold?

It has a real gold coating but the base is sterling silver. It is not solid gold throughout.

What is the resale value of gold vermeil?

Minimal - only the sterling silver base has meaningful scrap value. The gold layer is too thin to recover economically.

How is vermeil different from gold plated?

Vermeil has a thicker gold layer (2.5+ microns vs 0.05 microns) and uses sterling silver as the base instead of brass.

What stamp does vermeil have?

Usually 925 (for sterling silver) with a gold appearance. Sometimes labeled 'Gold Vermeil' explicitly.

Is vermeil a good investment?

No - the resale value is essentially silver scrap. Vermeil is a fashion jewellery choice, not an investment.

How long does gold vermeil last?

2–5 years of daily wear before the gold layer shows wear through. Much longer if worn occasionally.

What Is Gold-Filled Jewellery? Purity, Durability & Resale Value in India

Gold-filled jewellery is one of the most confusing categories in the jewellery market. The name suggests solid gold - but it is not. It is a base metal (usually brass) bonded with a thick layer of gold alloy under heat and pressure.

If you have gold-filled pieces and are wondering what they are worth when you sell them, this guide gives you the honest answer.

At a Glance

What is gold-filled?Base metal bonded with a thick gold layer - not solid gold
Gold content5% of total weight by US FTC standards (1/20th gold)
Common stampsGF, 1/20 14K GF, 12K GF, 1/20 12K
Resale valueVery low - typically not accepted at gold buyer rates
Difference from gold platedThicker gold layer - more durable but still not solid
Difference from solid goldSolid gold is 100% gold alloy throughout
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Gold-Filled vs Gold Plated vs Solid Gold

TypeGold ContentDurabilityResale Value at Gold Buyer
Solid 22K gold91.6% throughoutLifetimeFull IBJA rate
Solid 18K gold75% throughoutLifetimeFull IBJA rate
Gold-filled~5% of total weight (gold layer only)5–30 yearsVery low - base metal dominates
Gold plated0.05–0.5% of weight1–5 yearsNil - gold layer negligible
Gold vermeil~5% (sterling silver base)5–20 yearsSilver scrap value only

Can You Sell Gold-Filled Jewellery at a Gold Buyer?

XRF testing immediately identifies gold-filled pieces - the gold layer is visible but the base metal underneath shows through. Because the gold content is only about 5% of the total weight, the gold value in a typical 10g gold-filled piece is only about 0.5g of gold - worth approximately ₹4,461 at 14K rates.

Most dedicated gold buyers either do not accept gold-filled pieces or pay only scrap rates. The payout is extremely low compared to solid gold of the same weight and appearance.

How to Identify Gold-Filled Jewellery

  • Look for the stamp: 'GF', '1/20 14K GF', '12K GF' or '1/20 12K' - these indicate gold-filled
  • Gold-filled is significantly heavier per piece than gold plated (base metal adds weight)
  • The gold layer on gold-filled is thick enough to survive XRF - it shows the gold layer clearly but the base metal underneath is also detected
  • If the piece has no hallmark, XRF testing will determine whether it is solid gold or gold-filled
  • Gold-filled pieces made in the USA often have GF stamps; European pieces may have different marking systems

What to Do If You Have Gold-Filled Pieces

  • XRF test it first - confirm whether it is gold-filled or solid gold (they can look identical)
  • If gold-filled: the resale value at a gold buyer will be minimal
  • Consider keeping it as wearable jewellery if it is in good condition
  • Some antique dealers value vintage gold-filled pieces for their aesthetics
  • Do not assume it is worthless - bring it for XRF testing and let the result determine the value

Frequently Asked Questions

Is gold-filled jewellery real gold?

It contains real gold - but only as a surface layer (about 5% of total weight). The core is brass or another base metal. It is not solid gold.

What is the resale value of gold-filled jewellery?

Very low. The gold content per gram is minimal. A 10g piece may yield only 0.3–0.5g of gold value.

How do I know if my jewellery is gold-filled?

Is gold-filled better than gold plated?

Yes - gold-filled has a much thicker gold layer (100x or more than gold plating) and is far more durable. But neither is solid gold.

What is the GF stamp on jewellery?

GF stands for Gold-Filled. A stamp like 1/20 14K GF means the gold layer is 14K gold and represents 1/20th (5%) of the total weight.

Does gold-filled jewellery tarnish?

The gold layer does not tarnish. However, at cut edges or worn areas, the base metal underneath may show through over time.

description: Gold has been used in dentistry for over a century - crowns, inlays, onlays and bridges are made from gold alloys because of their durability and biocompatibility. When a crown or…
html:
Selling Dental Gold in India: Crowns, Bridges & What They Are Worth

Gold has been used in dentistry for over a century - crowns, inlays, onlays and bridges are made from gold alloys because of their durability and biocompatibility. When a crown or bridge is removed during dental work, many people have no idea that the small metal piece has real cash value.

In India, dental gold can absolutely be sold to a gold bu

yer. Here is what it contains, how it is tested, and what you can realistically expect to receive.

At a Glance

Dental gold purity range10K – 18K (375–750) depending on type and era
Modern dental gold crownsOften 10K–14K - 40–60% gold
Older dental gold (pre-1990s)Sometimes higher purity (16K–18K)
Typical weight per crown1g – 3g per crown or inlay
Tested byXRF - same as jewellery
Cash value per crownApprox ₹8,921 – ₹34,312 depending on purity and weight
Last UpdatedMay 2026

What Is Dental Gold Made Of?

Dental gold is not 22K or 24K - it is an alloy designed for durability and biocompatibility. Common types:
• High-noble dental gold: 60%+ gold (≈14K–18K) + palladium, platinum - most valuable
• Noble dental gold: 25–60% gold (≈6K–14K) + silver, copper
• Base metal dental alloys: Less than 25% gold - some barely qualify
• Porcelain-fused-to-metal (PFM) crowns: Metal base may be very low gold or none at all

XRF testing immediately identifies the actual gold content.

How Much Is a Gold Crown Worth?

Crown TypeTypical WeightTypical PurityApproximate Value Today
High-noble gold crown2g – 3g14K – 18K (58–75%)₹17,842 – ₹34,312
Noble gold crown1.5g – 2.5g10K – 14K (40–58%)₹9,150 – ₹17,842
Gold inlay / onlay0.5g – 1.5g14K – 18K₹4,461 – ₹22,875
Old gold bridge (3 units)5g – 10g16K+ (historical)₹44,606 – ₹1,14,375
Porcelain-fused crown1g – 2gLow or no goldTest first - may be near zero

Palladium and Platinum in Dental Gold

High-noble dental alloys often contain palladium and sometimes platinum alongside gold. At a standard gold buyer, only gold content is typically valued - palladium and platinum are not separately extracted.

For very large quantities of high-noble dental gold, a specialist precious metals refiner may offer a better total return by assaying all precious metals separately. For individual crowns and bridges, this extra complexity is rarely worth it.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell old gold dental crowns in India?

How much is a gold crown worth?

Typically ₹8,921–₹34,312 depending on purity (10K–18K) and weight (1–3g per crown). XRF testing at the branch gives the exact figure.

How do I know if my crown is gold or porcelain?

Gold crowns are metallic - gold-coloured or silver/white metal. Porcelain or ceramic crowns are tooth-coloured. If unsure, XRF testing confirms immediately.

Do I need to clean dental gold before selling?

Remove visible residue. No polishing is needed - branch staff handle the rest.

What is the purity of dental gold?

Modern dental gold is typically 10K–18K. Older pieces (pre-1990) may be higher. XRF confirms the exact percentage.

Is palladium in dental gold paid for separately?

At a standard gold buyer, typically no - only gold content is paid. For large quantities, consider a specialist precious metals refiner.

Documents needed to sell dental gold?

Same as any gold sale: Aadhaar (mandatory) and PAN (if sale > ₹2,00,000).

Aadhaar is mandatory for selling gold - but what if your Aadhaar shows your hometown address while you are selling gold in a different city? What if your Aadhaar was not updated after you moved?

Common Address Mismatch Scenarios

What If You Do Not Have Aadhaar?

PAN Card - Address Not Relevant

Your PAN card address is also irrelevant to the gold sale. PAN is used only to link the transaction to your tax records. The printed address (often old) is not checked for current residence.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell gold if my Aadhaar has my old address?

Yes. The Aadhaar address is not verified against current residence for a gold sale.

I moved to a different city and my Aadhaar has my hometown - can I still sell?

This is extremely common. Bring your Aadhaar regardless of the address.

Do I need a separate address proof?

No. Aadhaar itself is the required document. A separate utility bill or rental agreement is not part of standard gold sale KYC.

Can I use a Driving Licence instead of Aadhaar?

What if I don't have my physical Aadhaar?

Use e-Aadhaar (downloaded from uidai.gov.in) or the mAadhaar app - both are officially valid.

Can I sell gold if I am visiting from another state?

Yes - no state-specific restriction. Aadhaar is a national ID, valid everywhere.

My Aadhaar is unreadable. What can I do?

Get a reprint from any UIDAI enrolment centre (fee: ₹30), or use the mAadhaar digital version on your smartphone.

html:
Old Jewellery Without a Hallmark: Can You Still Sell It & What Rate Do You Get?

BIS hallmarking became mandatory for Indian jewellers only from June 2021. This means most gold bought before 2021 - and virtually all gold bought before 2000 - is not BIS hallmarked.

Does this mean you get less for it when you sell? No - but the purity must be determined differently. Here is exactly how unhallmarked gold is valued and what to expect.

At a Glance

BIS mandatory hallmarking fromJune 2021 (14K, 18K, 22K jewellery)
Pre-2021 jewelleryNot hallmarked - but completely sellable
How purity is determinedXRF testing - same as any gold
Rate for unhallmarked 22K₹13,965/g - same as hallmarked 22K if XRF confirms
Does no hallmark reduce value?No - XRF result determines rate, not the stamp
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Why Most Old Indian Jewellery Has No BIS Hallmark

BIS hallmarking was introduced in 2000 but was voluntary until June 2021. This means:
• Jewellery bought before June 2021 - no BIS hallmark required by law
• Family heirlooms, ancestral pieces, jewellery from small local jewellers - likely no hallmark
• None of this makes the jewellery less valuable - purity simply needs independent verification.

How Unhallmarked Gold Is Valued at Resale

Why Older Jewellery May Test Below Expected Purity

  • Old KDM jewellery (pre-2000, cadmium soldering) may have slightly lower purity near solder joints
  • Some older jewellers sold jewellery at lower purity than claimed - without mandatory hallmarking, there was no verification
  • Pieces repaired or altered with lower-purity gold may test lower overall
  • Lac and resin filling inside hollow pieces affects weight but not the purity of the gold itself
  • Family heirlooms repaired over generations may be a mix of purities

Does No Hallmark Mean Lower Payment?

No - provided XRF confirms the expected purity. A 22K piece testing at 91.6% gets the same rate as a BIS-hallmarked 916 piece: ₹13,965/g.

The hallmark is a pre-verified purity certification. XRF at the branch does the same job - in real time, in front of you.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell gold without a BIS hallmark?

Will I get less money for unhallmarked gold?

No - if XRF confirms the expected purity, you receive the same rate as hallmarked gold of that purity.

How is purity determined for old unhallmarked jewellery?

XRF (X-ray fluorescence) testing - non-destructive, identifies exact gold content in 30–60 seconds.

What if the XRF shows lower purity than I expected?

You are paid at the tested purity. If the piece tests at 18K when you assumed 22K, the 18K rate applies.

Is KDM gold (old cadmium solder) affected?

XRF tests the gold body, not the solder joint. The gold portion of a KDM piece is paid at its actual purity.

Should I get my old gold tested before visiting?

Does old ancestral gold always test lower?

Not necessarily. Old South Indian hand-crafted jewellery is often genuinely 22K or close to it.

html:
How to Check the IBJA Gold Rate: Step-by-Step for First-Time Sellers

Every gold seller in India is told: 'Check the IBJA rate before you sell.' But for first-time sellers, ibja.co can be confusing - multiple rows, different purity levels, AM and PM columns, and rates that differ slightly from news apps.

This step-by-step guide shows you exactly how to read the IBJA rate table, which row applies to your gold, and how to convert the per-gram rate into what your specific piece is worth.

At a Glance

IBJA stands forIndia Bullion and Jewellers Association
Websiteibja.co
PublishedTwice daily - ~11:30 AM and ~5:00 PM (working days)
What it showsRate per 10g for multiple purities (995, 916, 750 etc.)
Convert to per gramDivide the shown rate by 10
Most relevant row for jewellery916 (22K) - Indian jewellery standard
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Step 1: Go to ibja.co

Open ibja.co in your browser - this is the official IBJA website. Alternatively, Moneycontrol or Economic Times publish the IBJA rate daily. For the authoritative source, ibja.co is primary.

Step 2: Find the Most Recent Rate Publication

The IBJA rate is published twice per working day:
• First publication: approximately 11:30 AM
• Second publication: approximately 5:00 PM

The website shows the date and time of the most recent publication. On weekends or holidays, the last published rate from the previous working day is displayed - this is the applicable rate.

Step 3: Read the Rate Table

The IBJA table shows rates per 10 grams for multiple purities. Key rows:

IBJA Purity RowKaratWhat It Applies ToPer 10g Rate TodayPer Gram Rate
99924KInvestment coins/bars₹1,52,500₹15,250
995~24KInstitutional bars₹1,51,738₹15,174
91622KMost Indian jewellery₹1,39,690₹13,969
87521KGulf-region gold₹1,33,438₹13,344
75018KDiamond jewellery₹1,14,375₹11,438
58514KLess common in India₹89,212₹8,921

Step 4: Calculate What Your Gold Is Worth

Formula: Weight (g) × IBJA per-gram rate for your purity

Examples with today's rates:
• 15g of 22K: 15 × ₹13,965 = ₹2,09,535
• 25g of 22K: 25 × ₹13,965 = ₹3,49,225
• 10g of 18K: 10 × ₹11,438 = ₹1,14,375
• 8g sovereign (22K): 8 × ₹13,965 = ₹1,11,752

This is the reference figure to walk in with. A reputable buyer offers within 1–2% of this.

Step 5: Verify the Buyer's Offer

  • Ask: 'What rate per gram are you paying for 22K today?' Today's IBJA: ₹13,965/g
  • Calculate the gap: if they offer ₹13,546/g, that is a 3% discount from IBJA - acceptable but on the high end
  • If they cannot state their rate in per-gram terms - or refuse to - that is a red flag
  • Ask to see the XRF reading after testing - confirm it matches what they are paying against

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the IBJA gold rate?

The IBJA (India Bullion and Jewellers Association) gold rate is India's national benchmark, published twice daily on working days.

How do I check today's gold rate?

Visit ibja.co or check Moneycontrol/Economic Times. For the official source, ibja.co is primary.

Why does my gold buyer quote below the IBJA rate?

Buyers pay slightly below IBJA (1–3%) to cover operating costs and margin. IBJA is the wholesale benchmark, not a retail buying rate.

Is the IBJA rate different for different cities?

No - one national rate applies everywhere.

Why does the IBJA show rates per 10 grams?

Historical convention - gold was quoted per 10g in India. Divide by 10 for the per-gram rate.

What does AM and PM rate mean on ibja.co?

IBJA publishes two rates per working day - morning (~11:30 AM) and evening (~5:00 PM). The more recent publication is current.

Can I use the IBJA rate to verify any gold buyer?

Yes - it is the standard benchmark all reputable buyers in India use as their pricing reference.

html:
How to Negotiate Making Charges with a Jeweller Before Buying Gold

Making charges typically add 8–25% to the cost of gold jewellery - and none of it is recovered when you sell. Reducing making charges at purchase is the single most impactful way to improve your gold investment's resale efficiency.

Can you actually negotiate making charges? Yes - in many cases, significantly. Here is how.

At a Glance

Making charges typical range8% – 25% of gold value
Most negotiableIndependent and local jewellers
Least negotiableLarge chains during peak festival seasons
Best time to negotiateOff-season, large purchases, cash payment
Maximum realistic saving3% – 10% reduction from quoted charges
Biggest leverBuying a larger quantity at once
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Step 1: Always Ask for Per-Gram Making Charges

Never ask 'what is your making charge?' in percentage terms - the answer is hard to verify. Ask: 'What is the making charge per gram on this specific piece?' This forces a concrete, comparable answer. Typical range: ₹150–800/g for hand-crafted pieces, ₹80–250/g for machine-made.

Step 2: Get Three Quotes First

Visit three jewellers before committing. Real competitor quotes are the most powerful negotiating tool: 'Jeweller B is offering this at ₹200/g making charges. Can you match or beat that?'

Step 3: Know When Jewellers Are Most Flexible

  • Off-season months (February–March, June–August) - lower footfall, more flexibility
  • Large purchases - ₹5L+ gives significant bargaining leverage
  • Slow-moving designs - pieces in display for months are more negotiable
  • Cash or UPI payment - eliminates the jeweller card fee (1.5–2%), which they may share with you
  • End of financial year (March) - jewellers clearing old stock
  • 6+ months advance for wedding orders - time and value both create leverage

Step 4: Separate Wastage from Making Charges

Some jewellers combine wastage (3–5%) with making charges (8–12%) - a combined quote hides the negotiable part. Ask: 'Can you show me the wastage and making charges separately?' Wastage is less negotiable (actual manufacturing loss); making charges have a profit component.

Step 5: What You Cannot Negotiate Away

  • GST on making charges (5%) - statutory, not the jeweller's to waive
  • BIS hallmarking cost - minor but fixed
  • The gold value itself (IBJA rate + buy premium) - market-set
  • Machine-made basics (chains, plain bangles) - often already at minimum 8–10%

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you negotiate making charges with Tanishq or Malabar?

Large chains have less flexibility during peak seasons. Off-season, for large purchases, some reduction is possible. Independent jewellers offer much more room.

How much can I realistically reduce making charges?

3–10% reduction from the initial quote is common for experienced negotiators on off-season purchases.

Is it rude to negotiate making charges?

Not at all. Gold is a major purchase in India - bargaining is expected and respected.

Does negotiating making charges affect gold quality?

No - making charges and gold purity are completely separate.

What is the minimum making charge on gold jewellery?

Machine-made plain jewellery can be as low as 6–8%. Handcrafted or designer pieces rarely go below 12–15%.

Can I negotiate for a wedding order?

Yes - wedding orders are large-value and planned well in advance. Place the order 3–6 months before the wedding and negotiate hard.

Should I ask for zero making charges?

Very rarely achievable. Some jewellers offer it as a promotional event, but the gold rate offered may be slightly adjusted. Always calculate the total cost.

html:
Sell Gold to a Jeweller vs a Gold Buyer: Who Pays More & Why

When you decide to sell gold, the two obvious options are: take it to the jeweller you bought it from, or visit a dedicated gold buying company. Most people assume the jeweller would give the best price back. In most cases, the opposite is true.

This guide explains exactly why dedicated gold buyers typically pay more than jewellers, and what to check to get the best rate either way.

Quick Comparison

Dedicated buyer typical rate1–2% below IBJA - closer to market
Jeweller typical buy-back rate3–8% below IBJA - wider margin
For cash paymentDedicated buyer almost always better
For exchange (old for new)Calculate the full equation - may depend on specific offer
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Side-by-Side Comparison

Rate offered1–2% below IBJA3–8% below IBJA typically
Cash paymentSame day - cash or bank transferOften exchange credit, not cash
Purity testingXRF - shown to you, preciseVariable
TransparencyRate shown, IBJA verifiableMay not explain calculation
Exchange optionNot applicable (buy-only)Available
Best forCash saleExchange for new jewellery (if maths work)

Why Jewellers Pay Less for Old Gold

  • Jewellers have two profit opportunities: buying your old gold cheap and selling new jewellery expensive
  • Their buying price is designed as a raw material cost for manufacturing - not market rate
  • A dedicated buyer's entire business model is buying gold - they compete on rate, so margins are smaller per gram but higher in volume
  • Jewellers who offer exchange may waive making charges - which seems like a benefit but often compensates for the below-market old gold rate

The Exchange Equation - When It Makes Sense

When to Choose Each Option

SituationBetter Choice
You need cash urgentlyDedicated gold buyer
You want to buy new jewellery from same jewellerCalculate exchange vs sell+buy separately
You have no specific plan for the moneyDedicated gold buyer
Jeweller offers full IBJA rate + making charges waivedExchange may be excellent value

The Bottom Line

Frequently Asked Questions

Who pays more for old gold - jeweller or gold buyer?

In most cases, a dedicated gold buyer pays closer to the IBJA market rate. Jewellers typically have wider margins.

Can I get cash from a jeweller?

Some jewellers pay cash. But they typically pay below market rate - a dedicated buyer pays cash at a better rate.

What is the typical rate difference?

Dedicated buyers: 1–2% below IBJA. Jewellers: 3–8% below. On a 20g piece, the difference can be ₹3,000–10,000.

Is the exchange offer from a jeweller worth it?

Sometimes - if the jeweller offers full market rate for old gold AND waives making charges. Often the old gold rate is below market, which offsets the making charge benefit.

Do jewellers test purity properly?

Reputable jewellers do. Practices vary. A dedicated buyer using XRF is more transparent - the reading is shown to you in real time.

Should I get multiple quotes before selling?

Yes - especially for large amounts. Compare per-gram rate offered, not just the headline.

Selling Gold to Pay Medical Bills: What to Know Before You Go

A medical emergency is one of the most common urgent reasons people sell gold in India. Hospital deposits, surgery fees and ongoing treatment costs can require large sums quickly - and gold at home is often the fastest source of liquidity available.

This guide tells you exactly what to do, how fast you can get cash, and what to bring.

At a Glance

Time to complete sale20–30 minutes at branch
Same-day cash?Yes - cash or bank transfer same visit
Documents neededAadhaar + PAN if > ₹2L
Hospital letter needed?No - not required at a gold buyer
Broken or mixed jewellery?Yes - condition does not affect rate
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Step 2: Gather Your Gold

Do not sort, clean or separate pieces - just bring all the gold you want to sell. Broken, bent, mixed pieces with stones - all accepted. Condition does not affect the rate.

Step 3: Bring Documents

Aadhaar card (mandatory - no exceptions).
PAN card if you expect the total sale to exceed ₹2,00,000. At today's 22K rate of ₹13,965/g, ₹2L corresponds to approximately 14.3g of 22K gold.

Step 4: At the Branch (20–30 Minutes)

Step 5: Which Gold Sells Fastest?

Gold TypeEstimated TimeNotes
Coins/biscuits10–15 minsFastest - no stones, no filling
Plain jewellery (chains, bangles)15–20 minsQuick - no stone removal
Stone-set jewellery20–30 minsStones removed before weighing
Temple/antique jewellery25–40 minsLac filling assessed

Tips to Get the Best Price

  • Cash payments above ₹2,00,000 must be via bank transfer (Section 269ST limit) - have bank account details ready
  • Bring all gold rather than pre-selecting - more gold means more cash
  • Keep the sale receipt safe - you will need it for ITR

Frequently Asked Questions

How quickly can I get cash by selling gold?

Do I need a hospital letter?

No - Aadhaar and PAN (if > ₹2L) are all that is required.

Can I sell broken or damaged gold in an emergency?

Yes - condition does not affect the rate.

Is it better to take a gold loan or sell gold for medical bills?

If repayment is uncertain, selling is safer - no interest burden. If recovery is expected and you want to reclaim the gold, a loan may suit.

What if I don't have PAN?

For sales under ₹2,00,000, only Aadhaar is needed.

Can someone else sell my gold for me?

Yes - a trusted family member can sell on your behalf. The receipt is in their name.

What is the maximum cash payment?

Cash payments above ₹2,00,000 must be bank transfer under Section 269ST. Have bank details ready for large amounts.

html:
Selling Gold Received as a Wedding Gift: Tax Rules & Documentation

In India, gold gifted at weddings is one of the most significant sources of gold ownership. Families gift sovereigns, jewellery sets, biscuits and coins - and the recipient may hold this gold for years before deciding to sell.

The key question when selling wedding gift gold: how is it taxed? The answer differs from gold you purchased - the donor's purchase price and date become the basis for your capital gains.

At a Glance

Gift tax on wedding gifts?No - gifts from relatives at marriage are tax-exempt
Capital gains when you sell?Yes - based on donor original price and purchase date
Holding periodIncludes the donor holding period before gifting
LTCG rate12.5% if total period ≥ 24 months
Cost basisDonor original purchase price
Documents at branchAadhaar + PAN if sale > ₹2L
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Is Wedding Gift Gold Taxable When Received?

Under Section 56(2)(x) of the Income Tax Act, gifts from specified relatives are tax-exempt regardless of value. Relatives include parents, siblings, in-laws, grandparents. Gold gifts received on the occasion of marriage are also exempt - even from non-relatives for the recipient's wedding. So: the gold received as a wedding gift is not taxable when you receive it.

Capital Gains When You Sell Wedding Gift Gold

Even though the gift is not taxable, selling it later triggers capital gains:
1. Cost of acquisition = the price the donor originally paid
2. Holding period = from when the donor originally bought the gold (not from when gifted to you)
3. If total period 24+ months → 12.5% LTCG on the gain

Example: Parents bought 50g in 2015 for ₹3,00,000. Gifted at your 2019 wedding. You sell today for ₹7,00,000.
Capital gain = ₹7,00,000 − ₹3,00,000 = ₹4,00,000
Holding period: 2015–2026 = 11 years → LTCG
Tax: ₹4,00,000 × 12.5% = ₹50,000

StepWhat It Means for Wedding Gift Gold
Cost basisDonor original purchase price - not market value at time of gift
Holding period startDate the donor originally bought the gold
24-month ruleAlmost always met for wedding gifts (donors buy years before gifting)
Tax rate12.5% LTCG (typically)
Where to find cost basisDonor original purchase receipt or jewellery bill

What If You Don't Have the Donor's Original Receipt?

  • For very old gold (pre-2001): use FMV on 1 April 2001 as cost basis
  • For gold where purchase year is known but not exact price: approximate rate from that year's records
  • A chartered accountant can help reconstruct a reasonable cost basis
  • Income tax department generally accepts reasonable estimates for old ancestral gold

Selling Process

  • Bring Aadhaar and PAN (if sale > ₹2L)
  • No wedding invitation, gift certificate or donor bill needed at the branch
  • Keep the sale receipt for ITR filing
  • Keep the donor's original purchase bill if you have it - needed for cost basis in ITR

Frequently Asked Questions

Is gold received as a wedding gift taxable?

When received, no - wedding gifts from relatives are exempt. When you sell it, capital gains apply based on the donor original price.

What is the capital gains rate on wedding gift gold?

12.5% LTCG if total holding period (including donor period) is 24+ months.

Do I need wedding records at the branch?

No - Aadhaar and PAN only. Wedding records are for your own tax filing.

What if I don't know the original price my parents paid?

Use FMV on 1 April 2001. A CA can help for more recent purchases.

Can I sell gold gifted by in-laws after marriage?

Yes. Gold gifts from in-laws at marriage are also exempt. Capital gains based on in-laws original purchase price.

What if the donor has passed away?

Same rules apply - use the deceased donor original price as cost basis. If unavailable, use FMV on 1 April 2001.

Do I need to report the wedding gift in my ITR?

Not when received - exempt. Only when sold do you report the capital gain under Schedule CG.

Gold Found at Home or in a Safe: How to Prove Ownership & Sell Legally

You open an old almira, a family safe or a bank locker and find undocumented gold - inherited from a grandparent, accumulated over decades, or simply forgotten. Can you sell it? Is it legal? Will the income tax department ask questions?

Yes - you can sell undocumented gold. But how you handle the paperwork matters.

At a Glance

CBDT exemption (undeclared gold)Married woman: 500g | Unmarried: 250g | Man: 100g
Within limit - can you sell?Yes - no questions asked
Exceeds limit - can you sell?Yes - but have a source explanation ready
Documents needed at branchAadhaar + PAN if > ₹2L sale
Income tax implicationDeclare source if queried - family inheritance acceptable
Last UpdatedMay 2026

How Much Undeclared Gold Is Allowed?

CBDT guidelines provide exemption limits for household gold that cannot be seized during an income tax search:
• Married woman: up to 500 grams
• Unmarried woman: up to 250 grams
• Male (married or unmarried): up to 100 grams

Within these limits, no documentation is needed. Amounts above these limits are not automatically illegal - but may attract questions about the source.

What If the Gold Exceeds the CBDT Limits?

Excess gold is not automatically a crime. However, if queried by an income tax officer:
• Acceptable explanations: family inheritance, gifts over many years, agricultural income, pre-KYC era purchases
• If you cannot explain the source: may be treated as unexplained income, taxed at 60%+ under Section 69

For most families selling ancestral jewellery: the amount is typically within limits, and a reasonable family inheritance narrative is generally accepted.

Capital Gains on Old Found Gold

If purchase date and price unknown:
• Use FMV on 1 April 2001 as cost basis
• Holding period assumed 24+ months (if any reasonable evidence of age exists)
• 12.5% LTCG applies on the gain

A chartered accountant can help determine the appropriate tax treatment.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell gold found at home without a bill?

Yes. Aadhaar and PAN (if applicable) are sufficient. No purchase bill needed.

How much gold can I legally keep at home without documents?

CBDT: married women 500g, unmarried women 250g, men 100g.

What if my gold exceeds the CBDT limits?

You can still sell it, but have a credible source explanation ready if queried.

Does selling found gold make it declared income?

Yes - sale proceeds go to your bank account and are part of your income for that year.

What documents help prove the source of old gold?

Family photos, old purchase receipts, wills/inheritance documents, gift letters.

Is keeping found gold illegal?

Not if within CBDT limits or with a reasonable source explanation. It is a declaration/tax compliance issue, not a possession crime.

Can income tax seize gold I've already sold?

No - once gold is sold at a licensed buyer and proceeds are in your bank account, the transaction is complete and declared.

html:
Can a Minor Sell Gold? Legal Age, Guardian Rules & What to Bring

Gold is frequently gifted to children in India - at birth, naming ceremonies, religious occasions and school milestones. By adulthood, a child may hold significant gold from family gifts.

Can a minor (under 18) sell gold themselves? And if a parent sells on behalf of a minor, what are the rules?

At a Glance

Legal age to contract in India18 years
Can a minor sell gold alone?No - contract with minor is void under Indian law
Who can sell for a minor?Natural guardian (parent) or court-appointed guardian
Documents neededGuardian Aadhaar + minor birth certificate or school ID
Tax on minor gold sale?Clubbed with guardian income under Section 64(1A)
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Legal Position: Minors Cannot Enter Contracts

Under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a contract with a minor is void ab initio. Selling gold is a contract - therefore a person under 18 cannot legally sell gold on their own. The natural guardian (parent or legal guardian) must conduct the sale on the minor's behalf. The gold buyer records the guardian's Aadhaar - not the minor's.

Process: Selling Gold Owned by a Minor

  1. Natural guardian (parent) brings the minor's gold to the branch
  2. Guardian presents their own Aadhaar card
  3. Guardian presents PAN if sale > ₹2,00,000
  4. Minor's birth certificate or school ID may be asked to confirm relationship
  5. Receipt is issued in the guardian's name as legal representative
  6. Proceeds belong to the minor - guardian holds them in trust
  7. Capital gain is reported in the guardian's ITR (clubbed with their income)

Tax Treatment: Minor Gold Sale

Under Section 64(1A) of the Income Tax Act, a minor's income is clubbed with the parent with higher income. This applies to capital gains from selling the minor's gold:
• Capital gain added to the higher-earning parent's taxable income
• Parent may claim ₹1,500/minor/year exemption
• Holding period uses the original gift date

When a Minor Turns 18

At 18, they can independently sell their gold. They will need their own Aadhaar and PAN (if sale > ₹2L). The transaction proceeds like any adult seller's.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can a 16-year-old sell gold?

No - under 18 cannot legally enter a sale contract. The natural guardian must sell on their behalf.

What documents are needed to sell a minor's gold?

Guardian's Aadhaar and PAN (if applicable). Minor's birth certificate or school ID may be requested.

Who receives the money when a minor's gold is sold?

Legally, the proceeds belong to the minor. The guardian holds them in trust for the minor's benefit.

Is the capital gain on a minor's gold sale taxable?

Yes - clubbed with the higher-earning parent's income under Section 64(1A).

Can grandparents sell gold gifted to a minor grandchild?

Only if they are the court-appointed or natural guardian of the minor.

When can a child sell their own gold independently?

From age 18 - once legally an adult and able to enter contracts.

Can a minor have a PAN card?

Yes - applied through the guardian. But for gold sales, the guardian's PAN is typically used.

html:
Joint Gold Ownership: Who Needs to Sign When Selling?

Gold in India is frequently owned jointly - by spouses, parents and children, or siblings. When selling jointly held gold, questions arise: does both parties' consent need to be recorded? Who signs the receipt? What if one owner is abroad?

The answer depends on how the gold is held - physically at home, in a joint bank locker, or as a financial instrument.

At a Glance

Gold kept physically at homePerson physically selling it signs the receipt
Joint bank locker goldBank protocols apply - often both holders needed to remove
Gold in joint dematDemat instructions usually require joint consent
Tax implicationsEach owner reports their share of capital gain
One owner abroad?Power of attorney or physical presence options
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Scenario 1: Gold Physically Kept at Home

For gold jewellery, coins or biscuits kept at home, the person who brings the gold to the branch and provides their Aadhaar is the seller on the receipt. A gold buyer does not verify joint ownership of physical gold - the legal division of proceeds between owners is between the parties, not the buyer.

Scenario 2: Gold in a Joint Bank Locker

Most banks require both locker holders present to open a joint locker, unless an 'either or survivor' clause was set up at the time of opening. If one holder is deceased, the bank requires a death certificate and succession documents per their policy.

Once the gold is physically removed from the locker, the gold buyer transaction is standard - Aadhaar + PAN.

Scenario 3: One Owner Is Abroad or Unavailable

  • Power of Attorney (POA): the absent owner can give a registered POA authorising the present owner to act for the gold sale
  • For physical gold at home: the person present can sell it - but the absent owner retains legal rights to their share of proceeds
  • For locker gold: the bank's rules govern access - check with your specific bank
  • If the absent person does not consent: do not sell their portion of jointly owned gold without consent

Tax: How Joint Gold Capital Gains Are Reported

If both owners are on record as holding the gold, each owner reports their proportionate share of the capital gain in their respective ITR. If only one owner's Aadhaar is on the receipt, that owner reports the full capital gain in their ITR and transfers the other party's share separately.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does my spouse need to come to the branch when I sell our gold?

For physical gold at home, no. For joint bank locker gold, your bank's procedures govern.

Can I sell gold from a joint locker alone?

Only if your locker agreement has an 'either or survivor' clause. Check with your bank.

Who pays capital gains tax on jointly held gold?

Each owner reports their share proportionally. If only one person's name is on the receipt, that person reports the full gain.

What if my co-owner is deceased?

For physical gold, the living owner can sell with standard documents. For locker gold, bank requires death certificate and succession documentation.

Can I use a Power of Attorney to sell on behalf of a joint owner?

Yes - a registered POA authorising the gold sale can be used.

What if joint owners disagree on whether to sell?

A gold buyer cannot adjudicate ownership disputes. Both owners need to agree before selling.

Is the sale receipt in one name or both?

In the name of the person presenting their Aadhaar at the branch.

How to Store Gold at Home Safely: Best Practices & Risks

Most Indian families keep gold at home - in jewellery boxes, hidden in cupboards, or in small home safes. While this is common and legal within limits, there are real risks: theft, fire damage, and family disputes.

This guide covers the best practices for storing gold at home, how much is considered safe to keep, and when a bank locker makes more sense.

At a Glance

CBDT limit for undeclared goldMarried woman: 500g | Unmarried: 250g | Male: 100g
Beyond these limitsExplainable with source documentation - not illegal
Home theft riskHigh - gold is a prime target; proper concealment is critical
Fire riskGold survives fire - but melting damages hallmarks
Bank locker cost₹1,500–₹6,000/year depending on bank and locker size
Insurance for home gold?Some home insurance policies cover gold - check your policy
Last UpdatedMay 2026

Home Storage Options Compared

Storage MethodSecurity LevelCostNotes
Jewellery box / drawerVery low - accessible to burglarsNilNot recommended for high-value gold
Home safe (wall-mounted)Medium - deters casual burglars₹10,000–₹50,000Heavy, anchor to wall or floor
Fireproof safeMedium - fire + some theft protection₹15,000–₹1,00,000Best for home storage of bars/coins
Bank lockerHigh - bank-grade security₹1,500–₹6,000/yearBest for large holdings
Hidden locationVariable - effective if truly secretNilRisk of forgetting or inaccessible in emergency

Best Practices for Storing Gold at Home

  • Never tell more people than necessary where your gold is kept
  • Use a heavy-duty safe bolted to the wall or floor - unsecured safes can be carried away
  • Do not store all your gold in one location - split between two or more secure spots
  • Keep an inventory (list of pieces, weights, approximate values) in a separate secure location
  • Photograph your jewellery for insurance purposes before storing
  • Check your home insurance policy - some cover gold up to a limit (typically ₹50,000–₹2,00,000)
  • Consider a bank locker for high-value items (over ₹5 lakh total)

Bank Locker vs Home: When to Switch

SituationRecommendation
Gold value under ₹2 lakhHome storage with a good safe is acceptable
Gold value ₹2–5 lakhConsider locker for bars/coins; home for jewellery
Gold value above ₹5 lakhBank locker strongly recommended
Planning to be away from home for 3+ monthsBank locker while travelling
Living in a high-crime areaBank locker regardless of value
Ancestral/heirloom gold of irreplaceable valueBank locker - monetary value not the only concern

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it legal to keep gold at home in India?

Yes - within the CBDT limits (500g for married women, 250g unmarried women, 100g for men) without documentation. Above these limits, you should have a source explanation.

How do I keep gold safe at home?

Use a heavy-duty safe bolted to the wall, split storage between locations, limit who knows about it, and document/photograph pieces for insurance.

Does home insurance cover gold?

Some policies do - check your specific policy. Many cover gold up to a limit (often ₹50,000–₹2,00,000). Standalone jewellery insurance is also available.

Should I use a bank locker for gold?

For holdings above ₹2–5 lakh, a bank locker provides significantly better security at a low annual cost.

What happens if home gold is stolen?

File a police complaint immediately. Claim from home insurance if covered. The CBDT documentation (receipts, photographs) helps with insurance claims.

Does gold melt in a house fire?

Gold melts at 1,064°C - most house fires do not reach this temperature. However, hallmarks may be damaged, affecting the purity verification. Fireproof safes protect best.

How much gold can I legally keep without documents?

CBDT guidelines: 500g (married women), 250g (unmarried women), 100g (men). These are exemption limits for IT searches, not ownership caps.

Gold Price per Ratti: What Is a Ratti & How to Convert to Grams

In parts of North and Central India, gold jewellery is still quoted and weighed in rattis - a traditional unit inherited from the pre-metric system. If your jeweller quotes you a ring 'of 8 rattis' or a nose pin 'of 1.5 rattis', you need to know how to convert this to grams to verify the price.

This guide explains what a ratti is, the conversion factor, and how to calculate today's gold price in rattis.

At a Glance

1 ratti equals0.1215 grams (approximately)
8 rattis equals0.972 grams (approximately)
1 ratti of 22K gold today₹1,697
8 rattis of 22K gold today₹13,574
10 rattis of 22K gold today₹16,967
Standard used by IBJAGrams - always convert from rattis to grams for IBJA rate
Last UpdatedMay 2026

What Is a Ratti?

A ratti is a traditional Indian unit of weight originally based on the weight of a ratti (gunja) seed - the red and black seed of the Abrus precatorius plant. It was used across India for weighing gold, gemstones and medicines before metric standardisation.

1 ratti = 0.1215 grams (the commonly used conversion in modern practice)

Note: regional variations exist - some markets use 0.121g, others 0.1215g. For practical purposes, 0.1215g is the standard.

161.944g₹27,148₹29,646

How to Calculate Gold Value in Rattis

Is Ratti Still Used in India?

  • Ratti is still used informally in some jewellery markets in Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Gujarat
  • For selling at a certified gold buyer: grams is the official unit - your gold will be weighed in grams on a precision scale
  • The IBJA publishes rates in rupees per gram - not per ratti
  • If a jeweller quotes you a price per ratti, always convert to grams to verify against the IBJA rate

Frequently Asked Questions

What is 1 ratti in grams?

1 ratti = 0.1215 grams (the commonly used standard conversion).

What is 1 ratti of gold worth today?

1 ratti of 22K gold = ₹1,697. 1 ratti of 24K gold = ₹1,853.

How many rattis in 1 gram of gold?

Approximately 8.23 rattis in 1 gram (1 ÷ 0.1215 = 8.23).

Is ratti still used at gold buyers?

No - certified gold buyers weigh in grams on precision digital scales. Ratti is a traditional reference unit only.

How do I convert my ratti-weight jewellery to grams?

Multiply the ratti weight by 0.1215. For example, 10 rattis = 10 × 0.1215 = 1.215 grams.

Does ratti weight affect the selling rate per gram?

No - you are paid the per-gram IBJA rate on the actual gram weight shown on the scale.

Is ratti the same as ratti in gemstones?

The ratti unit is the same seed-based weight historically, but gemstone rattis may use slightly different conversions in practice.

This is a personal financial decision. Gold has historically provided better long-term value in India, but silver has some uses where gold does not. Consult a financial advisor for investment decisions.
