Why Are There Different Gold Weight Units?

Different units emerged from different trading traditions. The gram became the international standard. Pavan (8g) is the South Indian conventional unit – widely used in Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh for pricing jewellery. Tola (11.6638g) is the traditional North Indian and Pakistani unit still used in the Gulf gold market.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many grams in 1 pavan of gold?

1 pavan = 1 sovereign = 1 savaran = 8 grams.

How many grams in 1 tola of gold?

1 tola = 11.6638 grams exactly.

How do I convert tola to grams?

Multiply tolas by 11.6638. Example: 5 tolas = 5 × 11.6638 = 58.319 grams.

How do I convert pavans to grams?

Multiply pavans by 8. Example: 10 pavans = 10 × 8 = 80 grams.

What is the 22K gold rate per pavan today?

1 pavan = 8g. At today’s 22K rate of ₹13,965/g: ₹1,11,752 per pavan.

What is the 22K gold rate per tola today?

1 tola = 11.6638g. At today’s 22K rate: ₹1,62,932 per tola.

Difference Between 18K and 22K Gold: Complete Comparison

18K and 22K gold are the two most common gold purities in Indian jewellery. 22K dominates traditional Indian jewellery (necklaces, bangles, chains), while 18K is standard for diamond and gemstone jewellery. Understanding the difference helps you know what you have and what to expect when selling.

Note: we published a 22K vs 24K comparison separately. This page focuses specifically on the 18K vs 22K comparison.

Why 18K Is Used for Diamond Jewellery

18K gold is harder and more durable than 22K because it has more alloy content (25% copper/silver/zinc vs 8.4% in 22K). This extra hardness is important for prong settings that hold diamonds and gemstones in place – a 22K prong would be too soft and could bend, releasing the stone. This is why engagement rings, diamond pendants, and most stone-set jewellery globally uses 18K (or 14K) gold rather than 22K.

Why 22K Is Used for Traditional Indian Jewellery

Traditional Indian jewellery (necklaces, bangles, haram) prioritises gold content and colour over extreme durability. 22K’s higher purity gives a richer, warmer yellow colour and is seen as more prestigious for gifting and dowry. Most Indian jewellery sold by traditional jewellers (from Tanishq to local goldsmiths) is 22K hallmarked.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between 18K and 22K gold?

22K has 91.6% gold (harder yellow, softer metal, used in traditional Indian jewellery). 18K has 75% gold (slightly paler, harder metal, used for diamond/stone-set jewellery).

Which is more expensive, 18K or 22K gold?

22K is more expensive per gram: ₹13,965/g vs 18K at ₹11,438/g – a difference of ₹2,527 per gram.

Is 22K better than 18K for resale?

22K gives a higher per-gram payout because it has more gold content. But the total value depends on the weight of each piece, not just the karat.

Which gold should I sell first – 18K or 22K?

There is no rule. Both can be sold whenever needed. 22K gives a higher rate per gram; 18K gives less per gram but is still fully valued at its correct purity rate.

How do I know if my ring is 18K or 22K?

Do most Indian necklaces come in 18K or 22K?

Most traditional Indian necklaces are 22K. Modern necklaces designed to hold diamonds may be 18K.

Gold Rate History in India: How Prices Have Moved Over Time

Understanding how gold prices have moved historically helps sellers set realistic expectations and make informed decisions about when to sell. India’s gold price history is shaped by a combination of global commodity markets, the US dollar, and domestic demand cycles.

This guide covers the major price movements in Indian gold rates, what drove each shift and what the historical pattern suggests for sellers today.

At a Glance

What Drives Gold Prices in India?

·         International gold price (USD/troy oz) – the primary driver

·         USD-INR exchange rate – a weaker rupee pushes Indian gold prices higher

·         US Federal Reserve interest rates – lower rates support gold

·         Geopolitical events – wars, crises, uncertainty boost gold demand

·         Indian seasonal demand (Diwali, Dhanteras, wedding season) – minor upward influence

·         RBI and government import duties – affect domestic prices independently of global prices

What Gold Rate History Tells Sellers

The long-term trend is clearly upward – gold in India has roughly doubled every 5–7 years over the past two decades. This means waiting often rewards patience, but the timing of peaks is genuinely unpredictable. The 2020 COVID spike showed how quickly gold can surge 40%+ in months, then correct. Sellers who needed funds and sold in 2019 at ₹3,400/g still received fair value for their era; those who waited and sold in 2026 at ₹13,965/g received significantly more. Practical guidance: if you need cash and the current rate is strong relative to recent years, selling now is rational. Waiting for a further peak carries the risk of a correction.

Frequently Asked Questions

What was gold price in India 5 years ago?

In 2021, 22K gold was approximately ₹4,500–₹5,200/g. Today (May 2026) it is ₹13,965/g – a significant increase.

Has gold price always gone up in India?

Not in every year, but the 10–20 year trend is strongly upward. There have been correction periods (2012–2015, post-2020) but the long-term direction is up.

What was the highest gold price in India ever?

As of May 2026, current levels are at or near all-time highs for 22K gold in India.

Does the gold rate change every day in India?

Yes. The IBJA (Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association) publishes the benchmark rate every trading day, based on international gold prices and the USD-INR rate.

Will gold rate go up or down in the future?

This cannot be predicted reliably. Gold is driven by global factors (USD, geopolitics, central bank policy) that are genuinely uncertain.

When was gold cheapest in the last 10 years?

Approximately 2014–2016, when 22K gold was around ₹2,400–₹2,700/g.

Is it better to sell gold now or wait?

If the rate is at a historically strong level and you have a need to sell, selling now is rational. Market timing is very difficult even for professionals.

Gold Hallmark Types in India: BIS, HUID, KDM & Older Marks Explained

A gold hallmark is an official mark stamped on gold jewellery confirming its purity has been tested and certified. In India, hallmarks are governed by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). Understanding the different hallmark types helps you know what you have before selling.

This guide covers every hallmark type found on Indian gold jewellery and what each means for resale.

At a Glance

Current standard (2021–)

BIS 6-symbol mark with HUID

Old BIS mark (pre-2021)

BIS mark without HUID

KDM mark

Old mark for 916 solder-joined jewellery

Fineness code

999/916/750/585 – purity in parts per thousand

How to verify

BIS Care app (free, Android/iOS)

Last Updated

May 2026

The 6 Official BIS Hallmark Symbols (Current Standard)

Symbol

What It Means

BIS Logo (triangle with letters)

Confirms BIS certification

Fineness/Purity Mark

999=24K, 916=22K, 750=18K, 585=14K, 375=9K

Assaying & Hallmarking Centre (AHC) ID

Code of the testing lab

Jeweller’s ID Mark

Registered jeweller who made/sold the piece

Year of Hallmarking (letter code)

Year the piece was certified

HUID (6-digit alphanumeric)

Unique ID for that specific piece (post-June 2021)

What Is a HUID?

HUID (Hallmark Unique ID) is a 6-digit alphanumeric code mandated since June 2021. Each piece of gold jewellery sold in India must now have a unique HUID registered in the BIS database. You can verify any HUID using the free BIS Care mobile app.

What Is the KDM Hallmark?

KDM stands for cadmium – an older soldering material used in Indian goldsmithing. A KDM hallmark on jewellery indicates it was made using a cadmium-based solder, typically in the 22K (916) class. KDM marking is now banned in India (cadmium is toxic), but older jewellery with KDM marks still exists and can be sold freely at the standard gold rate.

Older BIS Hallmarks (Pre-2021, Without HUID)

What If My Gold Has No Hallmark?

Does Hallmark Type Affect Resale Price?

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the different types of gold hallmarks in India?

Current: 6-symbol BIS mark with HUID. Old: BIS mark without HUID. KDM: older cadmium-solder mark. Older pieces: international fineness marks only.

What does 916 mean on gold?

916 is the BIS fineness code for 22-karat gold – it contains 916 parts gold per 1,000 (91.6% pure gold).

What is the difference between a BIS hallmark and a HUID?

BIS hallmark is the full certification system. HUID (Hallmark Unique ID) is the 6-digit code added since June 2021 to make each piece uniquely traceable.

Is KDM gold safe to sell?

Yes. KDM-marked gold is accepted by all reputable gold buyers. The KDM mark indicates an older soldering method, not a purity issue.

Does my gold need a hallmark to be sold?

How do I verify a HUID hallmark?

Use the free BIS Care app (Android/iOS). Enter the 6-digit HUID code to verify purity and certification details.

Does having a HUID get me a better price?

No. The price is based on XRF-tested purity, not the hallmark type.

html:
How to Get Best Price for Gold: 7 Tips Before You Sell

Getting the best price for your gold isn’t about negotiating — it’s about knowing what you should receive and ensuring nothing is unfairly deducted. Gold is a commodity valued at the daily IBJA rate; the price is transparent and calculable. What varies between buyers is how honestly they apply that rate.

These 7 tips help you walk into any gold buying transaction fully prepared.

At a Glance

Key number to know

Today’s IBJA 22K rate per gram

Key formula

Weight × Purity Fraction × 24K Rate

Non-negotiable deductions

Stones, lac, non-gold elements only

Illegal deductions

Making charges, handling fees, arbitrary cuts

Best protection

Know the rate before you walk in

Last Updated

May 2026

Tip 1: Know the Live IBJA Rate Before You Go

The IBJA (Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association) publishes the gold rate each trading day. Check it before visiting any buyer. This is your benchmark — the maximum you can receive per gram for each purity level.22K rate today: ₹13,965/g. 24K rate today: ₹15,250/g.

Tip 2: Calculate Your Expected Payout Before Visiting

Tip 3: Insist on XRF Testing (Not Just Visual/Acid)

XRF (X-ray fluorescence) is the most accurate purity test — accurate to ±0.1%

Acid tests and visual estimates are less accurate and can understate purity

If a buyer refuses XRF or charges for testing, that is a red flag

Tip 4: Know What CAN and CANNOT Be Deducted

Item

Deductible?

Notes

Non-gold stones (diamonds, rubies, etc.)

Yes — excluded from weight

Stones returned to you

Lac or wax filling

Yes — excluded from weight

Filling returned

Making charges paid at purchase

No — NOT deductible at resale

Illegal to deduct

Handling or processing fees

No — NOT deductible

No legitimate buyer charges this

Wastage charges

No — NOT deductible

Only applicable when buying new jewellery

Tip 5: Get a Written Receipt

A signed receipt is a legal requirement in India for gold transactions. It should state: weight, purity, rate per gram, total amount paid and your KYC details. Refuse to sell to any buyer who will not issue a receipt.

Tip 6: Bring Your KYC Ready

Aadhaar is mandatory for all gold sales. PAN is required if your total sale exceeds ₹2,00,000. Having these ready speeds up the process and avoids any delay at the branch.

Tip 7: Choose a Regulated, Reputable Buyer

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I get the best price for my gold?

Check the live IBJA rate first, calculate your expected payout, insist on XRF testing, and choose a reputable buyer who does not make arbitrary deductions.

Are making charges deducted when selling gold?

No. Making charges are paid when buying new jewellery and are not recoverable at resale. No legitimate gold buyer deducts making charges.

What is the IBJA rate?

IBJA (Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association) publishes the daily benchmark gold price. Today’s 22K rate is ₹13,965/g.

Should I get multiple quotes before selling?

Yes, especially for large quantities. The IBJA rate is the benchmark; compare how closely different buyers offer this rate.

Can I negotiate the gold buying rate?

The per-gram rate is based on IBJA — there is little room to negotiate the rate itself. The protection is ensuring no unfair deductions and using XRF testing.

What documents should I bring to sell gold?

Aadhaar card (mandatory). PAN card (if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000).

Is XRF testing free?

Selling Gold Online in India: Is It Safe? Complete Guide

Several platforms offer to buy gold online in India — you send your jewellery by courier and receive payment digitally. While convenient, online gold selling carries significant risks compared to selling at a reputable physical buyer.

This guide explains how online gold selling works, what the risks are and how it compares to visiting a branch.

At a Glance

Online gold buying — legitimate?

Some platforms are legitimate; many are not

Main risk

Gold in transit, value disputes, delayed payment

Physical buyer advantage

Instant rate, immediate payment, XRF on the spot

Regulated by

No specific regulator for gold buying in India

Last Updated

May 2026

How Online Gold Selling Works

Online gold buyers typically follow this process: you request a quote online, they send you a courier kit, you pack and ship your gold, they receive and test it, then offer a price. If you accept, they transfer payment to your bank account.

The quote given online is usually preliminary — the actual offer may differ after they test the purity and weight at their facility.

Gold in transit risk — if the courier is lost or damaged, the insurance claim process is complex and may not cover full market value

Price dispute after receipt — online buyers may claim lower purity or weight than expected, and you cannot be present during testing

Delayed payment — some platforms take several days or weeks to process and pay

Difficulty returning gold — if you reject their offer, getting gold returned can be slow and costly

Unregulated space — no specific regulator governs gold buying in India; consumer protection is limited

Scam platforms — some fraudulent platforms collect gold and disappear; verifying legitimacy is difficult

Online vs Physical Gold Buyer — Comparison

Convenience

High — from home

Moderate — branch visit needed

Speed of payment

2–7 days typically

Same day — immediate

Purity testing

Done at their facility (not visible to you)

XRF at branch in front of you

Price dispute risk

High — you cannot witness testing

Low — you see the results live

Gold-in-transit risk

Yes — courier risk

None

Receipt issued

Digital (may not be reliable)

Signed physical receipt guaranteed

Rate offered

Often below IBJA (spread wider)

IBJA-based rate

How to Verify an Online Gold Buyer (If You Choose to Use One)

Check company registration on MCA21 portal (Ministry of Corporate Affairs)

Verify GST registration (legitimate businesses have GST numbers)

Look for physical address and phone number — test by calling

Read independent reviews (not testimonials on their own site)

Check insurance coverage explicitly — get it in writing before shipping

Start with a small piece to test the process before sending large quantities

Why a Physical Buyer Is Safer

Frequently Asked Questions

Is selling gold online in India safe?

Some platforms are legitimate, but the process carries significant risks: gold in transit, price disputes you cannot witness, and delayed payment. Physical buyers are safer and faster.

Which is better — selling gold online or at a branch?

Do online gold buyers offer better rates?

Generally no. Online buyers have higher operational costs (courier, logistics) and often offer below-IBJA rates. Physical buyers with low overhead can offer competitive IBJA-based rates.

What if I cannot travel to a branch?

Is there any government regulation of online gold buyers?

No specific regulator governs gold buying in India. This makes the online space riskier than regulated financial products.

What documents do I need to sell gold online?

Requirements vary by platform, but generally Aadhaar and PAN are needed. Physical buyers require the same KYC.

Can I be scammed when selling gold online?

Yes. Fraudulent platforms exist. Always verify company registration and physical address before shipping your gold to any online buyer.

Best Time to Sell Gold in India: When to Get Maximum Value

People often wonder whether to wait for a higher gold price before selling. While timing the gold market is genuinely difficult, there are predictable seasonal and cyclical patterns that can help sellers make more informed decisions.

This guide covers what drives gold prices in India, seasonal patterns and a practical rule of thumb for when to sell.

At a Glance

US dollar / international commodity markets

What Drives Gold Prices in India?

Gold prices in India are determined primarily by the international commodity price (USD per troy ounce) converted at the daily USD-INR exchange rate. The IBJA (Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association) publishes the benchmark rate each trading day.This means gold price changes in India are mostly driven by global factors: US Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, geopolitical events, global inflation and dollar strength/weakness. Indian seasonal demand (festivals, weddings) has a smaller but observable impact.

Seasonal Patterns in Indian Gold Prices

Period

Jul–Sep (Monsoon, Shraadh period)

Lowest jewellery buying

Prices may dip slightly

The Honest Answer: Timing Is Very Difficult

Gold price prediction is notoriously difficult — even professional analysts regularly get it wrong. The factors driving price (geopolitics, Fed decisions, currency movements) are genuinely unpredictable.The practical guidance most financial advisors give: if you have a reason to sell (need cash, want to reinvest, upgrading jewellery), sell when the rate is reasonable — don’t wait for a peak that may or may not come.

What You Can Control: Getting the Best Rate Today

Check the live IBJA rate before visiting any buyer — this is your benchmark

Visit during market hours (Mon–Fri, before 4 PM) when IBJA rate is confirmed for the day

Compare offers from multiple buyers if selling a large quantity

Sell all pieces at once rather than multiple small visits (no rate advantage to splitting, but saves time)

Avoid selling during economic disturbances when buyers may widen their spread

Does Selling During Festivals Give a Better Price?

Not usually. While gold buying demand peaks during Dhanteras and Akshaya Tritiya, gold buyers pay IBJA rates — they do not pay a ‘festival premium’ above the benchmark. The IBJA rate itself may be slightly higher during demand peaks, but the direct impact on your resale rate is marginal and unpredictable.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the best time to sell gold in India?

There is no reliably predictable “best time.” Gold prices move on global factors. Practically: sell when the IBJA rate is strong relative to recent months and you have a need to sell.

Is Dhanteras a good time to sell gold?

Demand during Dhanteras is high, which may support prices. However, gold buyers pay IBJA rates regardless of the festival. The IBJA rate itself may be marginally higher, but this is not guaranteed.

Does the gold rate change daily?

Yes. The IBJA publishes a new rate every trading day (Monday–Friday). Rates can move significantly based on overnight global market movements.

Should I wait for gold price to go up before selling?

Only if you can afford to wait and have no urgent need. Market timing is difficult; many sellers who waited for a higher price saw prices fall instead. Sell when the rate is acceptable and you have a reason to sell.

Is Akshaya Tritiya a good time to sell gold?

Akshaya Tritiya is traditionally auspicious for buying gold, which supports demand and may slightly elevate prices. However, buyers pay IBJA rates and the practical impact on your resale price is small.

Gold Filigree Jewellery: Weight, Today’s Rate & Resale Value

Filigree jewellery (called tarkashi in Hindi, or koftgari in some regions) is a delicate jewellery technique where thin gold wire is twisted and curled into intricate lacy patterns. Famous filigree-making centres in India include Karimnagar (Telangana), Cuttack (Odisha) and parts of Rajasthan.

At resale, filigree craftsmanship adds no premium. Only the gold weight and purity determine cash value. Because filigree uses very fine wire, pieces are typically lighter than solid gold jewellery of the same visual size.

For a 20g piece: ₹2,79,380. Important note: filigree uses very fine gold wire, which is accurately weighed on precision scales. The intricate craftsmanship is paid at the same per-gram rate as plain gold — not more, not less.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

Stones or lac weighed with gold — insist on removal before weighing

Visual purity check instead of XRF — always request machine testing

No written receipt — a signed receipt is a legal requirement

Making charge deductions at resale — these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is gold filigree jewellery worth today?

A 10g 22K filigree piece is worth ₹1,39,690. A 20g piece brings ₹2,79,380.

Does the intricate filigree craftsmanship add resale value?

No. Gold buyers pay only for the weight of gold wire and the purity. Filigree, tarkashi and koftgari craftsmanship add no premium at resale, regardless of their artistic value.

Is filigree jewellery lighter than solid gold?

Yes. Filigree uses thin twisted wire, so pieces look larger than their weight suggests. A 10g filigree necklace may appear as large as a 20g solid necklace.

Are stones embedded in filigree paid?

No. Stones are removed before weighing and returned to you.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. Most filigree pieces are below ₹2L PAN threshold.

What purity is filigree gold?

Most is 22K. Karimnagar filigree is typically 22K. XRF at the branch confirms.

How is very fine filigree wire weighed accurately?

On precision digital scales accurate to 0.01g. Even light filigree pieces are weighed precisely.

Yes. Pendant and chain are weighed separately if sold individually.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. Bar pendants are typically well below ₹2L PAN threshold.

Most are 18K or 22K. XRF confirms.

Can I sell a bent bar pendant?

Yes. Physical damage does not affect gold purity.

10–15 minutes.

Gold Kundan Jewellery: Weight, Today’s Rate & Resale Value

Kundan jewellery is a traditional Indian jewellery technique originating from Rajasthan, featuring uncut glass stones (kund) set in gold using a refined gold foil (kundankari) technique. Unlike polki (which uses real uncut diamonds), kundan uses high-quality glass to replicate the look of precious stones.

At resale, only the gold content is paid. Kundan glass stones have no resale value at a gold buyer and are excluded from the weight.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

Stones or lac weighed with gold – insist on removal before weighing

Visual purity check instead of XRF – always request machine testing

No written receipt – a signed receipt is a legal requirement

Making charge deductions at resale – these do not apply

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is gold kundan jewellery worth today?

Only the gold portion is paid. A 25g kundan necklace (gold only) is worth ₹3,49,225.

What is kundan jewellery?

Kundan is a traditional Rajasthani jewellery technique using uncut glass stones set in gold using a refined gold foil. The result resembles precious-stone jewellery but uses glass.

What is the difference between kundan and polki?

Kundan uses glass stones; polki uses real uncut natural diamonds. At a gold buyer, neither the kundan glass nor the polki diamonds add to the gold payout – but polki stones can be separately assessed by a diamond specialist.

Are the kundan glass stones paid at resale?

No. Kundan glass has no resale value. Only the gold setting and base are paid.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory. PAN required if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000 – most kundan sets exceed this.

What purity is kundan jewellery gold?

Traditional kundan uses 22K or 24K gold foil (kundankari). Most pieces are 22K. XRF confirms.

html:
Gold Hallmark Verification Online: How to Use the BIS Care App

Since 2021, BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) mandates that all gold jewellery sold in India carry a unique 6-digit HUID (Hallmark Unique ID). This allows any buyer or seller to verify the jewellery’s hallmark certification online through the official BIS Care mobile app.

This guide walks through verifying your gold‘s hallmark step by step before selling.

At a Glance

Verification app

BIS Care (official, free)

Available on

Android and iOS

HUID format

6-digit alphanumeric code

What it confirms

Purity, jeweller, hallmarking centre, date

Cost to verify

Free

Last Updated

May 2026

What Is HUID Hallmark Verification?

HUID (Hallmark Unique ID) is a 6-digit alphanumeric code engraved on BIS-hallmarked gold jewellery sold in India since June 2021. Each HUID is unique to that specific piece and is recorded in the BIS database along with details like purity, the assaying & hallmarking centre, and the jeweller.Verifying the HUID confirms the piece is genuinely BIS-certified at the stated purity – useful both when buying and before selling.

Step-by-Step: How to Verify Your Gold’s Hallmark

Download the official “BIS Care” app from Google Play Store or Apple App Store

Open the app and select “Verify HUID” or similar option from the menu

Locate the 6-digit HUID code engraved on your jewellery (usually near other hallmark symbols)

Enter the HUID code into the app

The app displays verification details: purity, hallmarking centre, and registration status

Cross-check the displayed purity matches what you expect (916 for 22K, etc.)

What the BIS Care App Shows You

Information Displayed

What It Means

Purity (Fineness)

Confirms 999/916/750/585 grading

Assaying & Hallmarking Centre (AHC)

Where the piece was tested and certified

Registration Status

Confirms the HUID is genuine and registered

Jeweller Details

Registered jeweller who sold the piece (where available)

What If My Gold Has No HUID?

Does Hallmark Verification Affect Resale Price?

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I verify my gold’s hallmark online?

Download the official BIS Care app (Android/iOS), enter your jewellery’s 6-digit HUID code, and the app displays purity and certification details.

What is a HUID number?

HUID (Hallmark Unique ID) is a unique 6-digit alphanumeric code assigned to each piece of BIS-hallmarked gold jewellery sold in India since June 2021.

Where do I find the HUID code on my jewellery?

It is engraved near other hallmark symbols, typically on the inside of rings/bangles or on a small tag/clasp for chains and necklaces.

What if my gold jewellery has no HUID?

This is normal for jewellery purchased before June 2021. It does not indicate lower quality – XRF testing at a gold buyer determines exact purity regardless.

Is the BIS Care app free?

Yes. It is the official free app from the Bureau of Indian Standards, available on Google Play Store and Apple App Store.

Can a hallmark be faked?

Counterfeit hallmarks exist, which is why XRF verification at the time of resale is important – it independently confirms actual purity rather than relying solely on stamped marks.

Difference Between 22K and 24K Gold: Complete Comparison

22K and 24K are the two most common gold purities discussed in India – 24K is pure gold, while 22K is gold alloyed with other metals for strength. Understanding the difference helps you make informed decisions whether buying, gifting or selling gold.

This guide compares purity, durability, colour, pricing and which is better suited for jewellery versus investment.

At a Glance

22K gold purity

916 – 91.6% pure gold

Purity: The Core Difference

24K gold is 99.9% pure – essentially as pure as gold can be refined. 22K gold is 91.6% pure, with the remaining 8.4% made up of alloying metals (typically copper, silver or zinc).The BIS hallmark codes reflect this: 24K carries the 999 mark; 22K carries the 916 mark.

Side-by-Side Comparison

22K Gold

91.6% (916)

Why Is 22K Used for Jewellery Instead of 24K?

Pure 24K gold is very soft – it bends and scratches easily, making it impractical for daily-wear jewellery like rings and bangles that endure friction and impact. Alloying gold with copper, silver or zinc (creating 22K) significantly increases hardness and durability while retaining a rich gold colour.This is why most traditional Indian jewellery – necklaces, bangles, earrings – is crafted in 22K gold, while 24K is reserved for coins, bars and certain ceremonial pieces.

Which Is Better for Resale?

24K gold technically has a higher per-gram resale rate (₹15,250 vs ₹13,965) since it has zero alloy content. However, this does not mean 24K jewellery is ‘better’ – it simply reflects purity.For a 10g piece: 24K = ₹1,52,500 vs 22K = ₹1,39,690. The ₹12,810 difference reflects the 8.4% non-gold content in 22K, not any quality judgment. Both are valued fairly at their true purity through XRF testing.

How to Tell Which Purity You Have

Check the BIS hallmark: look for 999 (24K) or 916 (22K) stamped on the piece

Visual colour alone is unreliable – always confirm with hallmark or XRF

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the price difference between 22K and 24K gold today?

24K is ₹15,250/g; 22K is ₹13,965/g – a difference of ₹1,285 per gram, reflecting 24K’s higher purity.

Is 24K gold better than 22K gold?

Neither is “better” – they serve different purposes. 24K is purer and better for investment (coins, bars). 22K is more durable and better suited for daily-wear jewellery.

Can jewellery be made from 24K gold?

Rarely, because 24K is too soft for jewellery that needs durability. Some ceremonial or investment-grade pieces use 24K, but most jewellery is 22K or lower.

How much more do I get selling 24K gold vs 22K?

For the same weight, 24K pays the full ₹15,250/g rate, while 22K pays ₹13,965/g (91.6% of the 24K rate). A 10g piece: 24K = ₹1,52,500, 22K = ₹1,39,690.

Is 22K gold considered “real” gold?

Yes. 22K (91.6% pure) is genuine, high-purity gold – it is simply alloyed with other metals for strength. Most fine jewellery worldwide uses 18K–22K, not 24K.

Selling Inherited Gold in India: Complete Legal Guide

Inherited gold — jewellery or coins received through a will or family succession — is one of the most common forms of gold that Indians sell. Many people are unsure of the legal requirements: Can you sell without the original purchase bill? What KYC is needed? What are the tax implications?

This guide answers all those questions clearly.

At a Glance

Can you sell inherited gold?

Yes — fully legal

Original purchase bill required?

No — not needed for sale

KYC required

Aadhaar (all) + PAN (if >₹2L)

Tax on sale

LTCG 12.5% if held >24 months

Purity determined by

XRF machine test at branch

Last Updated

May 2026

Is It Legal to Sell Inherited Gold?

Yes. Selling inherited gold is completely legal in India. Gold received through inheritance, a will (vasiyat) or family succession is your property and can be sold freely.

There is no restriction on selling inherited jewellery. The only requirements are standard KYC documents — the same as for any gold sale.

Documents Required to Sell Inherited Gold

Document

Required?

Notes

Aadhaar Card

Yes — mandatory for all gold sales

Prevention of Money Laundering Act

PAN Card

Yes — if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000

Income Tax Act Section 114B

Original purchase bill

No — not required

XRF determines purity instead

Will / succession certificate

Not required for sale

May help for tax cost-basis

Death certificate of original owner

Not required for sale

Not asked by gold buyer

What Happens Without the Original Bill

The original purchase bill is not needed to sell at a gold buyer. XRF machine testing determines the exact purity of the inherited gold piece in 30–60 seconds. You are paid the IBJA rate × weight × purity fraction — regardless of when the original owner bought it or at what price.

However, without the original purchase bill, you may not be able to prove the cost of acquisition to the Income Tax Department for LTCG purposes.

Tax on Selling Inherited Gold

Inherited gold is subject to Capital Gains Tax when sold:

• Long-Term Capital Gain (LTCG): If the original owner held the gold for more than 24 months before death AND you (as heir) have held it for any period after inheritance, the combined holding period applies. LTCG rate: 12.5% (without indexation, post Budget 2024).

• Short-Term Capital Gain: If total holding period is under 24 months, the gain is added to your income slab.

• Cost of acquisition: For inherited gold, the cost basis is the fair market value on the date of inheritance (not the original purchase price). If you have a valuation certificate from the date of inheritance, this helps.

Consult a tax advisor for your specific situation.

Special Situations

Multiple heirs: If the gold is shared among heirs, each person’s share can be sold by them individually with their own KYC.

Gold received before hallmarking era: No hallmark is fine — XRF tests regardless.

Very old/antique inherited gold: Age and antique value add no premium at a gold buyer. Only the gold content is paid.

Selling on behalf of an elderly heir: The heir must be present with their own Aadhaar.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell inherited gold without the original bill?

Yes. No original purchase bill is needed. XRF testing determines purity and you are paid the IBJA rate by weight.

What documents do I need to sell inherited gold?

Aadhaar card (mandatory for all). PAN card (mandatory if sale exceeds ₹2,00,000).

Do I need to show the will or succession certificate?

No. Gold buyers do not ask for the will or succession documents. Only standard KYC (Aadhaar + PAN if >₹2L) is needed.

Is there tax on selling inherited gold?

Yes — Capital Gains Tax applies. If the combined holding period (original owner + heir) exceeds 24 months, LTCG at 12.5% applies on the gain. Consult a tax advisor.

What is the cost of acquisition for inherited gold for tax purposes?

For inherited gold, the cost basis is typically the fair market value on the date you inherited it, not the original purchase price. A valuation certificate from the inheritance date helps.

Can I sell gold I inherited 10 years ago?

Yes. There is no time limit on selling inherited gold.

What if multiple family members inherited the same gold?

Each heir sells their proportionate share with their own Aadhaar + PAN. If the gold is physically combined, it should be divided or one person designated to sell with others’ consent documented.

html:
How to Check Gold Purity at Home: 5 Methods Explained

Before selling gold, many people want to estimate their gold‘s purity at home before visiting a buyer. Several methods exist – from simple magnet tests to density calculations. Each has different accuracy levels and limitations.

This guide covers all 5 home testing methods, what they can and cannot tell you, and why the XRF machine test at a reputable gold buyer remains the only definitive answer.

At a Glance

Most accurate home method

BIS hallmark check (999/916/750)

Most common mistake

Trusting acid test colour alone

Magnet test tells you

Whether it is NOT gold (not the karat)

Definitive professional test

XRF machine (±0.1% accurate)

Last Updated

May 2026

Method 1: Check the BIS Hallmark (Most Reliable Home Method)

Look for the BIS hallmark stamped on your jewellery. Since 2021, all gold sold in India must carry a 6-digit HUID (Hallmark Unique ID). The hallmark includes the purity code: 999 = 24K, 916 = 22K, 750 = 18K, 585 = 14K.You can verify the HUID on the BIS Care mobile app (available on Android and iOS). This is the most reliable home check – though it applies only to hallmarked jewellery bought after 2021.

Method 2: Magnet Test

Hold a strong magnet near your gold. Pure gold is not magnetic – it will not be attracted to the magnet. If your jewellery is attracted to the magnet, it likely contains iron or steel and is not solid gold.Important limitation: this test only tells you if something is definitely NOT gold. It cannot distinguish between 24K, 22K and 18K. Brass, copper and silver are also non-magnetic but are not gold.

Method 3: Float/Density Test

Gold is very dense (19.3 g/cm³). Drop your piece into a glass of water. Real gold should sink immediately. Fake gold (plated brass or hollow pieces) may float or sink slowly.Limitation: most gold jewellery has some hollow sections or alloys that can affect the result. This test is a rough indicator, not a reliable purity test.

Method 4: Acid Test (Home Kit)

Gold acid test kits are available online (typically ₹200–500). You make a small scratch on a touchstone, rub the gold on it, and apply acid. The colour reaction indicates approximate karat range.Accuracy: ±2–3K (approximate range, not exact). The acid test also scratches the touchstone and can slightly damage the piece surface. Home kits are less accurate than professional acid testing at a lab.

Method 5: Electronic Gold Tester

Handheld electronic gold testers (available online, ₹1,500–5,000) apply a small electrical signal to the piece and estimate purity based on conductivity. They are quick (10–20 seconds) but accuracy is limited – typically ±3–5K.They can also give false readings on plated gold, heavily alloyed pieces and soldered sections.

Why Home Tests Are Not Enough for Resale

Frequently Asked Questions

How can I check if my gold is 22K or 18K at home?

Does a magnet test tell me the karat of my gold?

No. The magnet test only tells you if something is NOT gold (if it attracts a magnet). It cannot distinguish between 24K, 22K and 18K.

Can I use the BIS Care app to check my gold?

Yes. If your gold has a 6-digit HUID hallmark, you can verify purity on the BIS Care app. This applies to hallmarked jewellery bought in India after 2021.

Is the acid test accurate?

The acid test gives an approximate range (±2–3K), not an exact reading. It is better than nothing but not reliable enough for resale pricing.

How accurate is a home electronic gold tester?

Typically ±3–5K accurate. Better than a magnet test but less reliable than XRF. Not recommended for resale price estimation.

Why does gold rate change every day?

The IBJA sets the rate twice daily based on the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) spot price, converted to INR. MCX intraday futures trading adds further movement within each day. Dollar-rupee exchange rate fluctuations, RBI gold purchase activity and global geopolitical events all influence the daily rate.

Should I sell gold when the rate is high this week?

If you need cash and today’s rate meets your target value, selling now is rational. Trying to time the exact peak carries the risk of a pullback. Historical patterns show that gold rates do correct after strong rallies – but timing those corrections is speculative. If the rate today covers your need, selling eliminates the risk of waiting.

html:
Gold Acid Test vs XRF: How Purity Is Tested When You Sell Gold

Before paying you for your gold, a buyer must confirm the exact purity of your piece. There are two main methods: the acid test (traditional) and XRF machine testing (modern standard). Understanding both helps you know what to expect and ensures you are not underpaid.

At a Glance

Acid test accuracy

~±2–3K (approximate)

XRF test accuracy

±0.1% (very precise)

Time for XRF test

30–60 seconds per piece

Damages your jewellery?

Acid: minor scratch / XRF: none

Last Updated

May 2026

What Is the Gold Acid Test?

The acid test uses nitric acid to check gold purity. A small scratch is made on a touchstone, the metal is rubbed on it, and acid is applied. The colour reaction indicates the approximate karat: 24K resists, lower karats show reactions. The acid test is a rough guide – it can indicate purity within a range (e.g., 18K–22K) but cannot pinpoint exactly 91.6% vs 88% purity. It can also slightly damage the surface of your jewellery.

What Is XRF Testing?

Acid Test vs XRF – Comparison

Factor

Acid Test

XRF Test

Accuracy

±2–3K approximate

±0.1% precise

Damage to jewellery

Minor surface scratch

None (non-destructive)

Time

2–5 minutes

30–60 seconds

Result format

Visual colour range

Exact % composition

Can detect plating?

Limited

Yes – detects plated surfaces

Industry standard (2026)

Declining

Yes – universally adopted

What to Do If a Buyer Only Uses Acid Testing

·       Ask why XRF is not being used – reputable buyers use XRF

·       Acid tests can understate purity – you may receive less than you deserve

·       Request a second opinion at an XRF-equipped buyer before accepting

Can You Test Gold at Home?

Home testing kits (magnet test, acid kits, electronic testers) exist but are not reliable for determining exact purity for resale. A magnet test only confirms whether something is not gold (magnets attract iron/steel, not gold). Home electronic testers have poor accuracy. For resale purposes, only an XRF test at a reputable buyer gives the definitive purity reading.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the acid test still used to buy gold?

Can acid testing damage my jewellery?

Yes – a small scratch is made on a touchstone. The scratch is minor but present. XRF requires no scratching.

How accurate is the XRF test?

XRF is accurate to ±0.1% purity – it gives the exact elemental composition of your gold piece.

Can XRF detect gold plating?

Yes. XRF can detect a thin gold layer over a base metal – it will show a thin gold reading over copper or silver. This distinguishes solid gold from gold-plated items.

What if I test my gold at home with a kit?

Home kits (acid kits, electronic testers) are not reliable for exact purity. For resale, always use XRF at a professional buyer.

How long does XRF testing take?

30–60 seconds per piece. For multiple pieces, testing is done one at a time and typically takes 5–15 minutes total.

Gold Price Calculator: Check Your Gold’s Resale Value Before Selling

Before selling your gold, you want to know exactly how much you should receive. A gold price calculator tells you your jewellery’s resale value based on today’s IBJA rate, the weight of your piece and the purity (karat).

At a Glance

Formula

Weight (g) × Purity Fraction × Today’s 24K Rate

Last Updated

How the Gold Resale Calculator Works

The gold resale value formula is: Cash Value = Weight (grams) × Purity Fraction × Today’s 24K IBJA Rate. The purity fraction converts your karat into a decimal: 24K = 1.000, 22K = 0.916, 18K = 0.750, 14K = 0.585.

Example: You have a 15g 22K necklace. Today’s 24K IBJA rate is ₹15,250/g. Resale value = 15 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹2,09,535. That is the cash you should receive before any deductions.

Live Calculator

The widget above calculates using the live IBJA rate updated every trading day. Always verify at the branch — the final price depends on XRF purity testing.

What Affects Your Final Payout

·       Purity — XRF machine testing at branch confirms actual karat

·       Weight — measured on calibrated scales, accurate to 0.01g

·       Non-gold elements — stones, lac filling, soldering removed before weighing

·       Making charges — NOT deducted at resale. You get full metal value.

KYC Required

Aadhaar is mandatory for all sales. PAN is required if your total sale exceeds ₹2,00,000 in a financial year. This is a regulatory requirement under Section 114B of the Income Tax Act.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I calculate my gold resale value?

Formula: Weight (g) × Purity Fraction × Today’s 24K Rate. For 10g of 22K: 10 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹1,39,690.

What is the purity fraction for 22K gold?

22K gold has a purity of 91.6%, so the purity fraction is 0.916.

Does the calculator include making charges?

No. Making charges are NOT deducted at resale. You receive the full metal value at the IBJA rate.

What is the IBJA rate?

IBJA (Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association) publishes the daily benchmark gold price in India. All reputable gold buyers use this rate.

Is the calculator value the exact amount I receive?

What if my gold has stones or lac filling?

Stones and lac are removed before weighing. You receive the per-gram rate for the net gold weight only.

How often is the gold rate updated?

IBJA publishes rates every trading day (Monday–Friday). The widget on this page updates accordingly.

Gold buyers melt or recycle gold; the market price is for raw gold content. Designer premium is paid only by buyers wanting the specific design, not by commodity gold buyers.

At a gold buyer, no. The brand does not add resale value. Hallmarking matters (it confirms purity), but the brand name itself does not add to the per-gram rate.

Many branded jewellers offer exchange schemes where you can use the value toward a new purchase. The cash value is typically the same as a gold buyer offers. Exchange is convenient but not financially superior.

Gold Purity Chart: 24K 22K 18K 14K – Complete Guide for Sellers

Gold purity determines exactly how much of your jewellery is actual gold – and therefore how much cash you receive when you sell. Understanding the gold purity chart is the single most important step before selling any gold ornament.

This guide explains every purity level, the BIS hallmark codes on your jewellery and how purity directly impacts your resale value.

At a Glance

How to Find Your Gold’s Purity

·       BIS hallmark on your jewellery – look for the 6-digit HUID and the purity code (916, 750, etc.)

·       XRF (X-ray fluorescence) test – the most accurate method; takes 30 seconds at the branch

·       Acid test – older method; less common now that XRF is standard

·       Stamping alone – not always reliable; XRF gives the final definitive reading

How Purity Affects Your Resale Value

A 10g necklace at 22K yields ₹1,39,690 today. The same 10g piece at 18K yields ₹1,14,375 – a difference of ₹25,315. Knowing your purity before selling prevents being underpaid. Formula: Cash Value = Weight (g) × (Purity / 24) × Today’s 24K Rate.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the purity of 22K gold?

22K gold is 91.6% pure gold – it has 22 parts gold and 2 parts alloying metals (usually copper and silver for strength). The BIS hallmark code is 916.

How do I check gold purity at home?

The most reliable way is to visit a gold buyer or jeweller for XRF testing. At home, look for BIS hallmarks stamped on the jewellery (916 = 22K, 750 = 18K, 999 = 24K).

Is 22K or 24K gold better for resale?

24K gold gives a higher per-gram payout (since it is 100% gold), but most Indian jewellery is 22K. At resale, each is paid at the correct rate for its actual purity as tested by XRF.

What does the BIS hallmark mean?

BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) hallmark certifies gold purity. The 6-digit HUID (Hallmark Unique ID) on BIS-hallmarked jewellery allows you to verify purity via the BIS Care app.

Can the acid test prove my gold is 22K?

Why does my antique jewellery test at 20K?

Older jewellery was often made to traditional standards (20K or 21K) before BIS hallmarking became standard. This is common and expected.

Does a higher karat mean more durable jewellery?

No – higher karat (more pure gold) is actually softer. 24K pure gold is the softest; 18K and 14K are more durable because of alloying metals. For resale, higher purity gives a higher per-gram rate.

html:
Think Hallmarking Is All That Matters? Here’s What Really Determines Your Gold’s Value

What Determines Your Gold Value? Factors That Affect Gold Price

Think Hallmarking Is All That Matters? Understanding the Real Value of Your Gold Before You Sell

If you’re planning to sell old gold in Bangalore or anywhere across South India, you’ve probably heard someone confidently say,

“My jewellery is hallmarked, so I’ll definitely get the best value.”

While hallmarking is an important indicator of purity and authenticity, it is only one part of the valuation process. The actual resale value of your gold depends on several factors that work together to determine its worth on the day you sell it.

Many people assume that a hallmark alone guarantees the highest payout. Others believe that the amount they originally paid for their jewellery determines its resale value. In reality, professional gold buyers evaluate jewellery using scientific testing, live market prices, net gold weight, and transparent calculations before making an offer.

Whether you’re comparing gold buyers in Bangalore, searching for a trusted gold buying company, or simply trying to understand how your jewellery is valued, knowing these factors can help you make a better financial decision and avoid unnecessary losses.

This guide explains exactly what determines your gold’s value, how professional valuation works, and why transparency plays the most important role when selling your gold.

Today’s Live Gold Price Matters More Than Ever

Gold prices change throughout the day based on global demand, international bullion markets, currency movements, and the benchmark rates published by the Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA).

Every reputed gold buying company uses the current market price while calculating the final value of your jewellery.

  • 24K Gold Rate
  • 22K Gold Rate
  • 18K Gold Rate
  • Last Updated Time
  • Disclaimer:
    “Rates are indicative. Final valuation depends on purity testing conducted at the branch.”

How Professional Gold Buyers Calculate Your Gold Value

Your jewellery is never valued simply by looking at it.

Professional buyers follow a transparent valuation formula.

Gold Value Formula

Final Gold Value = Net Gold Weight × Tested Purity × Live Gold Rate − Applicable Adjustments

For example,

If your jewellery weighs 20 grams and the XRF machine confirms 91.6% purity (22K) while today’s live gold rate is ₹9,000 per gram:

20 × 0.916 × ₹9,000 = ₹1,64,880

Minor deductions may apply only for:

  • Stones
  • Enamel
  • Wax
  • Solder

No deductions should be made for making charges that were paid when purchasing the jewellery.

Hallmark Is the Beginning, Not the Final Answer

A hallmark certifies the purity of gold at the time it was tested and manufactured. It confirms that the jewellery met BIS standards when it received its hallmark.

However, the actual purity of jewellery can vary slightly over time because of repairs, soldering, resizing, or alterations.

This is why every reputed gold buying company performs a fresh purity test using advanced XRF technology before calculating the value.

Scientific purity testing provides a real-time assessment of your jewellery’s gold content without melting or damaging it.

Rather than relying only on the hallmark, professional buyers rely on the actual purity measured during evaluation.

Why XRF Purity Testing Is the Industry Standard

Modern gold valuation is based on X-Ray Fluorescence (XRF) technology.

Unlike traditional touchstone testing, XRF testing:

  • Is completely non-destructive
  • Takes only a few minutes
  • Provides highly accurate purity readings
  • Requires no melting
  • Gives instant digital reports

Because of its accuracy and transparency, XRF testing has become the preferred method used by leading gold buyers across India.

Net Gold Weight Determines Your Gold Value

One of the biggest surprises for customers is that jewellery is not valued using its total weight.

Decorative materials such as:

  • Diamonds
  • Gemstones
  • Pearls
  • Beads
  • Enamel work
  • Wax fillings

do not contribute to the value of gold itself.

During valuation, these materials are excluded, and only the actual weight of pure gold is considered.

This explains why two necklaces with identical overall weights may receive completely different valuations.

The net weight of pure gold is always the foundation of a fair valuation.

Why Purchase Price Doesn’t Decide Today’s Gold Value

Many customers expect to receive the same amount they originally paid for their jewellery.

However, jewellery purchase prices include several additional costs, including:

  • Making charges
  • GST
  • Design costs
  • Craftsmanship
  • Wastage
  • Retail margins

These costs increase the purchase price but do not become part of the intrinsic value of the gold itself.

Professional gold buyers calculate the value using today’s live market price rather than the historical purchase price.

When selling a solitaire ring to a gold buyer, it is important to understand that the gold band and the solitaire stone are valued separately – the gold is paid by weight and purity, while the diamond requires separate certification-based valuation.

At a gold buyer, only the gold band’s weight and purity are paid for the gold portion.

●      Setting/prongs are part of the gold band weight

Resale Value & Worked Example

The gold band is weighed after the stone is removed. For a 4g 22K band: 4 × 0.916 × ₹15,250 = ₹55,876.

The solitaire diamond is valued separately based on its 4Cs and certification – a gold buyer pays only for the gold. If you wish to sell the diamond too, bring its GIA/IGI certificate for separate assessment.

Tax Treatment When You Sell

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Aadhaar is mandatory; PAN is required if your sale exceeds ₹2,00,000.

What to Watch For

●      Stones or lac weighed with gold – insist on removal before weighing

●      Visual purity check instead of XRF – always request machine testing

●      No written receipt – a signed receipt is a legal requirement

●      Making charge deductions at resale – these do not apply

How much is a gold solitaire ring worth at a gold buyer?

The gold band is paid by weight: a 4g 22K band is worth ₹55,876. The diamond is valued separately with certification.

Is the diamond included in the gold buyer’s price?

No. A gold buyer pays for the gold band by weight and purity. The diamond requires separate certificate-based valuation.

How is the diamond removed?

At the branch, the diamond is carefully removed from the setting and returned to you, or assessed separately if you wish to sell it.

Does the ring setting count as gold?

Yes. The band and prongs are weighed as gold after the stone is removed.

What documents?

Aadhaar mandatory for the gold sale. For the diamond, a GIA/IGI certificate helps with valuation.

What purity are solitaire bands?

Commonly 18K or 22K. XRF at the branch confirms.

Is a solitaire ring the same as a diamond ring?

A solitaire has a single stone. A diamond ring may have multiple stones. Both have the gold portion valued the same way.

With numerous gold buying companies operating across Bangalore, customers often find it difficult to determine which buyer offers the best value and most transparent process. Before selling your gold, it is important to evaluate several factors that directly impact the amount you receive.

Transparency in Gold Evaluation

The best gold buyers in Bangalore always perform purity and weight testing in front of customers. Transparency builds trust and ensures customers understand exactly how their gold value is calculated.

Accuracy of Purity Testing

Gold purity plays a major role in determining value. Even a small difference in purity percentage can significantly affect the final payout.

Instant Payment Assurance

Many customers sell gold during emergencies and require immediate funds. The best gold buyers in Bangalore provide instant payment after valuation approval.

Why Bangalore Has Become One of India’s Largest Gold Markets

Bangalore is one of India’s fastest-growing metropolitan cities and has a strong culture of gold ownership. Families often invest in gold jewellery for weddings, festivals, savings, and future security.

As lifestyles evolve and financial needs change, many individuals choose to unlock the value of their idle gold assets. This growing demand has increased the need for trustworthy gold buyers who offer fair valuations and transparent services.

Emergency Financial Needs

Many customers choose to sell old or outdated jewellery and purchase new designs that better match their preferences.

Unlocking Idle Assets

Unused jewellery stored in lockers often remains dormant for years. Selling such assets allows customers to convert them into productive funds.

Debt Clearance

Individuals frequently use the value of their gold to clear outstanding debts or manage financial obligations more effectively.

Investment Diversification

The Dhanteras-Diwali window typically accounts for 15%–20% of India’s annual gold jewellery sales. Gold Rate During Diwali Season – What to Expect

The gold rate during Diwali is determined by international gold price and USD-INR exchange rate – the same factors that drive the rate every other day. Diwali creates high retail buying demand, but this demand is met through jewellery manufacture and imports – it does not directly push the IBJA rate.

For sellers: Diwali is simply another day at the current IBJA rate. The best time to sell is when the IBJA rate meets your financial goal – festival or not.

Gold rate aftre budget – India’s Union Budget typically presented in February – is one of the most-watched events in the Indian gold market. The government’s decision on customs duty for gold imports directly affects domestic gold prices. This guide explains how the 2026 budget has affected gold rates and what it means for sellers.

How the Union Budget Affects Gold Prices

Gold import duty is the primary lever the government uses to regulate domestic gold prices. When import duty rises, domestic gold becomes more expensive (supporting higher IBJA rates). When duty falls, domestic prices may soften relative to international levels.

The IBJA adjusts its benchmark rate immediately after any budget announcement that affects import duty. The live rate in the widget above is the post-budget IBJA rate.

Current Gold Rate After Budget 2026

Today’s live 22K rate is ₹13,965/g. 24K rate: ₹15,250/g. This rate already incorporates any changes announced in Budget 2026.

Should You Sell Before or After Budget?

●      If duty is expected to rise (e.g. government signals higher protection for domestic gold) – selling after the budget may yield a slightly higher rate

●      If duty is expected to fall – selling before the budget announcement may be better

●      In practice, budget expectations are priced into the market before the announcement

●      The safest strategy: sell when today’s live rate meets your financial goal – regardless of budget timing

If you expect a duty increase (which typically pushes prices up), selling after may benefit you. If duty falls, selling before may be better. In practice, budget effects are priced in quickly – the best strategy is to sell when today’s live rate meets your financial goal.

title: How to Weigh Gold at Home Before Selling – Accurate Methods
metaTitle: How to Weigh Gold at Home Before Selling – Accurate Methods | Aryan Gold Buyers
description: Knowing the approximate weight of your gold before visiting a buyer puts you in control of the transaction. If a buyer’s scale shows 12g but your home scale showed 15g, that…
html:
Knowing the approximate weight of your gold before visiting a buyer puts you in control of the transaction. If a buyer’s scale shows 12g but your home scale showed 15g, that discrepancy – worth ₹41,907 at today’s rate – is worth questioning before you agree to any price.

What You Need

A digital kitchen scale or postal scale accurate to 0.1 grams is sufficient. Many pharmacy scales and kitchen scales marketed as accurate to ±1g work well for individual pieces. Jewellery scales accurate to 0.01g are available online for ₹300–₹800.

How to Weigh Your Gold at Home

Step 1: Turn on the digital scale and press tare/zero. Step 2: Place the gold piece alone on the scale – no wrapping, no box. Step 3: Note the reading in grams. Repeat for each piece separately. Step 4: Add the individual weights for the total.

What to Include and Exclude

●      Include: all gold metal components – chain, ring body, bangles, pendant frame

●      Exclude: plastic bags, paper, boxes – these add weight the buyer won’t pay for

What scale should I use to weigh gold at home?

A digital kitchen scale or jewellery scale accurate to 0.1g is sufficient for gold weighing. Postal scales and kitchen scales accurate to 1g give a reasonable estimate but may be off by ±1g on small pieces.

Knowing your gold’s approximate weight before visiting a buyer means you can verify their quoted weight and identify any major discrepancy before agreeing to a price.

Weigh each piece separately to identify individual weights. This helps you spot if a piece is missing from the buyer’s total.

title: HUID Number on Gold: How to Check & Verify on BIS Care App Before You Sell
metaTitle: HUID Number on Gold: How to Check & Verify on BIS Care App Before You Sell | Aryan Gold Buyers
description: From June 2021, every gold jewellery piece sold in India is required to carry a six-digit alphanumeric HUID – Hallmark Unique Identification number – that links it permanently to the…
html:
From June 2021, every gold jewellery piece sold in India is required to carry a six-digit alphanumeric HUID – Hallmark Unique Identification number – that links it permanently to the BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) database. Before you sell your gold, knowing how to check and verify this number gives you two advantages: it confirms the BIS-certified purity of your piece, and it protects you from buyers who undervalue properly hallmarked gold.

This guide explains what the HUID number is, how to check it on the BIS Care app in under 60 seconds, and what to do if your gold was purchased before 2021 and has no HUID.

At a Glance

Introduced

June 2021 (BIS mandatory hallmarking)

Format

6-digit alphanumeric (e.g., AB1234)

Location on piece

Stamped alongside BIS logo, purity mark & jeweller code

Verification

BIS Care app (Android & iOS) – free

Pre-2021 gold

No HUID – still sellable, XRF confirms purity

Benefit for seller

Confirms purity before accepting any buyer’s quote

Last Updated

May 2026

What Is the HUID Hallmark? – The Four-Part BIS Mark Explained

Every hallmarked gold piece sold in India carries four elements: the BIS hallmark logo (triangle), the purity grade (916/750/585/999), the HUID (6-digit alphanumeric) and the assaying centre code. The HUID is the newest addition – mandatory since June 2021 – and it is the most consumer-friendly because it is verifiable instantly on your smartphone.

BIS Hallmark Elements

Element

What It Means

Where on the Piece

BIS Hallmark Logo

Certified by Bureau of Indian Standards

Triangle with BIS text

Purity Grade

916 = 22K, 750 = 18K, 585 = 14K, 999 = 24K

Adjacent to BIS logo

HUID (6-digit)

Unique ID traceable on BIS Care app

Engraved alongside purity mark

●      Step 1: Download ‘BIS Care’ from Google Play or the Apple App Store (free).

●      Step 2: Open the app and tap ‘Verify HUID’ on the home screen.

●      Step 3: Enter the 6-digit alphanumeric HUID from your piece – or scan it using the app’s camera.

●      Step 4: The app instantly shows the registered purity (e.g., 916 = 22K), karat, jeweller name, assaying centre and date of hallmarking.

●      Step 5: Compare the app result with what the buyer is telling you. If there is any discrepancy, ask for XRF testing before accepting the quote.

●      Identifying pieces that may have been incorrectly hallmarked

What is a HUID number on gold?

HUID stands for Hallmark Unique Identification. It is a 6-digit alphanumeric code stamped on hallmarked gold jewellery by a BIS-accredited assaying centre. Every HUID is unique to that piece and is linked to the purity, karat, jeweller and assaying centre in the BIS national database.

How do I check HUID on the BIS Care app?

Download the BIS Care app (Android or iOS). Open the app and tap ‘Verify HUID’. Enter the 6-digit code from your piece. The app shows the purity, karat, jeweller name and assaying centre in seconds. The app is free and does not require registration.

What if my gold does not have a HUID?

Does HUID affect the price I get for my gold?

Can a HUID be faked or duplicated?

The BIS database is centralised and government-controlled. A fake HUID either won’t appear in the BIS Care app or will show a mismatch between the claimed purity and the database entry. Always verify using the official BIS Care app before accepting any seller’s verbal purity claim.

What is the BIS Care app?

BIS Care is the official app of the Bureau of Indian Standards, available free on Android and iOS. It allows consumers to verify gold hallmark HUID numbers, check product certifications and file complaints about substandard goods.

The gold nose pin – variously called nath, nosepin, nath ring or nathni – is among the most gifted and most accumulated small gold items in Indian households. South Indian brides receive naths at multiple ceremonies; North Indian families pass down elaborate kundan nath pieces across generations. When considering resale, what matters is the gold weight and purity – not the design, tradition or sentimental value.

This guide covers typical gold weight ranges by nose pin design, today’s live IBJA rate per gram and the exact formula to calculate your resale cash value before walking into any gold buyer’s branch.

●      Maharashtrian nath – round ring with central stone, typically 2g–4g gold

●      Length-based pricing instead of weight-based pricing – resale is always by gram, never by length or design

●      Visual purity check instead of XRF on old chains – pre-2000 chains are sometimes below 916

●      Making charge deductions at resale – making charges apply only to new purchases, never to resale

●      Buyers who round down weight – always watch the scale and get a printed receipt

Box and rope chains for daily wear commonly range 8g–14g. Heavy Cuban link and Franco chains worn as statement pieces range 15g–30g. Temple chains and traditional designs often fall between 12g and 20g. Weight varies with length and link thickness.

Does chain design affect resale value?

No. Resale value is calculated purely on gold weight and purity – not the chain design, pattern, or jeweller brand. A box chain and a Cuban link of identical weight and karat will fetch exactly the same cash at resale.

If you want to sell only the chain, the pendant (especially if stone-set) is removed and returned to you. You receive payment only on the chain weight. Alternatively, if the pendant is plain gold, you can sell both together.

Aadhaar is mandatory for all gold sales. PAN is required if your total sale amount exceeds ₹2,00,000. For a single chain in the typical 10g–20g range, current values are below this threshold – but always bring both documents.

Digital Gold – What It Is and How Selling Differs from Physical Gold

This guide covers both routes: (1) selling digital gold directly within the app at the platform’s buy-back rate, and (2) redeeming digital gold to physical bullion and selling at IBJA rates at an organised buyer. Today’s reference rate: 24K = ₹15,250/g. Digital gold platforms typically buy back at 95–98% of this benchmark.

Today’s Live Rate Reference for Digital Gold

Method 1: In-App Sale at Paytm Gold

Paytm Gold is backed by MMTC-PAMP, India’s largest gold refiner. Selling within the app is simple:

●Open Paytm app → ‘Gold’ section → ‘Sell Gold’.

● Enter quantity to sell (in grams or rupee value); current sell rate displayed.

● Confirm sale; money credited to Paytm wallet or directly to linked UPI bank account.

● Settlement: Wallet credit instant; bank transfer typically within minutes via UPI.

Paytm’s buyback rate is updated continuously and displayed before sale confirmation. There are no transaction charges; the spread between buy and sell rate (typically 3–4% bid-ask) is how the platform monetises. KYC is automatic via the linked Paytm account.

Method 2: PhonePe and Google Pay (Same Process)

PhonePe Gold and Google Pay Gold operate similarly to Paytm – backed by MMTC-PAMP, with in-app sell rates 1.5–3% below IBJA. The interface is similar: select gold balance → choose ‘Sell’ → confirm → receive money in wallet/UPI. All three Paytm/PhonePe/GPay routes net you 96–98% of IBJA.

Method 3: MMTC-PAMP Direct (Best Digital Rate)

If you bought digital gold directly through MMTC-PAMP’s website or app (rather than via Paytm/PhonePe wrapper), you can sell back at MMTC-PAMP’s direct buyback rate – typically 1–2% below IBJA, which is the best digital-gold buyback rate available. The process: log in to MMTC-PAMP account → ‘My Gold’ → ‘Sell’ → confirm. Money credited to your linked bank account within 1–2 working days.

Method 4: Redeem to Physical Bullion + Sell at Organised Buyer

Tax Treatment of Digital Gold Sales

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Digital gold sales are reported by the platform to the tax department; the platform issues a tax statement at year-end showing your buy/sell transactions for ITR filing. Holding period clock starts from purchase date in-app; for purposes of LTCG vs STCG, the in-app holding date is what counts (not redemption date). For very high-net-worth individuals using digital gold for systematic accumulation, this tax record-keeping is one of digital gold’s advantages over physical gold.

What to Watch For When Selling Digital Gold

●Compare in-app rate vs IBJA – if your platform’s buyback is more than 3% below IBJA, consider redeeming to physical and selling at an organised buyer instead.

● Beware of ‘discontinued platforms’ – some smaller digital gold issuers have shut down or paused buyback; choose only major names (Paytm/PhonePe/Google Pay/MMTC-PAMP/Tanishq) with proven reliability.

●Redemption charges add up – for small balances (below 1g), redemption to physical may not be cost-effective; in-app sale is usually better.

● Tax records – keep digital screenshots of your transactions for tax filing; platforms also send year-end statements.

●Don’t confuse Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGB) with digital gold – SGBs are different (RBI-issued, 2.5% annual interest, 8-year maturity); selling SGBs early on the secondary market involves bond market mechanics, not platform buyback.

How do I sell digital gold from Paytm?

Open Paytm → ‘Gold’ → ‘Sell Gold’ → enter amount → confirm. Money is credited to your Paytm wallet or linked bank account instantly. Paytm’s buyback rate is typically 1.5–3% below the IBJA reference rate.

Can I redeem digital gold for physical coins or bars?

Yes – most platforms (Paytm, PhonePe, MMTC-PAMP) allow redemption of digital balances above 1g to physical bullion. Redemption charges (typically ₹100–250) plus making charges (5–10% for coins) apply. Delivery in 5–10 days via insured courier.

What’s the best way to sell digital gold for maximum cash?

Is digital gold better than physical gold?

Different use cases. Digital gold offers convenience (small denominations from ₹100, no storage worry) but pays slightly less on resale (1–3% below IBJA vs 1% below IBJA for physical at organised buyers). Physical gold offers better resale rates and emotional/cultural value, but requires safekeeping. Most diversified holdings have both

Are there taxes on digital gold sales?

Gold held over 24 months attracts 12.5% LTCG when sold; held under 24 months, your gain is added to slab income. Digital gold sales are reported by the platform; a year-end tax statement is provided for ITR filing. The holding period starts from the in-app purchase date.

Can I sell digital gold from a closed account?

No – SGBs are RBI-issued bonds backed by gold, with 2.5% annual interest and 8-year maturity. Digital gold platforms are private (e.g., MMTC-PAMP backing Paytm/PhonePe). SGBs cannot be ‘sold back’ to the issuer until maturity; they trade on secondary stock exchanges. Tax treatment also differs (SGBs have favourable LTCG treatment on maturity).

What deductions are legitimate when selling old gold?

Can a gold buyer charge making charges at resale?

html:
Where to Sell Gold – All Six Options Honestly Compared

If you have gold and want cash for it, you have six broad options in India: (1) the jeweller you bought from (exchange or buyback), (2) any other jeweller (third-party gold buying), (3) ISO-certified cash-for-gold companies, (4) pawnshops or local lenders, (5) banks (gold loans against pledge, not direct sale), and (6) online platforms (mail-in services). Each has its place, but they are not equal in terms of rate, transparency or convenience. This guide compares all six honestly so you can choose what’s right for your situation.

Today’s reference rates as a benchmark: 24K = ₹15,250/g, 22K = ₹13,965/g. The ‘best’ option depends on what you optimise for: highest rate, fastest cash, lowest hassle, or some combination. For most sellers wanting straightforward cash at fair rates, organised ISO-certified buyers are the strongest choice; for emotional pieces you may want back, banks (via gold loan) preserve the asset.

Six Options at a Glance

Today’s Live Rate as Your Reference Benchmark

Option 1: Original Jeweller (Buyback or Exchange)

Most jewellers offer ‘buyback’ on pieces sold by them – typically at 70–85% of today’s IBJA rate, often only as credit toward new purchases (not cash). Designer jewellery’s making charges are not refunded. This is convenient if you bought there originally and want a quick exchange, but the rate is usually significantly below market. Best for: customers upgrading to new pieces from the same jeweller, not for those wanting cash.

Option 2: Third-Party Jeweller

Other jewellers may buy your gold to refine into new inventory. Rates are typically 75–88% of IBJA, sometimes only as credit toward a new purchase. The variability is high – small jewellers often don’t have XRF testing and use touchstone/acid methods that under-rate purity. Best for: customers willing to shop around 2–3 jewellers and accept moderate rates for the convenience of in-shop transactions.

Option 3: ISO-Certified Cash-for-Gold Buyers

Option 4: Pawnshops and Local Buyers

Pawnshops and small local ‘gold buying’ shops often advertise ‘highest rates’ but typically offer 80–90% of IBJA after factoring in their hidden margins, weight tricks and stone-weight deductions. Most don’t have XRF; some don’t have properly calibrated scales. KYC is often informal or missing. Best for: very small sales (under ₹5,000) where the convenience may outweigh rate concerns; otherwise, avoid.

Option 5: Bank Gold Loans (Asset Preservation)

Banks like SBI, HDFC, Axis, and ICICI offer gold loans where you pledge your gold as collateral and receive a loan of 70–90% of its value. You pay 8–12% annual interest and reclaim your gold on repayment. This is not a sale – you keep ownership and the gold returns to you when the loan is repaid. Best for: customers who want cash but emotionally cannot part with gold permanently (e.g., wedding pieces, inherited heirlooms). Note: defaulting on the loan results in a gold auction.

Option 6: Online Mail-In Gold Buyers

Some online platforms accept gold via insured courier and pay digitally after verification. Rates are typically 85–93% of IBJA, with the lower end reflecting transit risk and remote verification limitations. The buyer cannot physically test purity in your view, so the system relies on photographic documentation and post-arrival XRF. Best for: sellers in remote areas without nearby trusted buyers, or those selling non-sentimental small pieces. Caveats: transit insurance gaps, dispute risk if the buyer disagrees with the declared purity.

What to Watch For Across All Options

● IBJA rate verification – every option should reference IBJA; if they refuse, move on.

●XRF testing availability – modern buyers test purity in seconds; lack of XRF means you’re being valued by guess.

● KYC compliance – Aadhaar mandatory; PAN if > ₹2,00,000. Buyers who skip KYC are not properly licensed.

●Itemised receipts – every deduction (margin, stone weight) should be a separate line.

●  Same-day payment – reputable buyers pay immediately; deferred payment is a red flag.

Where is the best place to sell gold for cash?

Can I sell gold to a bank?

Banks don’t directly buy gold for cash. Banks offer gold loans – you pledge your gold as collateral and receive 70–90% of its value as a loan, repaid with 8–12% interest. Gold is returned on repayment. This is asset preservation, not a sale.

Is selling to a jeweller a good option?

Generally not for maximum cash. Jewellers offer 70–85% of IBJA (often only as credit toward new purchases). If you bought from them and want to upgrade, an exchange may be convenient. For straightforward cash, ISO-certified buyers offer significantly better rates.

Are pawnshops safe for selling gold?

Variable. Some are properly licensed with reasonable practices; many operate without XRF, calibrated scales, or proper KYC. Rates are typically 5–10% below those of organised buyers due to hidden margins. For small sales, occasional convenience; for any meaningful amount, organised buyers are far better.

Should I sell gold online?

Online mail-in buyers offer 85–93% of IBJA, typically less than in-person organised buyers due to transit risk and remote verification. Suitable for remote-area sellers without nearby branches; otherwise, in-person at an established branch is significantly safer and pays better.
